comment:
Thank you for the report. The multiplication in this report cannot overflow. The proof follows.

**Proof**

1. The code in comment 0 is not in the tree. `dom/media/flac/` has no `SetIndex()` and no `aPreviousBlocksize`. The real code computes `mIndex` in [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#109). It multiplies only for a fixed blocksize stream. A variable blocksize stream uses the coded number directly.
2. The coded number has at most 31 bits. [FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#86) reads it with `BitReader::ReadUTF8()`. That function returns -1 for a first byte of `0xFE` or higher ([BitReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/BitReader.cpp#118)), and the caller then rejects the frame ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#87)). Thus the longest accepted number has 6 bytes, which is 31 bits.
3. The blocksize is at most 65536. The largest value is `ReadBits(16) + 1` ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#100)).
4. Thus the product is at most (2^31 - 1) * 65536 = `0x7FFFFFFF0000`. This value has 47 bits. It fits in `uint64_t` and in `int64_t`, so no overflow and no undefined conversion occur. The same limits apply to the product in `ResetStartTimeIfNeeded()` ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#326)).
5. The proof does not depend on `AssertedCast`. That cast checks only in debug builds. The value fits in all builds.
6. The numbers in the report also do not overflow. `0xFFFFFFFFF * 65535` is `0xFFFEFFFFF0001`, a 52-bit value, not `0xFFFEF0001FFFC0001`.
7. The impact in the report cannot follow. `mIndex` is a sample index. It sets only the frame time, in `Frame::Time()` ([FlacDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/flac/FlacDemuxer.cpp#337)). It is not a byte offset. The demuxer finds each frame in the file by a byte scan for the frame sync code. `TimeUnit` stores its ticks in a `CheckedInt64` ([TimeUnits.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/TimeUnits.h#266)), so the time conversion is also checked.

**Next steps**

The resolution is INVALID. If a FLAC file causes a crash, a sanitizer error or a wrong seek position in Firefox, please file a new bug and attach the file.
title: FLAC Demuxer SetIndex — Unchecked uint64 × uint32 Multiplication Overflow

comment:
Thank you for the detailed report. A review of the source confirms the cause.

**Analysis**

- **Root cause.** `ProcessMediaFragmentURI()` sets `mFragmentEnd` from the `#t=` fragment ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#6380)). `load()` calls `AbortExistingLoads()`, and `ShutdownDecoder()` sets `mDecoder` to null ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2605)). `AbortExistingLoads()` does not reset `mFragmentStart` or `mFragmentEnd` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2615)).
- **The crash.** With no decoder, `CurrentTime()` returns the stored start position, so the fragment check in `FireTimeUpdate()` is true. The branch then calls `mDecoder->SetFragmentEndTime()` with no null check ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#7917)).
- **Two paths.** A script `pause()` reaches `PauseInternal()` and then `FireTimeUpdate()` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e77c5131fd07ddab0731efab207539f5ae3a00ce/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#3888)). The stable-state task from `UnbindFromTree()` also calls `PauseInternal()`.
- **Crash Stats.** The signature `mozilla::dom::HTMLMediaElement::FireTimeUpdate` has 45 content-process crashes since April 2026, on Windows, Android, macOS and Linux. The two reports you name are bp-2a02d882-3e32-4598-a46d-175120260928 (Windows, from `pause()`) and bp-7c97682b-bfcf-43f3-974b-e781e0260930 (Android, from `UnbindFromTree()`). Both read address 0x0.
- **Related bug.** Bug 2083234 tracks the wider problem: the media element keeps stale state after a new source is loaded. This bug stays open because it tracks this crash signature.
- **Not a regression.** The call comes from the media fragment work in bug 648595, and the code is old.

This is a content-process crash: one tab crashes, and a reload recovers it. The volume is low, so the severity is S3.

**Next steps**

The fix is small and stays in `HTMLMediaElement.cpp`:

1. Reset `mFragmentStart` and `mFragmentEnd` in `AbortExistingLoads()`, before its own `FireTimeUpdate()` call.
2. Reset both fields at the start of `ProcessMediaFragmentURI()` in all cases. Now an old end time can go to the next decoder when the new source has no `#t=`.
3. Add an `mDecoder` null check before `SetFragmentEndTime()` in `FireTimeUpdate()`. Other `ShutdownDecoder()` callers also leave the fragment fields set.

The page in comment 0 can become a crashtest. A second version with `v.remove()` can cover the `UnbindFromTree()` path. No meta bug matches this crash.
title: HTMLMediaElement::FireTimeUpdate derefs a null mDecoder in the media-fragment branch, reachable from pause() after load() clears the decoder

Media element keeps stale state after a text track is removed or a new source is loaded

comment:
Thank you for the report and the about:support data.

**Analysis**

The about:support shows the Intel Arc (BMG G31) as the active GPU, and `HARDWARE_VIDEO_DECODING_VULKAN` is available. No modified pref explains the failure.

The Vulkan decoder selects its GPU in `SelectVulkanDecoderPhysicalDevice` in [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#1067). The code uses the match with the renderer GPU only to sort the list. When no GPU matches, it takes the first discrete GPU. Comment 3 shows this result: the log says `matches renderer: false`, and the NVIDIA GPU wakes up on an Optimus laptop.

The NVIDIA check from bug 2067923 is `NvidiaDrmModesetDisabled` in [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#913). It reads `/sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset`. When `nvidia-drm` is not loaded, this file does not exist, so the NVIDIA GPU stays a candidate. A GPU with no DRM node cannot export the decoded frame, so playback stops with "Failed to export NV12 FD". The fix for bug 2067923 is not in 155.0.1, and it does not cover a module that is not loaded.

Suggested fix direction:
1. When the renderer GPU is known and no Vulkan GPU matches it, do not use Vulkan decoding. Fall back to VA-API or software decoding on the renderer GPU.
2. Skip a GPU that has no DRM node. Treat a missing `nvidia_drm` module as unusable.

The pref `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.enabled` set to `false` in `about:config` turns off Vulkan decoding.

This bug blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

**Next steps**

:stransky, could you please look at the device selection rule for multi-GPU systems?

Thank you for the analysis and the patches.

**Analysis**

The code agrees with your cause for both cases. The attached log agrees too.

- Case (a): [AudioContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/webaudio/AudioContext.cpp#190) computes `allowedToStart`, but [AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#464) always requests `AUDIO_THREAD_DRIVER`. `MediaTrackGraphImpl::Init()` then creates an `AudioCallbackDriver`, and [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#2077) starts it before `CheckDriver()` runs. In the log, the output unit opens on device 96 and stops about 150 ms later.
- Case (b): [RTCRtpReceiver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/webrtc/jsapi/RTCRtpReceiver.cpp#147) requests `AUDIO_THREAD_DRIVER`. `AudioTrackPresent()` in [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#391) is true for any audio track without an output, so `CheckDriver()` keeps the driver.

Both changes are necessary. The fix in `CheckDriver()` alone does not fix case (a), because `Init()` starts the driver first. The `AudioDestinationNode` fix alone does not fix case (b).

The logged lines do not show a WebRTC module or the name of device 96. Thus the log does not prove which case moved the AirPods. This does not block the review.

comment:
Thank you for the profile in comment 2.

**Analysis**

The profile shows the cause. VA-API decoding in the RDD process works without errors. The stall is in the `MediaDecoderStateMachine` buffering logic, not in the decoder.

1. When the clip plays again after it ends, the state machine treats the seek to 0 as a warm seek ("startSinkAfterWarmSeek=true"). The code sets this flag in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3254).
2. With hardware decoding, a warm seek prerolls only 1 video frame. The pref `media.seek-resume.video-preroll-frames-hw` is 1 in [StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#14132). Software decoding prerolls 3 frames, so it does not stall.
3. 1 frame is less than `LOW_VIDEO_FRAMES` (2), so `HasLowDecodedVideo()` is true immediately. The state machine enters buffering 2 ms after playback starts, through the check in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3204).
4. Buffering cannot end early for this file. The buffered range ends at 4.97 s (the end of the video track), but the duration is 5.0 s (the audio track). Thus `HasLowBufferedData()` stays true, and only the 15 s buffering timeout ends the wait ("Buffered for 15.271s").

This is a regression from bug 2050845, which added the warm seek preroll in Firefox 154. :alwu wrote that change.

**Fix direction**

- Keep the hardware warm preroll at or above `LOW_VIDEO_FRAMES`, or skip the low-data check until the queues refill after a warm resume.
- Do not treat a seek from the ended state as a warm seek.
- As a separate change, limit the `HasLowBufferedData()` end to the buffered end when the download is complete.

This bug blocks bug 1610199 (Linux VA-API playback) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback). Bug 2045880 shows a similar replay stall without hardware decoding, so it stays a related bug. :stransky, the cause is now known, so a VA-API test of the sample is no longer necessary.
title: Replaying an MP4 stalls for 10–15 seconds with hardware acceleration enabled

Thank you for the report and the patch.

**Analysis**

The current tree still has the problem. In [hwcontext_vulkan.c](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/media/ffvpx/libavutil/hwcontext_vulkan.c#2636), `switch_layout()` calls `ff_vk_exec_add_dep_frame()` with the wait stage `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_NONE`. [vulkan.c](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/media/ffvpx/libavutil/vulkan.c#922) uses this value as the semaphore wait `stageMask`. Thus the export layout barrier does not wait for `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR` on the video queue. The fix direction is the upstream FFmpeg change `dc54ec7a`: wait at `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT`. D334921 does this.

This path runs only when `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.direct-export.enabled` is `true`. Its default is `false`, and Vulkan video decoding is on by default only in Nightly. The code came into ffvpx with bug 2045971, from upstream FFmpeg.

**Next steps**

We suggest a note in `media/ffvpx/README_MOZILLA` about this cherry-pick, so that the next ffvpx update keeps it. The next step is the review of D334921. comment:
Thank you for the profile and the pref test.

**Analysis**

The profile shows the problem. Firefox creates the cubeb stream once and reuses it on each seek, as `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` allows. After a seek during playback, the audio clock includes the Bluetooth output latency of about 270 ms. After a seek while paused, the clock includes only about 30 ms. Thus the video runs about 250 ms ahead of the sound until the next seek.

The cause is in the reuse path for a paused stream:

1. A user pause stops the cubeb stream.
2. On the seek, [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#725) keeps the stopped stream for reuse. This check does not test if cubeb still runs.
3. [AudioSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSink.cpp#362) restarts the stream with `Resume()`.
4. Because cubeb restarted, [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#533) rebases the clock with `CarryUnplayed::No`.

The macOS cubeb backend does not reset its frame count on stop. Thus the clock counts the frames that the stop dropped as played media. The clock then runs ahead of the sound by the output latency.

**Fix direction**

Two possible changes:

- In `AudioStream::RebaseLive`, carry the unplayed frames also when `Resume()` restarted cubeb.
- In `AudioSinkWrapper::Stop`, reuse only a stream whose cubeb still runs. A seek while paused then gets a new stream, as with the pref off.

A gtest for pause, seek and resume can cover the fix.

**Related bugs**

Bug 2052692 added the stream reuse. Bug 2071968 turned it on for macOS in the Firefox 158 release, which matches the start of the problem. Bug 2081761 reports audio dropouts with the same pref. Alastor Wu wrote this code. This bug now blocks the seek performance meta bug 2049891.

Until a fix lands, the workaround from comment 0 stays valid: set `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` to `false`.
title: Audio Video Desync with Bluetooth headphones on MacOS in Firefox 158

comment:
Thank you for the detailed report and the patch.

**Analysis**

The cause in comment 0 is correct. The ffmpeg58 header set mixes the FFmpeg 4.4.1 `avcodec.h` from bug 1745284 with the FFmpeg 4.0 version files. [version.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/ffmpeg58/include/libavcodec/version.h#31) still says 58.18.100, and [version.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/ffmpeg58/include/libavutil/version.h#82) still says 56.14.100.

Thus `FF_API_OLD_ENCDEC`, `FF_API_THREAD_SAFE_CALLBACKS` and `FF_API_DEBUG_MV` remove three `AVCodecContext` fields that the real libavcodec 58 has. The first one, `refcounted_frames`, is in front of `qmin` in [avcodec.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/ffmpeg58/include/libavcodec/avcodec.h#1353). The values that [FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#504) writes to `qmin` and `qmax` go to the wrong fields. libx264 then opens with a minimum QP of 35.

The layout error starts with bug 1745284. It became visible when bug 1903582 made `FFmpegVideoEncoder` set `qmin` and `qmax`. Bug 1909369 later changed the values to the current prefs. Also, `FF_API_BUFFER_SIZE_T` is not defined, so `AVPacketSideData.size` has the wrong type. Firefox does not read that field today.

**Fix direction**

Replace both ffmpeg58 version files with the FFmpeg 4.4.1 copies, as D333609 does. All libavcodec 58 releases use the same layout, so this is also correct for FFmpeg 4.0 to 4.3. A `static_assert` on `offsetof(AVCodecContext, qmin)` for each header set can catch a partial update in the future. The reviewer should know that `FFmpegVideoDecoder` now also sets `thread_safe_callbacks = 1` with libavcodec 58.

This bug is now linked to the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.
title: WebCodecs H.264 encoder ignores bitrate with system FFmpeg 4.x: stale ffmpeg58 version.h shifts AVCodecContext, x264 opens with qmin=35

comment:
Thanks for the clear test page.

**Analysis**

The cause is a contract mismatch in `H264::WriteExtraData` in [H264.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H264.cpp#1493). The function writes its own NAL header byte before the SPS and the PPS, and it adds 1 to each length. The encoder callers give it complete NAL units that already start with the header byte. Thus the SPS starts with `67 67`, the PPS starts with `68 68`, and each entry is one byte too long.

The shared caller is `AnnexB::ExtractExtraDataForAVCC` in [AnnexB.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/AnnexB.cpp#458). The Windows encoder ([WMFDataEncoderUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFDataEncoderUtils.cpp#136)), the FFmpeg encoders ([FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#963)) and the Android encoder ([AndroidDataEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/android/AndroidDataEncoder.cpp#390)) use it. The libx264 path calls `WriteExtraData` directly ([FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#1035)). The code shows the same problem on Android, but nobody confirmed it on a device yet. macOS uses a separate writer in `AppleVTEncoder`, so it does not show the problem.

As comment 5 says, the mismatch dates from bug 1570337. It is not a recent regression.

**Next steps**

The patch in comment 5 (D334650) follows the fix direction: copy complete NAL units as they are, and add the header only in `CreateExtraData`. The current gtest `H264.AnnexBExtractExtraDataForAVCC` does not compare the SPS and PPS bytes, so a byte-exact check can prevent this problem again.

Bug 2049470 and bug 2031056 report the same defect. Because the patch is on this bug, we suggest that a person closes them as duplicates of this bug. This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.
title: AVC VideoEncoder on Windows and Linux produces invalid AVCC record in decoder description

comment:
Thank you for the report and the test page.

**Analysis**

Firefox gives the correct timestamp to the Windows Media Foundation encoder (MFT). But it then copies the MFT output sample time into the chunk without a check. [WMFMediaDataEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFMediaDataEncoder.cpp#518) reads the output time with `GetSampleTime()`. Line 545 writes it to the encoded frame. [VideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoEncoder.cpp#590) then uses that value as `EncodedVideoChunk.timestamp`. So the shift of one frame duration (0 + 500 = 500, 500 + 250 = 750) comes from the MFT, and Firefox trusts it.

The test page uses `avc1.64001f` (High profile) with the default latency mode and hardware preference. For non-realtime use, [MFTEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/wmf/MFTEncoder.cpp#805) turns off low latency mode, and Firefox does not set the B-frame count. This can let the MFT reorder frames or change the output times. The WPT `full-cycle-test` checks timestamps only with Baseline profile and `prefer-software`, so CI does not see this.

**Fix direction**

1. Keep the time and duration of each input frame in `WMFMediaDataEncoder`.
2. Give each output chunk the time of its matching input frame, not the MFT time.
3. Set the B-frame count to 0 where the MFT allows it, because WebCodecs has no decode timestamp.
4. Add a WPT case with High profile, hardware allowed and different frame durations.

This bug now blocks bug 1746557, the WebCodecs meta bug.
title: AVC VideoEncoder shifts EncodedVideoChunk timestamps by their duration

comment:
This bug waits for an answer to the question in comment 7, and there is no reply. We close it as incomplete.

**Analysis**

comment:
Thanks for the report and the about:support data.

**Analysis**

The Vulkan video decoder picks the wrong GPU on a system with two GPUs. In [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#1067), the decoder sorts the devices: a device that matches the renderer comes first, then a discrete GPU. When no device matches, the decoder takes the first device in the list. Thus the discrete NVIDIA GPU wins, as the "matches renderer: false" log line in comment 3 shows.

The device filter does not check for a DRM render node or for dma-buf export support. The NVIDIA check in [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/4523d65b575546e2b588dfb8b91e3d94ebeec19a/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#913) reads `/sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset`. When the `nvidia-drm` module is not loaded, this file does not exist, and the decoder keeps the NVIDIA GPU. Then the export fails with "Failed to export NV12 FD".

In Firefox 153 and 155, this export failure is a fatal error, so playback stops. Bug 2067923 changed it to a decode error in Firefox 157. Playback then continues, but with software decoding, not VA-API on the Intel GPU. The analysis does not show why the Intel GPU did not match the renderer.

**Fix direction**

When a device matches the renderer, use only that device. Remove devices that have no DRM render node or no dma-buf export support. Treat a missing `nvidia_drm` module the same as a disabled modeset. When no device is left, return `NS_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE`, so that VA-API decodes the video.

Comment 4 gives a workaround: set `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.enabled` to `false` in `about:config`.

This bug now blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

Martin, could you please look at the Vulkan device selection on systems with more than one GPU?
title: Video cannot play because vulkan video decode try use wrong device

comment:
Thank you for the report. The underflow in comment 0 cannot occur, because the code checks the crop values before the subtraction. But the same function has a debug assertion that a WebM file can reach, so this bug stays open for it.

**Analysis**

1. [WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#534) skips the video track when `cropH` or `cropV` is not valid, or when `cropH.value() >= params.width` or `cropV.value() >= params.height`. The branch calls `continue` in the track loop, so the demuxer does not use this track.
2. The subtraction at [WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#546) runs only after this check. Thus `params.width - cropH.value()` cannot wrap.
3. The code in comment 0 does not show this check, and its line numbers do not match the current tree. The current form of the check comes from bug 2050477, which landed in July 2026.
4. The check rejects both files that comment 0 names. For `webm_crop_underflow.webm`, `cropH` is 250 and `params.width` is 100. For `webm_crop_extreme.webm`, `cropH` is `0xFFFFFFFF` or not valid.
5. `croppedWidth` and `croppedHeight` only make `pictureRect`. Then `IsValidVideoRegion()` in [VideoUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/VideoUtils.cpp#245) checks that `pictureRect` is in the frame. Thus no wrapped value gets to an allocation or a bounds check.
6. The fix in comment 0 is the same check. The only difference is that the tree skips the track and does not return `NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_METADATA_ERR`.

The remaining problem: a `PixelWidth` or `PixelHeight` of 2^31 or more trips `AssertedCast<int32_t>` at [WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#550). This occurs only in debug builds. In release builds, `IsValidVideoRegion()` rejects the negative value.

**Next steps**

The fix is to reject a `PixelWidth` or `PixelHeight` that does not fit in `int32_t` before the cast, in the same way as the crop check. A WebM file with such a size can become a crashtest for debug builds. The two files that comment 0 names are not attached to this bug. Could you please attach them?

Thank you, Alex and Diego, for the interest in this bug. At this time, it is not a good first bug, because nobody knows the cause of the abort.

**Analysis**

The crash happens in the RDD process at startup, in the `CGSShutdownServerConnections()` call in [RDDParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/ipc/RDDParent.cpp#151). The top frame of the signature is only the Breakpad signal handler. The system frames that called `abort()` are not in the stack.

The "pass `true`" change in comment 9 and comment 22 does not fix the crash. Chromium and WebKit pass `true` to a different function, `CGSSetDenyWindowServerConnections(bool)`. Firefox already calls that function with `true` in [ContentChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/ipc/ContentChild.cpp#1732). The known SPI declaration of `CGSShutdownServerConnections` takes no argument. An extra argument does not change its behavior.

The same call without an argument is also in [UtilityProcessChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/ipc/glue/UtilityProcessChild.cpp#178), [SocketProcessChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/netwerk/ipc/SocketProcessChild.cpp#185) and [ContentChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/ipc/ContentChild.cpp#1723). All these calls disconnect the process from the WindowServer for the macOS sandbox. One shared helper can hold a fix for all of them.

The failure on 2026-08-16 on mozilla-esr153 is not this crash. Its log shows a test timeout and a parent process hang in `CVDisplayLink::stop()`. Its signature is `libsystem_kernel.dylib + 0x3062`, and it has no RDD or `CGS` frames.

**Next steps**

To find why CoreGraphics aborts, the next step is an RDD minidump with symbolicated Apple system frames. We suggest that a developer removes the `good-first-bug` keyword until the cause is known. This bug gets the `stalled` keyword until new data shows the cause.

comment:
Thank you for the report. The analysis in comment 2 is correct. This comment adds one point for the fix.

**Analysis**

The data size from the WAV header never gets to `DurationFromBytes`. The only caller is the last-chunk branch in [WaveDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/wave/WaveDemuxer.cpp#493). There, `mDataLength - mChunkIndex * DATA_CHUNK_SIZE` runs after `++mChunkIndex`, so the result is 0 or wraps below zero. Thus the last sample gets a duration of 0, or a very large value when the data length is not a multiple of 768 bytes.

This wrong value does not cause a memory error. `FindNextChunk` limits each read buffer to 768 bytes. `FFmpegAudioDecoder` sizes its output from the decoded frame count. The element duration and the buffered ranges use `Duration()`, which widens to 64 bits correctly.

**Fix direction**

A wider multiplication in [DurationFromBytes](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/wave/WaveDemuxer.cpp#426) alone does not correct the duration. The wrapped input still gives about 48695 s for a 1000-byte file. We recommend these changes:

1. Compute the last-chunk duration from the bytes read: `DurationFromBytes(aRange.Length())`.
2. Widen in `DurationFromBytes` with `static_cast<uint64_t>(aNumBytes) * 8`.
3. Add a WAV demuxer gtest that compares the sum of the sample durations with `Duration()`.

The same logic is in the first version of the demuxer from bug 1231793, so this is not a regression. The two WAV files in comment 0 are not attached, but the fix does not need them.
title: WAV Demuxer DurationFromBytes uint32_t Overflow Before Widening

comment:
Thank you for the analysis and the patch.

**Analysis**

The code confirms the cause. A pause stops the cubeb stream. A later seek then stashes the stopped stream, because [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#725) checks only for an error or a drained stream, not for a running stream.

On resume, [AudioSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSink.cpp#362) restarts the stream. Then `RebaseLive` in [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#533) carries no unplayed audio, because the backend restarted. MockCubeb keeps the queued audio across a stop, and your logs show the same for PulseAudio. Thus the clock leads the audible audio by the queued amount.

This is a regression from bug 2052692. The pref `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` is on by default on macOS and on Nightly, see [StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#14485). The same cause can explain the macOS desync in bug 2083467.

**Next steps**

The fix direction in [D335026](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D335026) looks correct: `AudioSinkWrapper::Stop` stashes the stream only when cubeb still runs. A seek after a pause then gets a new stream, as with the pref off. The patch waits for review. This bug now blocks the meta bug 2049891 (video decoding and seeking performance).

Workaround: set `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` to `false` in `about:config`.
title: media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek reuses a stream stopped by a pause, so the clock leads audio and 60 fps video judders

comment:
Thank you for the clear test case and the analysis.

**Analysis**

This is a regression from a recent change to the display size check in the MP4 demuxer.

1. mp4parse takes the display size from `tkhd`. For this init segment, the display size is 0x0.
2. `MP4VideoInfo::Update` in [DecoderData.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/mp4/DecoderData.cpp#344) rejects the track when `IsValidVideoDisplaySize(mDisplay)` fails. The check ignores the valid sample entry size (768x432).
3. `IsValidVideoDisplaySize` in [VideoUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/VideoUtils.cpp#266) requires a width and a height above 0.
4. The demuxer then drops the video track. `TrackBuffersManager::OnDemuxerInitDone` finds no track and calls `RejectAppend(NS_ERROR_FAILURE)` in [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d0d4af3c69ea85c292cbbdf68ae00126d5bae45b/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#1434). This gives the `rv=2147500037` in comment 0.

**Fix direction**

When the `tkhd` width or height is 0, use the sample entry size as the display size. Then run the current check. This keeps the current upper size limit. The init segment in the attached test case can become a gtest or a mochitest.

Alastor, could you please set the Regressed by field to the change that caused this, and confirm the fix direction?

comment:
Thanks for the report.

**Analysis**

The crash report is from a Fenix Nightly 160 content process on Android 12 (API 31). The crash is on the `WebrtcWorker` thread, at the `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_CRASH` in the black frame branch of `ProcessVideoFrame` ([VideoFrameConverter.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/VideoFrameConverter.h#491)). Crash Stats shows 2 crashes with this reason, all in 160.0a1.

The black frame branch gets a buffer from `mScalingPool`, which keeps at most `CONVERTER_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE` (5) buffers of one size. `CreateI420Buffer` returns `nullptr` when all 5 buffers are still in use, or when the allocation fails. The scaling branch uses the same pool ([VideoFrameConverter.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/VideoFrameConverter.h#396)). It drops the frame and asserts only after 100 failures in a row. The black frame branch crashes on the first failure.

A possible trigger is `SetTrackEnabled(false)`. The black frame then has the same size as the scaled frames that the encoder still holds, and `mLastFrameConverted` holds one more buffer. The crash report does not show which of the two `nullptr` causes occurred. The device had about 250 MiB of free physical memory.

In Beta and Release builds, the same branch logs a warning, drops the frame and continues. Bug 1931877 only changed the macro name, so it did not cause this crash. Bug 1538558 is an older intermittent with the same assertion message.

**Next steps**

We suggest that the black frame branch handle a `nullptr` buffer like the scaling branch. It can count the failures in a row and assert only after about 100. A real leak then still trips the assertion. Andreas Pehrson (:pehrsons) made the last change to this logic in bug 1938047 and knows this code.

comment:
The pernosco session in comment 10 is now available. Bugmon confirms that the testcase reproduces the assertion every time.

**Analysis**

- The assertion means that the graph did not finish its shutdown in 20 s after `ForceShutDown` ([AudioContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/webaudio/AudioContext.cpp#806), [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#1771)). In a release build, `Notify` removes the shutdown blocker and the graph leaks ([MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#1774)). We found no crash path in release builds.
- The stack has no `MediaTrackGraphShutDownRunnable` or `AudioCallbackDriver::Shutdown` frame. This is different from bug 2071751, where many queued cubeb `Init()` calls delayed the shutdown. Here the testcase uses only one AudioContext at 48 kHz.
- The worker shutdown in `nsThread::Shutdown()` runs a nested event loop. That loop still runs events, because the timer itself ran in it.
- Main hypothesis, not confirmed: the graph stopped its iterations before it handled the shutdown message. One possible cause is a cubeb stream that stops its callbacks and sends no `CUBEB_STATE_ERROR` ([GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#1103)). Another possible cause is a shutdown message that stays in the new tail dispatch path.
- The bugmon range in comment 2 has only Fenix and WPT meta changes. It does not explain the regression, so the regressor is not known.

**Next steps**

We recommend these checks in the pernosco session, at the time `Notify` runs:

1. Check whether `mForceShutDownReceived` is set.
2. Check `mAudioStreamState` and `mFallbackDriverState` of the `AudioCallbackDriver`.
3. Check the time of the last `DataCallback`.

The open needinfo on :karlt from comment 5 stays. This trace can also answer the question in bug 2071751 about an idle or blocked CubebOperation thread.

comment:
Thank you for the test files in comment 12.

**Analysis**

This is a known gap in the Firefox playback pipeline. It is not a regression. Bug 1273443 tracks the full work, and this bug depends on it.

- The MP4 demuxer makes a track demuxer for each track. But `MediaFormatReader::OnDemuxerInitDone` always uses track index 0 for video and for audio ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#1229), [MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#1269)).
- `MediaInfo` holds one audio track and one video track. Thus `HTMLMediaElement::ConstructMediaTracks` adds a maximum of one `AudioTrack` and one `VideoTrack` ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#8708)). This is why `audioTracks.length` is 1 in comment 0.
- mp4parse reads the `tkhd` enabled flag. But `Mp4parseTrackInfo` in the C API does not give the flag or the track language to Gecko ([lib.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/third_party/rust/mp4parse_capi/src/lib.rs#129)). Thus Firefox plays the first tracks of the comment 12 files, and `language` is empty.
- `media.track.enabled` is still `false` by default ([StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#13518)).

The HTML spec tells the browser to create one `AudioTrack` for each audio track in the resource ([HTML, media load resource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#concept-media-load-resource)). Firefox does not do this. The same steps let the media resource select the enabled tracks, with the first track as the fallback. The spec does not require the `tkhd` enabled flag. Thus the first-track choice conforms, but Chrome and Safari use the flag.

**Fix direction**

1. Give the `tkhd` enabled flag and the `mdhd` language from the mp4parse C API to `TrackInfo::mEnabled` and `TrackInfo::mLanguage` in [MP4Metadata.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/mp4/MP4Metadata.cpp).
2. In `OnDemuxerInitDone`, use the first enabled track of each type. If no track is enabled, use index 0.
3. For the full fix in bug 1273443, keep a list of tracks for each type in `MediaInfo`. Make one DOM track for each demuxed track, and add track switching in `MediaFormatReader`.

Steps 1 and 2 are a small change, and they fix the initial track choice in comment 12. Step 3 is large feature work. Bug 1999618 reports the same `audioTracks` problem, so we add it to See Also.
title: Firefox isn't seeing multiple audio tracks in a particular mp4 file

**Analysis**

The source tree agrees with comment 4. On Android, the native MediaCodec path creates the CDM in the RDD process. A decoder with a CDM can only run in the RDD process. But AImageReader runs only in the GPU process, and the GPU process decodes video only, not audio.

Affected code:

- [MediaKeys.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/eme/MediaKeys.cpp#450): the CDM is created with `RemoteMediaIn::RddProcess`.
- [RemoteDecoderModule.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/ipc/RemoteDecoderModule.cpp#74): on Android, a decoder with a CDM gets no support outside the RDD process.
- [RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/ipc/RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp#917): the GPU process gets `TrackSupport::DecodeVideo` only.
- [FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp#3139): AImageReader is used only when `XRE_IsGPUProcess()` is true.

**Next steps**

The fix direction is to create the CDM in the GPU process when AImageReader is on. Then the GPU process must also accept the audio decoder and the video decoder with a CDM. The WIP patch D331496 follows this direction. This bug now blocks meta bug 1980764 (Android Media Codec NDK).

comment:
Thank you for the report. This is the same problem as bug 2032329.

**Analysis**

Bug 2032329 reports the same handlers in [ContentParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/ipc/ContentParent.cpp), with the same missing `IsOwnedByProcess(ChildID())` check. That bug does not list `RecvNotifyGuessedPositionStateChanged`. This handler has the same shape and the same effect as `RecvNotifyPositionStateChanged`. Bug 2032329 closed in April 2026. Its comment 2 says that bug 2008912 added a check on the `BrowsingContext` arguments of IPC messages.

That check rejects a context when the sending process does not subscribe to its `BrowsingContextGroup`. Thus a compromised content process can name only a context in its own group, not an unrelated tab. Inside one group, it can still name a context that another process owns. Examples are an opener and its popup, or an embedder and its cross-origin iframes. The attack also needs a separate exploit that compromises the content process first.

The media keys always go to a context in the tab that owns the controller. They never go to a different tab.

New data that bug 2032329 does not cover can go on that bug, for example a working test case.

comment:
Thanks for the testcase. It gives a clear path to the crash.

**Analysis**

The WMF video decoder assumes that each input sample gives exactly one output frame. On the WebCodecs path, this assumption fails when one `EncodedVideoChunk` holds more than one H.264 access unit.

- WebCodecs is the only caller that sets `KeepOriginalPts` ([DecoderAgent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderAgent.cpp#116)).
- With that option, `WMFVideoMFTManager::Input` adds one PTS to `mPTSQueue` for each input sample ([WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp#507)).
- `WMFVideoMFTManager::Output` removes one PTS for each decoded frame ([WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp#1007)). Only a debug `MOZ_ASSERT` checks for an empty queue.
- In the first run of the testcase, the last chunk holds two pictures. Thus 5 chunks give 5 PTS values but 6 frames. The `flush()` call starts `ProcessDrain`, and the sixth frame reads `mPTSQueue[0]` on an empty array.

This is not only a debug problem. `nsTArray::operator[]` calls `InvalidArrayIndex_CRASH` in all build types, so release builds also crash. The crash is in the decoder process (RDD, or GPU with hardware decoding), not in the content process. Any web page can trigger it with the WebCodecs API.

Bug 1903669 fixed an earlier `mPTSQueue` underflow with the same signature. That fix limited the queue to the `KeepOriginalPts` path. It did not remove the one frame per input assumption, so the WebCodecs path still crashes. A second problem: `WMFVideoMFTManager::Flush()` does not clear `mPTSQueue`, so after a WebCodecs `reset()`, old PTS values can go to new frames.

**Fix direction**

1. In `Output`, when `mPTSQueue` is empty, keep the decoder PTS and log a warning. Do not index the array.
2. Clear `mPTSQueue` in `WMFVideoMFTManager::Flush()`.
3. As a more robust option, match each output frame to its input by sample time, not by queue position.
4. Add the attached testcase as a crashtest.

This bug blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557. Bug 1903669 is in See Also.
title: Hit MOZ_CRASH(ElementAt(aIndex = 0, aLength = 0)) at checkouts\gecko\mfbt\Assertions.cpp:51

comment:
**Analysis**

The defect in comment 0 is still in the current code. [UnderrunHandlerLinux.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/UnderrunHandlerLinux.cpp#17) has not changed since bug 1575883. `gRealtimeLimitReached` is one flag for the full process. The SIGXCPU handler sets it on the thread that the kernel selects (comment 1).

Two threads read the flag through `SoftRealTimeLimitReached()`. The first is the real-time audio callback thread in [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#755). The second is the graph iteration in [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#1637). Often that is the `GraphRunner` thread, which is not real-time on Linux ([GraphRunner.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/GraphRunner.cpp#121)). The thread that reads the flag first demotes only itself, then clears the flag. Thus the real-time thread that went over the limit can keep its real-time priority.

There is a second problem in `DemoteThreadFromRealTime()`. It reads the scheduling policy of the calling thread, which is already real-time. Then it sets the same policy again ([rt_linux.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/third_party/rust/audio_thread_priority/src/rt_linux.rs#250)). Thus the call does not lower the priority, but it clears the flag. Also, when the demote fails, the function returns before `atp_free_thread_info()`, and the `info` struct leaks.

The possible result is a kill of the content process at the RLIMIT_RTTIME hard limit. That is the crash type of bug 1653667. Bug 2080860 depends on this bug: `GraphRunner` can become real-time again on Linux only when the demotion works for each thread.

**Fix direction**

1. Keep a list of the promoted real-time threads, by thread id.
2. In the SIGXCPU handler, only write to a pipe or an eventfd.
3. Let a watchdog thread that is not real-time read the pipe and move each listed thread to `SCHED_OTHER`. This also removes the wait for the thread that went over the limit, as comment 0 says.
4. Make `DemoteThreadFromRealTime()` set a policy that is not real-time.

A deeper pass must check that the content sandbox lets one thread change the scheduling of a different thread id. If it does not, the parent process can do the demotion through AudioIPC.
title: Use thread-local instead of global in UnderrunHandlerLinux

comment:
Thank you for the reports. The drift still occurs after the bug 1955841 fix, on Linux with PipeWire and on Windows with WASAPI.

**Analysis**

The bug 1955841 fix is in Firefox 157 and later. It calls SoundTouch `flush()` on each switch from a non-1x rate back to 1x, in [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#719). `AudioStream` keeps the same time stretcher and never calls `clear()`.

`flush()` puts silence into the stretcher until the output has the number of frames that SoundTouch expects ([SoundTouch.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/media/libsoundtouch/src/SoundTouch.cpp#318)). This silence also increases `samplesExpectedOut` ([SoundTouch.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/media/libsoundtouch/src/SoundTouch.cpp#290)). Only `clear()` resets the counters. Thus each flush leaves a larger debt, and the next flush adds more silence.

`GetUnprocessed` plays this silence at 1x before new source audio ([AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#612)). The audio clock counts the silence as media time. Thus the clock moves ahead of the audio that you hear, and the gap grows with each switch. A model of the SoundTouch counters gives approximately 700 ms after 10 switches, which agrees with comment 6. A seek recreates the stream, and the drift goes away.

This analysis comes from the code and the model. Nobody has confirmed it with a log yet.

The fault is in `AudioStream` and in the bundled SoundTouch library, not in cubeb. The bug moves to Audio/Video: Playback, the component of bug 1955841. It also blocks bug 1904915, the YouTube playback meta bug.

A possible fix: reset the stretcher counters at each switch, or copy the flushed output into a buffer and then call `clear()`. The gtest in [TestAudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/gtest/TestAudioStream.cpp#102) checks drift in one direction only. It can also check for inserted silence.

**Next steps**

Paul, could you please look at this analysis? The per-switch `flush()` came with your fix in bug 1955841.
title: Audio and video desync when toggling playback speed on YouTube (Arch Linux / PipeWire)

comment:
Thanks for the patch in D335529. The analysis below confirms the cause and supports the fix direction.

**Analysis**

When a decode or flush completes, `DecoderTemplate` queues a separate output task with `QueueATask`. Nothing cancels that task. See the decode path at [DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#690) and the flush path at [DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#804). If `close()` or `reset()` runs before the task, `OutputDecodedData` runs with `mState` set to `Closed` or `Unconfigured`. It then fails the `MOZ_ASSERT` at [DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#352).

The ASan "SEGV on address 0x0" is the normal crash of a failed `MOZ_ASSERT`, not a real null pointer. In release builds, the decoder calls the output callback with stale frames after `close()`. This is a spec problem, not a memory safety problem, as comment 2 says.

An early return in `OutputDecodedData` when `mState != Configured` fixes the reported case. The flush path needs no other change, because reset and close already reject the pending flush promise. One gap stays: `configure()` sets `Configured` synchronously at [DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#173). Thus a stale task from before `reset(); configure()` can still pass the state check. A stronger guard compares the agent id that the output task captures with the current `mAgent`.

This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

**Next steps**

Chun-Min, could you please review D335529, or name a WebCodecs reviewer for it? The patch now asks `#media-playback-reviewers`.
title: VideoDecoder.close() does not prevent pending decode output callbacks, causing assertion failure and null-deref crash

comment:
Thank you for the report. Bug 2013013 and bug 2032329 report the same handlers. Bug 2008912 added a check that covers part of this report, but two problems are still open.

**Analysis**

Since bug 2008912, the parent checks every `MaybeDiscarded<BrowsingContext>` that a content process sends. The check is in [BrowsingContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#4670) and [BrowsingContextGroup.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/docshell/base/BrowsingContextGroup.cpp#272). The parent stops the IPC message when the sender process is not part of the `BrowsingContextGroup` of the context. Thus a content process cannot reach the `MediaController` of a tab in an unrelated group.

The ten handlers in [ContentParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/ipc/ContentParent.cpp#6755) still do not call `IsOwnedByProcess(ChildID())`. A compromised content process can name a context in its group that another process owns, for example an opener tab. It can then change the metadata, the playback state and the supported actions that the OS media controls show for that tab. It cannot receive the media keys of that tab, because [MediaController.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/mediacontrol/MediaController.cpp#282) sends each action only to the contexts of that tab.

A second problem does not need a context of another process. A false stop or pause message calls `DecreaseControlledMediaNum` or `DecreasePlayingMediaNum` in [MediaPlaybackStatus.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/fc216bdbdf04fca964b8f241844b0e6d048cc245/dom/media/mediacontrol/MediaPlaybackStatus.h#135). Only a `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT` guards each counter. Thus the parent process crashes on Nightly, and in release the counter wraps to `UINT_MAX`.

Both problems need a compromised content process. Web content cannot send these messages. The `FF160_VALID_SWEEP.md` file is not attached to this bug, so this analysis uses the code only.

**Next steps**

We suggest two changes:

1. Return early in all ten handlers when `IsOwnedByProcess(ChildID())` is false. The session history handlers in the same file use this pattern.
2. Ignore a decrease in `MediaPlaybackStatus` when the counter is already zero.

Caution: an owner check can drop late stop messages from the old process after a process switch. Test this case before the change lands.

Alastor, could you please look at the two fixes above?
title: Media-notify family writes any tab's MediaController: OS media-widget spoofing and media-key misrouting from a content process

comment:
Thank you for the detailed report and the vk_video_samples test.

**Analysis**

This looks like a defect in the NVIDIA driver (615.78.8 on the RTX 3090), in the AV1 decoding of Vulkan Video. NVIDIA's own vk_video_samples decoder gives the same wrong output without Firefox code. dav1d decodes the same data correctly, so the stream is valid. Keyframes are correct and most inter frames repeat the keyframe, which points to the reference frame handling in the driver.

In about:support, `HARDWARE_VIDEO_DECODING_VULKAN` is available and AV1 shows HWDEC. Firefox opens the FFmpeg AV1 decoder with the Vulkan hwaccel in `InitVulkanDecoder` ([FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp#671)). `VulkanCanDecodeFormat` ([FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp#521)) has no AV1 check for NVIDIA drivers. Thus no fallback stops this path.

Suggested fix direction: report the dumped stream and the vk_video_samples result to NVIDIA. Until a fixed driver is known, `VulkanCanDecodeFormat` can return false for AV1 on the affected NVIDIA drivers. Then AV1 falls back to VA-API or dav1d, and the other codecs keep Vulkan decoding.

This bug blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

**Workaround**

1. Open `about:config`.
2. Set `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.enabled` to `false`.
3. Close every Firefox window and restart Firefox.

**Next steps**

Martin, could you please look at this bug? Could you please decide on an AV1 fallback for these NVIDIA drivers?

**Analysis**

The failure in the filed job is one pixel over the fuzz limit. The job is `test-windows11-32-25h2/debug-reftest-wr-dc1-p-2` on autoland:

```
REFTEST TEST-UNEXPECTED-FAIL | dom/media/webvtt/test/reftest/vtt_overlapping_time.html == dom/media/webvtt/test/reftest/vtt_overlapping_time-ref.html | image comparison, max difference: 139, number of differing pixels: 191
REFTEST INFO | REFTEST fuzzy test (0, 0) <= (139, 191) <= (170, 190)
```

The manifest line in [reftest.list](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/webvtt/test/reftest/reftest.list#2) allows `fuzzy-if(winWidget,0-170,0-190)`. Bug 2075088 changed this limit from `0-190` pixels of `0-170`... see the next paragraph.

Bug 2075088 changed the pixel limit from 170 to 190. That change also made the Windows overlay state of a video depend on how many frames WebRender builds. It also widened the fuzz of about 20 WebVTT WPT tests on Windows. The differing pixel count is small, and the filer saw no visible difference. Thus the difference is most likely at the edges of the cue text, not in the video frame. Nobody has checked the failure images yet, so this is not confirmed.

The test is timing sensitive. [vtt_overlapping_time.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/webvtt/test/reftest/vtt_overlapping_time.html) takes the snapshot while the video plays, at the first `timeupdate` after 1 second. [vtt_overlapping_time-ref.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/webvtt/test/reftest/vtt_overlapping_time-ref.html) seeks to 2 seconds and takes the snapshot while the video is paused. Thus the two pages build very different numbers of frames.

Bug 1788347 was the earlier tracking bug for this test. It closed with no fix.

**Next steps**

Two fix directions are possible:

1. Increase the pixel limit in `reftest.list`, as bug 2075088 did for the WPT cue tests.
2. Make the test and the reference reach the same state. For example, pause the test page after 1 second, and play the reference page past 1 second before it pauses.

Alastor, could you please look at this failure? This test is in your WebVTT area.

comment:
Thanks for the tests and the spec issue.

**Analysis**

The MP4 demuxer copies the `tkhd` size into `VideoInfo::mDisplay` for every video codec ([DecoderData.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/mp4/DecoderData.cpp#340)). The H.264 and VP9 paths later replace that value, but each path does it differently. The AV1 path never replaces it.

- **H.264 and HEVC:** the demuxer replaces `mDisplay` with the SPS size before `loadedmetadata` ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#338)). This is why H.264 reports 320x240 throughout.
- **VP9:** `VPXChangeMonitor` keeps a pixel aspect ratio from `mImage` and `mDisplay`, which is 1.0 for this file. On the first keyframe that the monitor handles, it applies that ratio to the coded size ([MediaChangeMonitor.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/platforms/wrappers/MediaChangeMonitor.cpp#637)). The result is 320x240. For VP9 in MP4, this path runs only when the monitor creates a new decoder, so the switch looks like a side effect.
- **AV1:** `AV1ChangeMonitor::UpdateConfig` changes `mDisplay` only when the coded size changes ([MediaChangeMonitor.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/06fa2674be3db4f3b623bad938282310509cc54b/dom/media/platforms/wrappers/MediaChangeMonitor.cpp#723)). The av1C box and the sequence header both give 320x240, which equals `mImage`. Thus `mDisplay` stays at 160x120.

The rest of the pipeline only carries `mDisplay` to `videoWidth`/`videoHeight`. `requestVideoFrameCallback` reports the decoded image size, so it shows 320x240. This is not a regression: the aspect ratio logic in both monitors is from bug 1764425.

**Next steps**

The decision in [whatwg/html issue 13106](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13106) sets the correct behavior here. If the spec uses the declared size only for the aspect ratio, one rule in the MP4 demuxer for all codecs is the cleaner fix. That rule turns the `tkhd` size into an aspect ratio and applies it to the coded size. A smaller option is to make `AV1ChangeMonitor` apply `mPixelAspectRatio` on the first sequence header too. The VP9 path must then not depend on a new decoder. The tentative tests in WPT PR 63960 can land with the fix.

This bug now blocks bug 1452683 (AV1 playback support). Bug 2083754 is related: it is about a `tkhd` size of 0 in MSE.
title: videoWidth/videoHeight keep the MP4 tkhd size for AV1 instead of the decoded size

comment:
This reftest failed on Windows 11 32-bit debug (`reftest-wr-dc1-p`). 191 pixels are different, and the limit is 190.

**Analysis**

comment:
Thank you for the detailed work and the upstream fix.

**Analysis**

The cause is in the upstream OpenH264 plugin, not in Gecko. In OpenH264 2.6.0, `OpenH264VideoDecoder::Decode_w` in `module/gmp-openh264.cpp` gives a stack-local `data[3]` array to the decoder. With multithreaded decoding, the plugin frame threads (`WelsDec::pThrProcFrame`) can still use that array after the worker thread stack is gone. Your fix in [OpenH264 PR 4009](https://github.com/cisco/openh264/pull/4009) moves the array into the decoder object. OpenH264 2.7.0 includes it.

The attached crash data agrees with this. The macOS report (attachment 9631160) and bp-8b799ed2-15f8-49bc-b5df-92d640260825 and bp-312c5efa-3d84-48ee-be50-309e70260825 show a write to an unmapped address on a plugin frame thread. At the same time, the main thread waits in `CWelsDecoder::CloseDecoderThreads`, called from `GMPVideoDecoderChild::~GMPVideoDecoderChild`. The two Linux stacks (attachment 9645335 and attachment 9666343) show a pointer filled with `0x68` bytes while an OpenH264 frame thread decodes. No Gecko GMP frame causes the fault.

The link between the stale array and every crash is probable, not proven, because the plugin has no symbols. Your result that the patch removes the Linux crashes supports it.

The Gecko code does not need a change. The crash occurs only when `media.gmp.decoder.multithreaded` is `true`. Its default is `false` in [StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/034cd8a8207e38b04afec5e6f75e5161f75a112f/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#13464). Firefox still uses OpenH264 2.6.0 in [openh264.json](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/034cd8a8207e38b04afec5e6f75e5161f75a112f/toolkit/content/gmp-sources/openh264.json#72) and [openh264.yml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/034cd8a8207e38b04afec5e6f75e5161f75a112f/taskcluster/kinds/fetch/openh264.yml#10).

**Next steps**

The fix for this bug is the update to OpenH264 2.7.0. Bug 2085032 tracks it, and bug 2085033 updates the CI revisions. After that update lands, the steps in comment 23 can confirm the fix. Bug 2071378 is the related Linux sandbox problem with multithreaded mode.

The cause is in the WebRender code, so this bug moves to Core :: Graphics: WebRender.

**Analysis**

The `about:logging` profile in comment 2 shows hardware H.264 decode through D3D11 DXVA in the GPU process, with NV12 output. The decoder works. The GPU process Renderer logs this error about 120 times per second during playback:

`[GFX1-]: RenderDXGITextureHost descriptor (1920x1080 fmt 16) does not match resource (1920x1088 DXGI 103)`

The 1088 rows come from normal decoder padding. When this check fails, `RenderDXGITextureHost` gives no video texture to WebRender for that frame, so the frame shows green. The screenshot and the video in comment 0 and comment 1 show this green image.

The regressor in the Regressed by field changed this check in `RenderDXGITextureHost` in [RenderD3D11TextureHost.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/034cd8a8207e38b04afec5e6f75e5161f75a112f/gfx/webrender_bindings/RenderD3D11TextureHost.cpp). It landed on 2026-10-21. This is a regression in Nightly 160, and comment 3 gives the regression range.

comment:
Thank you for the two full vmmap captures and the test with hardware decoding off.

**Analysis**

The 8,112 KiB regions are probably IPC Shmem buffers that each hold one 1920x1080 frame in 32-bit RGB. That is 8,294,400 bytes, rounded up to the 16 KiB page. The probable allocator is `RemoteMediaManagerParent::RecvReadback` in [RemoteMediaManagerParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/034cd8a8207e38b04afec5e6f75e5161f75a112f/dom/media/ipc/RemoteMediaManagerParent.cpp#312). It copies a decoded frame into a new Shmem when a content process asks for that frame as RGB. Software frames and hardware frames give the same buffer size, so this matches the growth with hardware decoding on and off.

The RDD keeps each buffer until the content process frees its copy, or until that content process closes its connection to the RDD. Code reading did not find which side keeps the buffers. Thus the cause is not located yet.

The missing `shmem-allocated` reporter in the RDD does not show that shared memory is not involved. The RDD tries to register that reporter before XPCOM starts, so the registration probably fails ([SharedMemoryHandle.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/034cd8a8207e38b04afec5e6f75e5161f75a112f/ipc/glue/SharedMemoryHandle.cpp#45)). In the attached about:memory, only the Main Process has this reporter. This is a separate problem in the IPC code.

Andrew, could you please look at the `Readback` path and tell us what can keep these Shmems alive?

comment:
Bug 2014896 fixed the same assert for the case where maxDistance equals refDistance. This bug has a different cause, and that fix does not cover it.

**Analysis**

The testcase sends +inf and -inf from two GainNodes into `panner.positionZ`. The input sum is NaN, so the position and the distance in `ComputeDistanceGain` are NaN. `std::min` and `std::max` in `LinearGainFunction` keep the NaN, and `AssertedCast<float>` fails ([PannerNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/55c075041e43304459a082af8dfbac5f90e1a18d/dom/media/webaudio/PannerNode.cpp#398)).

The root cause is in `AudioParamTimeline::GetComplexValueAtTime` and `AudioParamTimeline::GetValuesAtTime` ([AudioParamTimeline.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/55c075041e43304459a082af8dfbac5f90e1a18d/dom/media/webaudio/AudioParamTimeline.h#111)). They add the AudioNode input to the param value with no NaN check. The spec section [Computation of Value](https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#computation-of-value) replaces a NaN computed value with the `defaultValue` of the param. The WPT [nan-param.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/55c075041e43304459a082af8dfbac5f90e1a18d/testing/web-platform/tests/webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audioparam-interface/nan-param.html) tests this step, and Firefox has it as `expected: FAIL`.

Release builds do not have the assert. There, `std::max(0.0f, NaN)` in `ComputeDistanceGain` returns 0, so the panner output is silent. This analysis comes from the code and the WPT expectation. Bugmon could not reproduce the assert on the same build (comment 1), so nobody confirmed it with a run yet.

This is not a known regression. The missing NaN step is old behavior.

**Next steps**

Suggested fix direction:

1. In both `AudioParamTimeline` functions, replace a NaN sum with the default value of the param.
2. Add a `DefaultValue()` accessor to `AudioEventTimeline`, because `mDefaultValue` is private.
3. Remove the FAIL expectation in [nan-param.html.ini](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/55c075041e43304459a082af8dfbac5f90e1a18d/testing/web-platform/meta/webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audioparam-interface/nan-param.html.ini).
4. Add a crashtest with the graph of this bug in an `OfflineAudioContext`, next to `2014896.html`.

A guard only in `LinearGainFunction` hides the assert. It keeps the NaN position for the other distance models and for the cone gain.
title: AssertedCast error: Cannot cast -nan from double to float: out of range

comment:
Thanks for the update. A profile refresh fixed it for you (comment 36), and it did the same in comment 28.

**Analysis**

The profiles in comment 25 show where the failure happens. On the failing profile, Firefox starts no RDD process. The logs show only `Sandbox Utility Generic decoder rejects requested type video/avc`, and no RDD decoder line. Without RDD, the only video decoder left on Linux is OpenH264, a GMP plugin. Thus Firefox reports VP9 and AV1 as unsupported, and YouTube sends H.264 (`avc1.4d401f`, Main profile).

On a seek, OpenH264 rejects the keyframe at the seek target with GMPErr 7. Firefox then reports `NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_FATAL_ERR`, and YouTube shows "An error occurred". This happens again each time YouTube recreates the decoder. On the fresh profiles, YouTube sends AV1, and ffvpx decodes it in the RDD process with no error.

**Code path**

[PDMFactory.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/dom/media/platforms/PDMFactory.cpp#724) adds the RDD decoder module only when `media.rdd-process.enabled` is true. The in-content ffvpx and FFmpeg modules stay behind `media.allow-audio-non-utility` ([PDMFactory.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/dom/media/platforms/PDMFactory.cpp#748)), which is false on desktop. So the decoder chain falls to [GMPDecoderModule.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/gmp/GMPDecoderModule.cpp#55), which supports only H.264 through OpenH264.

The probable trigger is a stale `media.rdd-process.enabled=false` value in the old profiles. "Refresh Firefox" resets the prefs, and that matches comment 28, comment 32 and comment 36. The about:support files in comment 32 are on an external host that the triage cannot read, so the pref is not confirmed. The analysis of the profiles in comment 16 and comment 17 did not complete.

**What stays open**

1. Firefox reports H.264 support through OpenH264 for media element and MSE playback when no remote video decoder exists. OpenH264 is mainly a decoder for WebRTC, and its Main profile support is probably partial.
2. When RDD is off, Firefox has no in-content decoder for VP9 and AV1 video.
3. Nothing shows the user that a non-default `media.rdd-process.enabled` breaks video playback.

**Fix direction**

We can stop reporting GMP H.264 support for playback when no remote video decoder exists. Another option is to let in-content ffvpx decode video when RDD is off. A note in about:support for a non-default `media.rdd-process.enabled` can also help.

Regression status is not known. The reporters first saw the problem in Firefox 124. The block on in-content decoding came from bug 1835804, in Firefox 116. The trigger is profile state, so mozregression cannot find it. Bug 1971032 shows the same OpenH264 GMPErr 7 failure on Arte. This bug stays in the YouTube playback meta bug 1904915.
title: Youtube video crashes when skipping time

comment:
Thanks for the versions, the about:support and the recordings. Tymur plans to look at this bug (comment 13).

**Analysis**

The probable cause is in `ChooseVulkanPixelFormatFromContext` in [FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp#480). For a libavcodec older than 63.8.101, Firefox sets `outputIsDpb = !mDriverDistinctDpb`. Then it writes `hwfc->usage` without `VK_IMAGE_USAGE_VIDEO_DECODE_DPB_BIT_KHR`.

RADV on the Radeon 680M reports both COINCIDE and DISTINCT. In that case, a libavcodec older than 63.8.101 uses the output image as the reference picture. Thus each reference picture is an image without DPB usage. The system FFmpeg 9.0.2 from comment 5 is probably in this version range, because the FFmpeg 9.0.1 in ffvpx is libavcodec 63.1.101.

The recordings match this cause. In attachment 9667298, a green band covers the bottom rows of the picture. The luma in the band is correct, and only the chroma is missing. The top edge of the band has macroblock steps, and green blocks follow the motion. This pattern comes from motion compensation with bad references, not from a wrong export layout.

This behavior started with the part 3 change of bug 2083226, in `ChooseVulkanPixelFormatFromContext`, which landed on 2026-10-19. Before that change, the same setup showed solid green frames. Thus this is not a regression of a setup that worked. Code reading found this cause, and no log confirms it yet. A run with the Vulkan validation layer can confirm it: the layer should report reference pictures without DPB usage.

H.264 always uses the system FFmpeg, because ffvpx has no H.264 decoder. This explains why `prefer-system-ffmpeg` has no effect.

The profile in comment 5 uses a newer profile format that our tools cannot read yet. This is a gap in our tools, and the analysis above does not use the profile.

**Fix direction**

1. Take `outputIsDpb` from the `hwfc->usage` that libavcodec sets, for every libavcodec version.
2. When the output image has DPB usage and the driver reports DISTINCT, skip direct export.
3. In that case, use the copy path and log the reason.
4. Detect ffvpx with `FFVPX_VERSION`, not with the libavcodec version number.

The last step is necessary because ffvpx reports 63.1.101 but already has the DISTINCT logic.

This bug blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).
title: [Linux][Vulkan Video] Decoded video is green with direct-export on Radeon 680M

comment:
Thanks for the clear analysis and the log. The code in the current tree agrees with it.

**Analysis**

[FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVideoEncoder.cpp#221) builds the level text in `GetH264Level()`, which inserts a '.' and so makes 31 into "3.1". `GetH264Settings()` adds it as the private "level" option. `InitEncoderInternal()` then passes it with `av_opt_set()`, and `OpenCodecContext()` fails. The FFmpeg libx264 wrapper gives this text to `x264_param_parse()`, which reads it with `strtod()`. Under a decimal-comma `LC_NUMERIC`, `strtod()` stops at the '.', so the open fails with EINVAL. This matches the "Error parsing option 'level'" line in the log.

The content process gets the user locale because [XPCOMInit.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/xpcom/build/XPCOMInit.cpp#280) calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")`. No code sets `LC_NUMERIC` back to "C" after that. In Release, the video encoder runs in the content process. On Linux Nightly, the encoder runs in the RDD process, which does not call `setlocale()`. Thus Nightly is probably not affected, but nobody has tested this.

The level is the only decimal value that this encoder passes as text. All other options are integers or names. `mCodecContext->level` already holds the integer 31, and the libx264 wrapper reads it.

**Fix direction**

For libx264 only, pass the level as its integer `level_idc` text ("31"). x264 reads a value of 7 or more as a `level_idc` with `atoi()`, which does not use the locale. Do not use "31" for all encoders: `h264_mediacodec` reads "3.1" as a named value. Do not change `LC_NUMERIC` around the open, because `setlocale()` is process-wide and not thread-safe. A gtest in `TestMediaDataEncoder.cpp` can set a decimal-comma locale and init an H.264 encoder at level 3.1. It must skip when that locale or a system libx264 is not available.

`isConfigSupported()` only checks that an encoder exists and does not open it, so it returns true here. This problem goes away with the fix above.

This bug blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557. It is not a regression: the "X.Y" level text is in the code since at least early 2024.
title: WebCodecs H.264 encoding fails on Linux under a decimal-comma locale: libx264 rejects level "3.1"

In [GPUProcessManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/774fa0cf68ccf50e8da30f50e71714abdc4686b5/gfx/ipc/GPUProcessManager.cpp), `GPUProcessHost::KillHard` with no minidump is one path that gives this pattern. The log shows this sequence for `codecs="hev1.1.6.L60.90"`:

1. The init segment and chunk0 append correctly. The buffered range grows to [0.08, 0.52).
2. The content process then logs `Decode error: NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_FATAL_ERR (0x806e0005) - mozilla::MediaChangeMonitor::CreateDecoderAndInit(MediaRawData *)::(lambda): Unable to create decoder`.

The probable cause is that DXVA is not available on these workers in some runs. HEVC on Windows has no software decoder, so the decoder cannot be created. The log has no decoder module log, so it does not show why DXVA is off.

- Is the DXVA failure on these workers an infra problem?
- Should the test listen for the `error` event, so that a decoder failure ends the test quickly and not with a timeout?

**Analysis**

The stuck file is `avc-2bytes-nalu.mp4` (H.264, video only). The `loadedmetadata` event fires, but no first frame arrives in 180 seconds. The debug dump shows `"videoDecoderName":"NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_FATAL_ERR (0x806e0005) - ProcessConstruct"`, and `hasDecoder` is false. Thus the creation of the Android video decoder failed in `RemoteDataDecoder::ProcessConstruct` ([RemoteDataDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/platforms/android/RemoteDataDecoder.cpp#1083)). The CI log has no media log and no child process crash, so the reason for this failure is not known.

The element stays in the loading state after the fatal error. Thus the error probably does not reach the media element as an `error` event. A check of the reject path in `MediaFormatReader::DecoderFactory::DoCreateDecoder` can confirm this.

The same file stalls with the same dump in bug 2075576 (`test_timeupdate_small_files.html`) and in bug 2051403 (`test_play_events.html`). Those dumps show the video decoder as "uninitialized", so they can have the same cause. This is not confirmed.

**Next steps**
