comment:
This failure is frequent and occurs only on android-hw-a55-14-0-aarch64 debug, in all geckoview-mochitest-media variants. Treeherder shows about 50 failures from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-24, on about 30 different devices.

**Analysis**

The probable cause is a race in the test. [test_bug966247.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/webaudio/test/test_bug966247.html) calls `ok()` only in `onaudioprocess`, and calls `SimpleTest.finish()` on the `ended` event. The clip `ting-48k-1ch.ogg` is 0.694 s long. If no audioprocess event fires before `ended`, the test has zero checks.

The captured media element and the AudioContext nodes use different clocks while the audio device starts. The `DecodedStream` output track advances on the fallback system clock while cubeb starts ([GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#692)). The AudioContext node tracks start suspended. They resume only when the audio driver runs without the fallback ([MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#424)). With the default buffer of 4096 frames, the ScriptProcessorNode fires its first event after about 85 ms of processed audio ([ScriptProcessorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/webaudio/ScriptProcessorNode.cpp#312)).

Thus, if the audio device starts about 0.6 s late, the clip ends first. The CI log has no media log lines, so this late start is not confirmed. A failing run with `MOZ_LOG=MediaTrackGraph:4,cubeb:4` can confirm it. The missing connection to `destination` is not the cause, because the node fires with only an input connection ([ScriptProcessorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/webaudio/ScriptProcessorNode.cpp#525)). No in-tree regressor is known. The start date can come from a change in the CI device pool, but this is not confirmed.

**Next steps**

Suggested test fix, with no product change:

1. Wait for `ac.resume()`, or for `ac.state` "running", before `a.play()`.
2. Count the audioprocess callbacks.
3. In the `ended` handler, assert that the count is above 0.
4. Optionally use a longer clip, or a smaller buffer such as `createScriptProcessor(1024, 1, 1)`.
title: Intermittent dom/media/webaudio/test/test_bug966247.html | single tracking bug

comment:
Thanks for the clear steps.

**Analysis**

The `Position` property getter in [MPRISServiceHandler.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/widget/gtk/MPRISServiceHandler.cpp#208) casts the position in seconds to `int64_t` before it multiplies by 1000000. The cast drops the fraction, so 142.374 s becomes 142000000. The value changes only when the position crosses a whole second, which explains the once-per-second steps.

The position before the cast is exact. `PositionState::CurrentPlaybackPosition` in [MediaSession.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/mediasession/MediaSession.cpp#23) computes it as a `double` from the last update time and the playback rate. The `mpris:length` metadata in [MPRISServiceHandler.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/widget/gtk/MPRISServiceHandler.cpp#826) uses the same cast, so the track length also loses its fraction. `EmitSeekedSignal` multiplies first and then casts, so the `Seeked` signal keeps full precision.

The cast came with the `Position` getter in bug 1634192 (Firefox 131), so this is not a regression. Bug 2065930 is a different `Position` problem in the same getter.

**Fix direction**

1. In the `Position` getter, multiply the `double` seconds by 1e6 first, then cast.
2. Check for overflow against the `gint64` maximum, as `EmitSeekedSignal` does.
3. Apply the same change to `mpris:length`.
4. Optionally, move the conversion into one helper for all three places.

No MPRIS test exists now. A GTest on the conversion helper can show the fix: 142.374 s must give 142374000.
title: MPRIS Position property is truncated to whole seconds

comment:
This regression comes from bug 2046813, and az is looking at it (comment 2). The analysis below is from the CI profiles and from code reading.

**Analysis**

The After profile on linux2404-64-shippable shows 110 shutdown blockers named `MediaCapabilities::CheckVideoDecodingInfo` on the content main thread. The Before profile has none. Their median duration is 16.6 ms, and the maximum is 68.3 ms. The main thread is idle during each wait, and `MediaCapabilities.decodingInfo` uses fewer samples than before. So the time is a wait for work on a thread that the profile does not record.

The probable cause is Part 2 of bug 2046813, not Part 4 at the push tip. Part 2 adds `MaybeSynthesizeCodecConfig` in [MediaCapabilities.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/mediacapabilities/MediaCapabilities.cpp). It writes a codec configuration for profile-less VP8 and for HEVC. Before this change, `MediaChangeMonitor` got no extra data for these test strings. It returned a shell decoder with no underlying decoder and no IPC.

`media.mediacapabilities.codec-support-cache.enabled` is false by default. So each video query runs the strict probe `PDMFactory::StrictSupportsAsync` in [PDMFactory.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/platforms/PDMFactory.cpp). Now this probe creates, initializes and shuts down a real remote decoder for VP8 and HEVC. The probes also go through a one-token `SingleAllocPolicy` in [AllocationPolicy.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/media/platforms/AllocationPolicy.cpp). The token comes back only after the remote shutdown, so each probe also waits for the previous one.

This explains the VP8 and HEVC regressions on Linux and macOS, and the small VP8 change on Windows. The VP9, AV1 and AVC test strings are fully qualified, so they already made a real decoder and did not change. The cost difference between Linux (about 30 ms) and macOS (about 5 ms) is not confirmed. One hypothesis is the hardware decoder setup in the FFmpeg decoder on Linux. The audio improvements and the Linux AV1 file improvement are not explained by this change and are probably noise.

**Next steps**

The profile has no media decoder threads, so it cannot split the wait between decoder creation, `Init`, the allocation queue and the IPC round trip. Possible directions are:

1. Compare the new VP8 and HEVC values with the old VP9 and AVC values. If they match, the old values measured a shell decoder, and the new baseline is the real cost.
2. Cache the strict probe results in the process, keyed on the codec, the profile and the bit depth.
3. Turn on the cached path once it reports hardware support correctly.

This bug blocks the MediaCapabilities meta bug 1758786.
title: 27911.46 - 6.54% media-capabilities decode-media-source-video-vp8-hot + 38 more (Linux, OSX, Windows) regression on Tue October 20 2026

comment:
**Analysis**

The parent process crashes on the AudioIPC server RPC thread, in the crash report from comment 0. The panic is in `LengthDelimitedCodec::decode`, at [codec.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/third_party/rust/audioipc2/src/codec.rs#142). The frame header had the correct `MAGIC`, but its length field was `0xFFFFFFFF`. The `n <= MAX_MESSAGE_LEN` assert then fails, and the panic stops the parent process.

The peer of this connection is a content process. It connects through `ContentParent::RecvCreateAudioIPCConnection` and `audioipc2_server_new_client`. Thus a bad frame from one content process stops the whole browser. `decode_length` has the same problem: its `MAGIC` assert at [codec.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/third_party/rust/audioipc2/src/codec.rs#94) also panics.

An error path already exists. `decode_data` returns an `Err`, and `FramedDriver::process_inbound` at [ipccore.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/third_party/rust/audioipc2/src/ipccore.rs#653) gives it to `EventLoop::poll`. There, the error closes only that connection, at [ipccore.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/third_party/rust/audioipc2/src/ipccore.rs#260).

Bug 1986089 has the sibling signature in `decode_length`, where the `MAGIC` bytes are wrong. Both crashes probably come from the same damage to the inbound header bytes. The source of that damage is not known. Code reading shows no framing desync.

**Fix direction**

1. In `decode_length` and `decode`, return an `io::ErrorKind::InvalidData` error in place of the two asserts.
2. Check the length before `buf.reserve(n)`.
3. Keep the assert in `encode`, because it checks local data.
4. Log or count the new error, so that the damage from bug 1986089 stays visible.

The fix must land upstream in `mozilla/audioipc` first. Then it must be vendored again.

The crash volume is low. SuperSearch shows 2 crashes with this signature in the last 6 months, and the other crash is on Android with a different panic message. This is not a regression: the signature exists since builds from February 2024. Matthew Gregan already has a needinfo on this bug from comment 0.
title: Crash in [@ <audioipc2::codec::LengthDelimitedCodec<In, Out> as audioipc2::codec::Codec>::decode]

comment:
This is the same defect as bug 1909744. That bug reports that `WorkletJSContext::Initialize` calls `JS_SetFutexCanWait`, so `Atomics.wait` can block a worklet thread although HTML gives worklet agents `[[CanBlock]]` false. Bug 1909744 is still open in DOM: Core & HTML.

**Analysis**

The call is in [WorkletThread.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/worklet/WorkletThread.cpp#147), with no condition. The engine throws the `TypeError` only when `canWait()` is false, in `DoAtomicsWait` in [AtomicsObject.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/js/src/builtin/AtomicsObject.cpp#1318). Workers limit the opt-in to dedicated workers in [RuntimeService.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/workers/RuntimeService.cpp#1025). All worklets share `WorkletJSContext`, so one fix covers AudioWorklet and PaintWorklet. `Atomics.waitAsync` is not affected.

About the component (comment 1): [moz.build](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/efd2d1e6f77570ae6bc5294731a68101e45c81a3/dom/worklet/moz.build) puts `dom/worklet/` in DOM: Core & HTML. That is why bug 1909744 is there. The fix is in the worklet code, not in the media code.

New detail for bug 1909744: no WPT covers `Atomics.wait` in a worklet. `requires-failure.https.any.js` covers only window and service worker. A cross-origin-isolated AudioWorklet WPT can show the fix.
title: Atomics.wait does not throw in worklets

comment:
Thanks for the clear steps and the test page.

**Analysis**

The server sends two different MP4 files for this URL. The `Referer` header selects the file. Without a `Referer`, the file has ETag `"4f9d3c22…"` and 4837174 bytes. With a `Referer` from `videos-cdn.ispot.tv`, the file has ETag `"7d3b9f3f…"` and 7170953 bytes. The responses send no `Vary` header. A HEAD request with and without the `Referer` header shows this every time.

The probable failure path in Gecko for a direct load:

1. [VideoDocument.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/html/VideoDocument.cpp#113) gives the navigation channel to the media element. That request has no `Referer`, so the server sends the smaller file.
2. The `moov` box is at the end of that file, at offset 4804084. [MoofParser.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/mp4/MoofParser.cpp#200) reads there, so [MediaCache.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/MediaCache.cpp#1589) seeks with a new range request.
3. For that request, [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#7866) sets the `Referer` from the owner document. In a video document, that is the MP4 URL itself, so the server now sends the larger file.
4. [ChannelMediaResource.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/ChannelMediaResource.cpp#267) accepts the new total length. It sends no `If-Range` and does not compare the ETag. The parser then reads `mdat` data of the other file at that offset, and [MP4Metadata.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/mp4/MP4Metadata.cpp#520) reports "Cannot parse metadata".

In a `<video>` element on a page, every request has the same `Referer`, so all bytes come from one file and playback works. This explains both results. A `MOZ_LOG=MediaResource:5,MediaCache:5,nsHttp:3` log of the direct load can confirm step 3 and step 4.

**Next steps**

The main fault is on the site: it changes the body by `Referer` without `Vary: Referer`. This is not a regression: the `Referer` and range code paths did not change recently.

Gecko can still be more robust. Suggest that `ChannelMediaResource` keeps the ETag and the total length of the first response. It can then send `If-Range` on range requests. When a range response shows a different file, it can restart from offset 0 or report a clear network error. It must not join the data of two files.
title: Navigating directly to MP4 url results in NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_METADATA_ERR while it plays fine embedded in a <video> element

comment:
The code confirms the cause in comment 3. Each `currentTime` set cancels the seek that is still running, and Firefox draws a frame only when a seek completes.

**Analysis**

- `MediaDecoder::CallSeek` ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#700)) disconnects the promise of the previous seek. Then `StateObject::HandleSeek` in the state machine makes a new `AccurateSeekingState` for each new seek.
- The new `DoSeek` stops the sink and calls `MediaFormatReader::ResetDecode` ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#2864)). This flushes the decoder, and the demuxer seeks again to the keyframe before the target. The work of the cancelled seek is lost.
- `DropVideoUpToSeekTarget` ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9098b3e11c2fbc2b2d84e53a3c784814cbdab3e/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#2117)) pushes only the frame at the target. A paused video shows the seek frame only through `Redraw` in `SeekCompleted`. No path shows a frame of a cancelled seek.
- Thus a seek must complete within one animation frame, about 16 ms, to show a frame. The video in the reduced testcase (attachment 9667178) has one keyframe for 300 frames. So each seek decodes from the first frame, and its cost grows with the target time. Probably only the early seeks complete in time, which agrees with the 27 `seeked` events in Firefox.
- This code is the same on all platforms, which agrees with the reports on Linux and Windows, in Nightly and in Release. It looks like long-standing design, not a regression.

**Fix direction (not tested)**

1. In `AccurateSeekingState`, keep the running seek when a new accurate seek arrives. Store only the newest target as a pending seek.
2. When the running seek completes, draw its frame with `Redraw`. Then start the pending seek at once, with no `seeked` event for the replaced seek.
3. When the new target is after the current decode position with no keyframe between them, skip the flush and the demuxer seek. Bug 1501715 tracks this idea.

This change is medium in size, because it changes the seek states. A spec check on whether the HTML seeking algorithm lets a browser show the frame of an aborted seek is not done yet.

**Related bugs**

Bug 2071427 (choppy scrubbing on x.com) shows a similar symptom. But it is a regression from Firefox 156, so its cause can be different. Bug 2049891 is the meta bug for decoding and seeking performance.

**Next steps**

Alastor has the needinfo from comment 5. We can file a Core :: Audio/Video: Playback bug for the seek handling, and make it block this site report.

comment:
Thank you for the detailed report and the workaround.

**Analysis**

This looks like a timing problem in the PipeWire camera backend, not in the permission prompt. Comment 3 shows that the prompt stops the preview about 2 ms before the page's capture starts. In [video_capture_pipewire.cc](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/third_party/libwebrtc/modules/video_capture/linux/video_capture_pipewire.cc#257), `VideoCaptureModulePipeWire::StopCapture()` calls `pw_stream_destroy()` and returns at once. It does not disconnect the stream or wait for PipeWire to release the camera. [CamerasParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/dom/media/systemservices/CamerasParent.cpp#1575) then creates a new capture module and a new PipeWire stream for the page. On a camera that allows only one client, the new stream gets EBUSY (-16) during link negotiation.

This explains the observations. With `permissions.default.camera = 1`, no preview runs before the page's stream, so the camera is free. "Hide preview" before *Allow*, or a reload with a remembered decision, gives the camera time to release. [MediaManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/dom/media/MediaManager.cpp#4494) tries the start again once after 200 ms, which gives the two `StartCapture failed` lines. The problem occurs only on Linux with `media.webrtc.camera.allow-pipewire` set to `true`. That pref is `false` by default.

One point is still open. `StartCapture()` fails at once only when `pw_stream_new()` or `pw_stream_connect()` fails. The EBUSY in the journal comes from the PipeWire server during negotiation, which is later. `OnStreamStateChanged` in [video_capture_pipewire.cc](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/third_party/libwebrtc/modules/video_capture/linux/video_capture_pipewire.cc#410) only logs `PW_STREAM_STATE_ERROR`. So the code does not show how this error becomes the `NotReadableError`.

The probable fix direction has two parts. In `StopCapture()`, disconnect the stream and wait for the `UNCONNECTED` state before `pw_stream_destroy()`. Also send `PW_STREAM_STATE_ERROR` to the caller, so that a busy camera fails clearly. The change belongs in upstream libwebrtc first, then in a backport.

**Next steps**

The code at fault is the libwebrtc PipeWire capture code and CamerasParent, which the WebRTC team owns. This moves the bug to Core :: WebRTC: Audio/Video. It is not known yet whether this is a regression. Andreas, could you please look at this bug?

The V4L2 device choice in the attachment is a separate problem: Firefox picks a raw IPU6 node first. We recommend a new bug for it.
title: getUserMedia fails with NotReadableError after granting permission when the camera serves a single client (Intel IPU6 / libcamera via PipeWire) — the permission doorhanger's preview keeps the device busy

comment:
This looks like a focus problem in the notification bar code, not in the media code. Moving to Toolkit :: UI Widgets.

**Analysis**

The "Enable DRM" button callback is in [EncryptedMediaParent.sys.mjs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/browser/actors/EncryptedMediaParent.sys.mjs#95). It turns on the DRM prefs and reloads the tab. Then the bar closes.

When a bar that has focus closes, `_removeNotificationElement()` in [notificationbox.js](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/toolkit/content/widgets/notificationbox.js#300) calls `Services.focus.moveFocus()` with `MOVEFOCUS_FORWARD`. This moves focus into the page as if the user pressed Tab. The content process focuses the first tab stop of the page with `FLAG_BYKEY`, so that element matches `:focus-visible`. On Amazon, the first tab stop is the "Skip to: Main content" link. The site opens its keyboard shortcuts panel when that link gets focus. The screenshot shows a focus ring on "Main content" and no bar, which agrees with this.

This also explains the platforms. On Windows and Linux, a mouse click focuses the bar button. On macOS, a mouse click does not focus the button ([nsXULElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/dom/xul/nsXULElement.cpp#336)), so `moveFocus()` does not run. The reload then removes the panel, so it shows only for a moment. This cause is probable: it comes from code reading, not from a log.

This is not a known regression. The `moveFocus()` call is old, and the problem also reproduces on Firefox 159.

**Next steps**

Hanna, could you please look at this bug? We suggest that `notificationbox.js` gives focus back to the tab's `<browser>` when a focused bar closes, in place of a forward focus move. This change fixes every bar whose button closes it. A smaller fix is to focus the browser in the EME button callback before the bar closes.

comment:
Thank you for the sample file. The cause is in the HEVC SPS parser, as comment 1 says.

**Analysis**

The attached file has a 2560x1920 picture in 4:2:0. Its SPS has no conformance window, and its VUI has no aspect ratio. The VUI has a default display window with all four offsets set to 1.

`H265::ParseVuiParameters` in [H265.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H265.cpp#807) multiplies the window offsets to get `mDisplayWidth` and `mDisplayHeight`. For this file, the result is 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 on each axis. The range checks accept 2, so `H265SPS::GetDisplaySize()` returns 2x2. Most files work only because one offset is 0, and then the code uses the image size.

The MP4 demuxer and the HEVC `MediaChangeMonitor` read the display size from the `hvcC` data, not from the decoder. This is why the result is the same with and without hardware decoding. The decoded picture is correct at 2560x1920, but Firefox draws it at a 1:1 display size.

A second error is in the conformance window crop at [H265.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H265.cpp#300). The code subtracts `subWidthC * (right - left)`, but the crop must subtract the sum of the left and right offsets. This error does not affect the attached file. The crop code came with bug 1917874. The display window code dates from bug 1849392, the first version of the parser, so this is not a regression.

**Next steps**

The fix is in the default display window branch of `H265::ParseVuiParameters`. One option is to ignore the default display window, so `GetDisplaySize()` returns the cropped image size. The other option is to subtract `subWidthC` times the sum of the offsets from the picture size, which gives 2556x1916 here. The same patch can correct the sign in the conformance window crop.

A gtest in [TestByteStreams.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/ff3b300c151f45f09f300284659f24f5d95b0f25/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/gtest/TestByteStreams.cpp), beside `TEST(H265, ConfWindowTest)`, can use the SPS from the attached file. It can expect a 2560x1920 display size.
title: HEVC: incorrectly computed video width and height

comment:
Thank you for the reports. The drift after a change from 2x back to 1x also occurs in bug 2007762, on Linux and on Windows 11. That bug has the same probable cause as this bug.

**Analysis**

The bug 1955841 change, in Firefox 157, calls SoundTouch `flush()` on each switch from a non-1x rate back to 1x, in [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#719). `AudioStream` keeps the same time stretcher and never calls `clear()`. `flush()` adds silence, and this silence also increases `samplesExpectedOut` in [SoundTouch.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/media/libsoundtouch/src/SoundTouch.cpp#290). Only `clear()` resets that counter. Thus each switch to 1x adds more silence than the one before.

The audio clock counts this silence as media time. Thus the clock moves ahead of the audio that you hear, and the audio lags the video. A change between two rates that are not 1x does not call `flush()`. This is the probable cause, from the code only. No log confirms it yet.

A seek can keep the audio stream and its time stretcher. On Nightly, and on macOS on all channels, `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` is on, in [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#725). Then the seek removes the current lag, but the counter stays. The next switch to 1x adds the old silence back. This agrees with comment 6, on Nightly 161, where a seek reduces the drift but does not remove it.

**Open points**

Comment 0 says that the lag also occurs on any video, without a rate change. At a constant 1x, `AudioStream` makes no time stretcher, so this cause does not explain that case. Comment 0 uses Firefox 156, which is before the bug 1955841 change. Thus the cause of a lag with no rate change is not known.

The triage tools could not read the profiles in comment 4 and comment 5. The profile format is newer than the tools. This is a gap in our tools, not a problem with the captures. The media profile in comment 5 can confirm the cause.

A probable fix direction: keep the flushed output in a buffer, then call `clear()` on the time stretcher at each switch to 1x. Also reset the time stretcher when a seek reuses the stream. A gtest can check for inserted silence after repeated rate switches.

Paul has an open request from comment 3 to look at this bug. This bug blocks bug 1904915, the YouTube playback meta bug.
title: Audio and video desync in youtube

comment:
Thanks for the clear A/B/A test and the log excerpts.

**Analysis**

The cause in comment 0 is correct. `NvidiaDrmModesetDisabled()` in [FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/platforms/ffmpeg/FFmpegVulkanVideoDecoder.cpp) sets the result to "disabled" first. It clears it only when `fopen()` on `/sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset` succeeds. The function does not read `errno`, so a missing module (ENOENT) and a root-only file (EACCES) give the same result.

`SelectVulkanDecoderPhysicalDevice()` then skips every device with vendor 0x10de. The attached log shows this in the RDD process: the "Skipping NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070" line, then `IsHardwareAccelerated=false`. A `std::call_once` keeps the result for the life of the process, so only a full restart changes it. The check runs before any codec choice, so the problem is not specific to H.264.

The sandbox does not cause this. The RDD broker policy allows this file read-only. The broker opens it as the user and gets EACCES from the 0400 permission, as `cat` does. The 0444 run proves that the policy allows the read.

This is a regression from bug 2071303, which changed the default to "disabled". It landed on 2026-10-19, in Nightly 161. Drivers before 615.71.09 keep the 0400 permission, so most current installs are affected.

**Fix direction**

1. Save `errno` when `fopen()` fails. Treat only ENOENT (and ENOTDIR) as "module not loaded".
2. For EACCES or another error, keep the device and log a separate message with the error.
3. Optionally, when the file cannot be read, use the `VK_EXT_physical_device_drm` data that device selection already queries.

One trade-off: with step 2, a 0400 driver with modeset set to `N` keeps NVIDIA selectable, as before bug 2071303. CI has no NVIDIA hardware. A GTest can cover the logic if it moves into a pure helper that maps the error and the first byte to a result.

Tymur already has a needinfo as the author of bug 2071303 (comment 2). This bug blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

**Workaround**

1. Run `sudo chmod 0444 /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset`.
2. Restart Firefox fully.

comment:
This crash shows a seek that reaches a new `MediaDecoderStateMachine` while it still reads metadata. The cause below is probable. It comes from code reading, and no log proves it yet.

**Analysis**

- In the last 30 days, all 57 crash reports are on Windows, in the content process. 42 are on DevEdition, 14 on Nightly and 1 on Beta. Release builds do not crash, because `HandleSeek` uses `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_CRASH` ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#320)). On Release, the seek is probably rejected and lost.
- `MediaDecoder::SwitchStateMachine` ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#401)) replaces the external engine state machine with a new `MediaDecoderStateMachine` in `DecodeMetadataState`. Two callers do this: `OnPlaybackErrorEvent` after an engine error, and `SetCDMProxy` when the external engine rejects a non-WMF CDM such as Widevine.
- The switch does not reset the element's readyState and does not block new seeks. `HTMLMediaElement::Seek` refuses only at `HAVE_NOTHING`. `MediaDecoder::CallSeek` checks only `mShouldDelaySeek`, the bfcache flag.
- `mMediaSeekable` is `true` by default until `OnMetadataRead`. So `MediaDecoderStateMachine::Seek` sends the seek to `DecodeMetadataState::HandleSeek`, which crashes by design.
- The switch is dangerous only after the element has metadata. Encrypted MSE with a Widevine `setMediaKeys`, and engine errors after metadata, fit this. Clear MSE falls back before metadata, so it does not crash.

Bug 1402584 fixed the same problem for the `<source>` fallback with a readyState reset. `SwitchStateMachine` does not go through that reset. Bug 1844478 had a tail of this signature and closed when the crashes stopped, with no new guard.

The crash report does not show that the fallback ran. It has no external engine annotation and no URL. A `GMPThread` exists, which can point to Widevine EME. No non-WMF path to this crash was found, so this cause does not explain the reports from before the external engine existed.

**Fix direction**

While `mPendingStatusUpdateForNewlyCreatedStateMachine` is set, `MediaDecoder::CallSeek` can skip `InvokeSeek`. `MediaDecoder::Seek` already stores `mLogicalPosition`. Then `SetStatusUpdateForNewlyCreatedStateMachineIfNeeded` can replay the seek after the new metadata. The replay should keep the original seek type. The bfcache delayed seek needs a check too.

Regression status: not known. No bisection exists. The late switch exists since bug 1756260 (2022), and bug 1833266 (2023) added the `SetCDMProxy` switch.

**Next steps**

Alastor, could you please review this analysis of the external engine fallback? A log with `MOZ_LOG=MediaDecoder:5,MediaDecoderStateMachine:5,EESM:5` can confirm the order of the switch, the seek and the new metadata. The needinfo from Clouseau on Jim stays open.
title: Crash in [@ mozilla::MediaDecoderStateMachine::DecodeMetadataState::HandleSeek]

comment:
**Analysis**

The error text hides the real decoder error. The code shows the cause of this.

1. `RemoteDecoderModule::Supports` does not reject clear content at the `UtilityProcess_MFMediaEngineCDM` location when the stream has no media engine id ([RemoteDecoderModule.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/ipc/RemoteDecoderModule.cpp#61)). The CDM process then always rejects the decoder with "only support for media engine playback" ([RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/ipc/RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp#443)). `SupportsAsync` already skips this location when there is no media engine id (bug 2082265). The sync `Supports` does not.
2. `PDMFactory::CheckAndMaybeCreateDecoder` keeps only the newest error ([PDMFactory.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/platforms/PDMFactory.cpp#376)). With the default Windows prefs, the CDM module is the last module that Firefox tries ([PDMFactory.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/platforms/PDMFactory.cpp#744)). So its error replaces the earlier, real error, for example a WMF HEVC error.

Bug 2043087 comment 14 shows the same problem for MSE. There, `media.wmf.media-engine.enabled=0` shows the real error "Use VP8/VP9/AV1 MFT only if HW acceleration is available".

The "file is corrupt" text has a separate cause. `HTMLMediaElement::DecodeError` picks the error code from `readyState`, not from the decoder error. The decoder fails after `loadedmetadata`, so the page gets `MEDIA_ERR_DECODE`. The video controls show this code as "file is corrupt".

**Fix direction**

In `RemoteDecoderModule::Supports`, return an empty set for the `UtilityProcess_MFMediaEngineCDM` location when `aParams.mMediaEngineId` is not set. This copies the check in `SupportsAsync`. Then the page gets the real WMF error, or "Error no decoder found". Before the change, make sure that `canPlayType` results for clear HEVC stay the same when `media.wmf.media-engine.enabled` is 1 or 3. A gtest on `Supports` with no media engine id can show the fix.

**Still open**

The reason that HEVC decoding fails on this computer is not known. Possible causes are a missing HEVC Video Extension, or no hardware decoding for this stream. The bug still waits for the media profile and the `about:support` text that comment 1 asks for.

**Analysis**

The cause is not known yet. The bug occurs on macOS and Linux, so a platform decoder is not a probable cause. A Shift+reload sets `LOAD_BYPASS_CACHE` and `LOAD_BYPASS_SERVICE_WORKER` for the page and its subresources ([nsDocShellLoadState.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/docshell/base/nsDocShellLoadState.cpp#1526)). A normal reload revalidates only the top-level document. MSE gets the same bytes in both cases. Thus the difference between the two reloads points first at the HTTP cache or a Service Worker, not at dom/media.

The hls.js `onWorkerError` path means that the transmux worker sent an `error` event. Gecko sends a plain `Event` with no message when the worker script fails to load. It sends an `ErrorEvent` with a message when the script throws.

**Next steps**

1. Could you please check if the same steps break playback in Firefox Release or Beta?
2. Could you please unregister the `app.slack.com` entry in `about:serviceworkers`, and then try a normal reload again?

comment:
This bug also waits for the open needinfo to Jim Mathies in comment 92, which asks for an owner.

**Analysis**

In the last 7 days, Treeherder lists 23 failures of this test. All of them are on Android: 22 on android-em-14-x86_64 emulators and 1 on an android-hw-a55 device. They occur on mozilla-central, autoland, mozilla-beta and try. Monthly Treeherder totals from July to October 2026 are steady, with no step change. So we found no regressor.

We read two logs: tasks dvj7m3dWSFmkoAPiicIUyA (emulator) and Tj7YwxE6RwmPaOcD0G4hww (a55). In both, all steps before the last step pass. The last step appends three AAC audio segments, calls `endOfStream()` and `play()`, then waits for `ended` ([test_ExperimentalAsync.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/mediasource/test/test_ExperimentalAsync.html#87)). The `ended` event does not come in about 300 seconds, for 2.9 seconds of media. The logs show no media error and no crash.

In the same emulator run, sub-test 25 of test_eme_waitingforkey.html (WebM Vorbis and VP9 with Clear Key) also hangs before `ended` after `endOfStream()`. This points to an Android problem in the end-of-stream path, and not to a problem in this test only.

**Probable causes**

These come from code reading only. No log proves them yet.

1. The cubeb AAudio drain. After the last data, the state thread waits until the frames read reach `drain_target`, and only then sends `CUBEB_STATE_DRAINED` ([cubeb_aaudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_aaudio.cpp#635)). This wait has no deadline. If the device read counter stops, the audio sink never completes and `MediaDecoderStateMachine` never fires `ended`. This cause also explains the Vorbis hang.
2. The Android audio decoder does not complete its drain at end of stream. This cause does not explain the Vorbis hang as well, but the data does not rule it out.

**Next steps**

John, could you please look at this Android failure? These steps can show which stage stalls:

1. Read the logcat artifacts of the two tasks above, near the time of the timeout.
2. Look for repeated "Output stream DRAINING. Remaining frames" lines and for MediaCodec errors.
3. In the last step of the test, log the `seeked`, `playing`, `timeupdate` and `error` events.
4. On timeout, dump `mozRequestDebugInfo()` to get the decoder name and the state machine state.
5. If necessary, run the test with `MOZ_LOG=MediaDecoder:4,MediaFormatReader:5,AudioSink:5,AudioStream:5,cubeb:5`.

comment:
Thank you for the clear test page and the JSON results.

**Analysis**

The cause is a rate check in `OpusTrackEncoder::Init`. It rejects a track rate above 192000 Hz with `NS_ERROR_INVALID_ARG` ([OpusTrackEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/encoder/OpusTrackEncoder.cpp#159)). Opus is the only audio encoder for MediaRecorder, so every audio recording goes through this check. But `AudioContext` accepts rates up to `WebAudioUtils::MaxSampleRate`, which is 768000 ([WebAudioUtils.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/webaudio/WebAudioUtils.h#35)).

The encoder uses the graph rate of the track. A getUserMedia track runs at the preferred output rate from CubebUtils, not at the microphone rate. With a 384000 Hz output device, the microphone track is also at 384000 Hz. This explains why `media.cubeb.force_sample_rate` set to 48000 fixes the microphone case. It also explains why an explicit 384000 Hz `AudioContext` still fails with that pref.

The init failure goes to `TrackEncoder::TryInit`, which calls `OnError()` and drops the nsresult ([TrackEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/encoder/TrackEncoder.cpp#208)). MediaRecorder then fires the generic UnknownError ([MediaRecorder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/MediaRecorder.cpp#2025)). This gives the start, error, empty dataavailable and stop order in the attached results.

This is not a regression: the 192000 Hz limit is old, and 158.0.1 and 159.0 both fail. The code is in `dom/media/encoder`, so this bug moves to Audio/Video: Recording.

**Fix direction**

1. Raise the limit in `OpusTrackEncoder::Init` to `WebAudioUtils::MaxSampleRate`, or remove it.
2. In the same change, size the `pcm` buffer in `OpusTrackEncoder::Encode` for the input frames per packet.

Caution: step 2 is necessary. The buffer now has the 48 kHz output size, and the interleave writes input-rate frames ([OpusTrackEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/encoder/OpusTrackEncoder.cpp#284)). At 384000 Hz stereo, the write is larger than the inline storage. The `frameToCopy <= 3844` assert also assumes the 192000 Hz limit.

A gtest in `TestAudioTrackEncoder.cpp` can encode at 384000 Hz. A mochitest like [test_mediarecorder_record_audiocontext.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/test/test_mediarecorder_record_audiocontext.html) with `new AudioContext({sampleRate: 384000})` needs no special hardware. A follow-up can pass the nsresult through `OnError()`, so that an unsupported setup gives a clear error.

Paul, could you please look at this bug and confirm the fix direction?
title: MediaRecorder fails with UnknownError on 384 kHz audio streams, breaking microphone dictation with high-rate default output

comment:
Thanks for the profiles. The fix in bug 1955841 does not cover this case. The audio lag still grows with each change from 2x back to 1x.

**Analysis**

The Media profile in comment 5 shows the problem clearly. It comes from Zen 158 on Linux, which uses Gecko 158 and has the bug 1955841 change. The video is AV1 and the audio is Opus, through `AudioSink` with one `AudioStream` for the whole capture. The capture has 17 changes from 2x to 1x, no seek and no underrun.

The audio that `PopFrames` gives falls behind the media clock by about 1.7 s at the end. At steady 1x, the gap stays flat. After each return to 1x, some audio callbacks in `GetUnprocessed` give audio with no `PopFrames` call. This audio comes from the time stretcher. The number of these callbacks grows with each cycle, from 1 to 10. The profile in comment 4 has no media threads, so it cannot show the cause.

**Probable cause**

In [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#710), `UpdatePlaybackRateIfNeeded()` calls `mTimeStretcher->flush()` at the change from 2x to 1x. [SoundTouch.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/media/libsoundtouch/src/SoundTouch.cpp#318) `flush()` adds blocks of silence until the output reaches its target. Each silence block also increases the count of expected output in `putSamples()`, so a debt stays in the counters. Only `clear()` or a new stretcher resets these counters. Bug 1955841 keeps the same stretcher alive, so the debt carries over and grows each cycle. `GetUnprocessed()` then gives this extra audio, and `UpdateFrameHistory()` counts it as media time.

Thus the clock and the video move ahead of the audio. This cause is probable. It comes from code reading, and the profile numbers agree with it. It explains why the lag grows only at rate changes and why it grows more on each cycle. A seek in Nightly can keep the same stream when `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` is on. Then the stretcher keeps its debt, and this can explain why a seek only partly helps (comment 6).

**Fix direction**

After `GetUnprocessed()` drains the flushed output, call `clear()` on the stretcher and prime it again. Also count the drained tail at the old rate, and reset the stretcher in `AudioSink::RebaseLive()`. `AudioDecoderInputTrack.cpp` uses the same `flush()` pattern and can need the same check. A test that changes the rate many times and compares the audio clock with the frames that `PopFrames` gives can confirm the cause.

This bug blocks bug 1904915 (YouTube playback). The bug also waits for Paul's answer to the needinfo from comment 3.
title: Audio and video desync in youtube

comment:
Thanks for the new captures and the detailed reports.

**Analysis**

Two Windows profiles show the same pattern: the HEVC hardware decoder is fast, and the frames drop in the playback state machine. The profiles are https://share.firefox.dev/4w3HsRD (comment 9) and https://share.firefox.dev/44Ucu4i (comment 7). Both use the "wmf HEVC codec hardware video decoder" in the GPU process. Each video request resolves in about 1 ms. The profiles show no DXVA slot errors and no decode errors, and the compositor stalls do not match the drops.

In the comment 9 profile, some decoded frames have a very long duration, for example 517 ms instead of 16 to 67 ms. The stream has a variable frame rate and deep frame reordering. After each long frame, MediaDecoderStateMachine sends no `RequestData:V` for the length of that frame. When the requests start again, the frames are already late, and 58 `VideoSinkDroppedFrame` markers follow in bursts. The comment 7 profile shows the same gaps of about 540 ms before each burst of late frames.

The probable cause is a wrong frame duration that spans the reordered frames. MediaDecoderStateMachine then decides that it has enough video and stops the requests. The code to check is the output duration in [WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp) and the video request scheduling in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp). Comment 0 also shows the drops on Linux with software decoding. Thus the wrong duration can come from code that the WMF and FFmpeg paths share, such as the sample timestamps from the demuxer. A check of the sample durations for one of the comment 8 videos can confirm the cause.

With `media.hevc.enabled` set to false, TikTok serves H.264 and playback is clean. Nobody tested H.264 content with the same frame reordering.

Our profile reader did not finish https://share.firefox.dev/3U6ZmSG (comment 8) or the three Linux profiles of comment 0 and comment 4. These profiles are not analyzed here.

Bug 1894818 is in the Regressed by field, but that change adds HEVC on Linux. Comments 7 to 11 reproduce on Windows, so that change does not explain the Windows drops.

This bug now also blocks bug 1416090, the meta bug for dropped video frames. The bug also waits for the open needinfo requests to Alastor (comment 8) and Jim (comment 9).
title: h265/hevc videos on TikTok drop a lot of frames

comment:
Thanks for the profiles and the measurements. Five of the six media profiles show the same pattern. This is true on Linux (VA-API and software FFmpeg) and on Windows (WMF hardware decode).

**Analysis**

The decoders are not slow. Each HEVC frame decodes in about 1 ms, and the compositor is not the source of the drops.

Some HEVC samples come out of the MP4 demuxer with a very long duration, from 133 ms to 567 ms. A normal frame is 16.7 ms or 33.3 ms. For example, the Linux profile in comment 0 has `ProcessDecode: mDuration=533333µs`, and the Windows profile in comment 7 has `sample=13166666, duration=533333`. A long sample comes about once per group of pictures, at the same media times on each loop of a video. All decoders copy this duration to the output frame unchanged.

One long frame causes a freeze and then a burst of drops:

1. [VideoSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/mediasink/VideoSink.cpp#551) keeps the long frame on screen until the clock passes its end time. This is the still image.
2. [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3577) `HaveEnoughDecodedVideo` counts frames, not time. The queue stays full, so no new video request goes out for about 0.5 s.
3. When the long frame expires, 10 to 15 frames decode in a few ms. They are already late, and VideoSink drops them.

The probable cause is in `Moof::Moof` in [MoofParser.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/mp4/MoofParser.cpp#485). It sorts the samples of one moof by composition time and sets the end of each sample to the start of the next one. Samples in the next moof are not part of this step. So when the next moof fills a hole in the composition times, the sample before the hole gets the full hole as its duration. Nothing limits the result to the trun `sample_duration`.

A second possible source is a large trun `sample_duration` on the last sample of a moof, see [MoofParser.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/mp4/MoofParser.cpp#1014). The profiles do not show which of the two sources applies. The parser code is the same for all codecs, so the difference is probably in the HEVC encodes that TikTok serves. This can also explain why only some videos fail and why the logged-out feed in comment 9 was clean.

The "Disable zero copy by using too many video frames" entry in comment 11 is probably a result of the burst, not the cause. This agrees with the test in comment 11, where zero copy off did not help.

Regression status: bug 1894818 is in the Regressed by field. It probably only exposed the problem on Linux, because TikTok can serve HEVC there since that change. The Windows reports use the WMF HEVC path, which does not depend on that change.

**Fix direction**

- In `Moof::Moof`, do not extend a sample to the next composition time when the gap is much larger than its trun `sample_duration`. This covers the first source only.
- A wider option is to expire the front frame in VideoSink when the clock reaches the start time of the next frame. This covers both sources, but A/V sync depends on that code.
- A gtest beside [TestParser.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b0625683b9b8cd108f6b3fa9eedbcd4aa0066d6e/dom/media/gtest/mp4_demuxer/TestParser.cpp) can show the parser problem with a crafted fMP4 of two moofs.
- To find which source applies, dump the trun entries of one affected HEVC segment from TikTok.

This bug now also blocks bug 1416090, the meta bug for dropped video frames. The open needinfo requests to Alastor (comment 8) and Jim (comment 9) stay.
title: h265/hevc videos on TikTok drop a lot of frames

comment:
This is a regression in Firefox 154 from bug 2049615. The cause is confirmed in the current tree. Marcus works on a fix (comment 5), based on the Hackbot patch D321849 (comment 3).

**Analysis**

On macOS, `MP4TrackDemuxer::GetNextSample()` replaces the container sync flag of each HEVC sample with the result of `H265::IsKeyFrame()` ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#480)). That function uses `H265NALU::IsIframe()`, which accepts only `IDR_W_RADL` and `IDR_N_LP` ([H265.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H265.h#113)). As a result, a CRA or BLA picture is not a random access point.

MSE demuxes appended `video/mp4` data through the same `MP4Demuxer`. In `TrackBuffersManager::ProcessFrames()`, the need random access point flag stays true, so the code skips every sample of the segment ([TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2038)). The only trace is a verbose `MediaSourceSamples` log line and a profiler marker. This explains rows B and C of the testcase and the BLA relabel row. Windows builds do not have the override, so Firefox on Windows plays the stream (comment 5).

The fix direction in D321849 and in comment 5 agrees with the code. `H265NALU::IsIRAP()` and `H265::IsRandomAccessPoint()` already exist ([H265.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H265.cpp#1823)). Bug 2006226 added them after D321849 was posted, so the rework in comment 5 can use them.

- `MatroskaDemuxer` has the same IDR-only rule for HEVC under `MOZ_APPLEMEDIA` ([MatroskaDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webm/MatroskaDemuxer.cpp#217)). Comment 5 does not name it.

comment:
Clouseau's open check now has an answer. Reports 77398351 and b327f398 both carry the `WindowsErrorReporting` annotation. So they reached crash-stats through the WER path that bug 2081421 fixed. This supports the idea that the crash existed before and only became visible now.

**Analysis**

- 27 crashes with `mfx_media_merit` in the signature, all on Nightly, all in the GPU process. 26 are on builds 20261029212358 and 20261030090406. One is on 159.0a1 (2026-10-02). Crash-stats shows none on Beta or Release.
- The GPUs are Intel Raptor Lake (0xA7A0, 0xA7AB), with drivers from 32.0.101.6647 to 32.0.101.7092. The blocklist from bug 2048390 in [GfxInfo.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/widget/windows/GfxInfo.cpp#1510) blocks only Ivy Bridge and older, so it does not cover these devices.
- In both reports, two GPU process threads are inside Intel encoder MFT code at the same time. "BackgroundThreadPool #2" runs the codec support probe from `RecvUpdateVar` in [GPUParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/gfx/ipc/GPUParent.cpp#516). That probe calls `CanCreateWMFEncoder` and `MFTEncoder::Create` for each codec. "MediaPEncoder #1" initializes a real encoder.
- In b327f398, the fault comes from `ActivateObject` in [MFTEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/platforms/wmf/MFTEncoder.cpp#522), through `MFGetMFTMerit` and `COPMDevice::Open`.
- `PEMFactory::sSupportedMutex` only stops two probes from running together. Nothing serializes `MFTEncoder::Create` between the probe and a real encoder.

The probable cause is concurrent activation of Intel hardware encoder MFTs, which the Intel DLL does not handle. This is probable only: the DLL is closed source, and no test shows the race. The probable source of the second encoder is the gfx sanity test from bug 2067454. After each update, this test encodes one H.264 frame with hardware preference. A WebCodecs or WebRTC page restored at startup can also be the source.

**Fix direction**

- Serialize `EnumEncoders` and `ActivateObject` in `MFTEncoder::Create` with one process-wide lock.
- Re-probe encoders in `RecvUpdateVar` only when an encoder-related gfxVar changes.
- If the crash continues after this, block `FEATURE_HARDWARE_VIDEO_ENCODING` for the affected Intel devices or drivers.

Later Nightly crash data can confirm the cause. Check whether all 27 reports show two threads in Intel MFT code. Also check whether the parent process report carries the sanity test annotation.

Andrew, could you please look at this crash? You wrote the hardware encoder blocklist and the encoder sanity test. The regression status is not known yet. Gabriele still has the open request from comment 0.

comment:
Thank you for the report and the patches.

**Analysis**

The current tree confirms the cause. In `CreateDecoderAgent`, the resolve and reject callbacks on the shutdown blocker promise capture `self = RefPtr{this}` ([DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#902)). `CreateEncoderAgent` does the same ([EncoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/EncoderTemplate.cpp#1318)). The `TicketBlocker` on the global AsyncShutdown barrier owns that promise ([MediaUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/systemservices/MediaUtils.cpp#141)). The promise resolves only at shutdown. It rejects only when `DestroyDecoderAgentIfAny` or `DestroyEncoderAgentIfAny` destroys the ticket, and these run only on reset(), close(), an error or a new configure().

In a worker, the `StrongWorkerRef` callback also captures `RefPtr{this}` ([DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#867), [EncoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/EncoderTemplate.cpp#1284)). The template keeps that worker ref in `mWorkerRef`, so the cycle collector cannot see this cycle. The worker ref releases the callback only when the worker shuts down. The cycle collection macros of the four classes traverse only the JS callbacks.

This cause explains each observation in the report. It applies to all four classes, on the main thread and in a worker. The platform decoder or encoder stays allocated until shutdown, so the leak checks in CI do not find it. This is not a regression: the strong captures come from the first landing of each template.

**Fix direction**

The attached Part 1 follows the correct direction. The callbacks capture a `WeakPtr`, and a new destructor calls the `Destroy*AgentIfAny()` function. The destructor is necessary: it destroys the ticket, which rejects the promise and releases the `ref` captures. Part 2 can show the fix on every platform, because VP8 and Opus use software codecs. Part 1 applies to the current tree with a small line offset.

Bug 2026835 changes the same template code for the close() case. This bug blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

**Next steps**

Nicola is working on a fix (comment 1 and comment 2). The [contributor quick reference](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/contributing/contribution_quickref.html) shows how to submit patches to Phabricator with moz-phab.

The open design question is the WPT timeout on the Android emulator after the fix. Firefox has no codec reclamation code in dom/media/webcodecs today. C.M. Chang, could you please answer the question in comment 0? The question is whether to work toward codec reclamation or to keep the emulator limit as an expected failure.

comment:
**Analysis**

The probable cause is bug 2025515, in the bugmon range. It added `MediaStreamRenderer::UpdateVideoTrackListeners` in [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#1174) with this assertion. It landed on autoland on 2026-04-09. The other dom/media changes in the range are in Web Audio, and the testcase does not use Web Audio.

`UpdateVideoTrackListeners` has no case for a first-frame `VideoOutput` in the `Detaching` state. The first block attaches `mFirstFrameVideoOutput` only when it is `Detached`. The third block asserts that it is `Attached` before it creates `mVideoOutput`. A `Detaching` output passes neither check. The method already waits while `mVideoOutput` is `Detaching`, but it does not wait for the first-frame output.

The testcase gets to this state as follows:

1. After the `getStats()` yield, the first-frame output is `Attached` to `track`.
2. `track.stop()` removes the track synchronously. `VideoStreamTrack::RemoveVideoOutput` sets the first-frame output to `Detaching`.
3. Only the graph sets `Detached`, later, through `VideoOutput::NotifyRemoved` in [VideoOutput.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/VideoOutput.h#170).
4. `play()` and `addTrack()` select the live clone. Then the WatchManager task runs and the assertion fails.

In release builds, this is probably a short visual glitch and not a crash. The new `mVideoOutput` shares `mVideoContainer` with the first-frame output, which is still detaching. When that output becomes `Detached`, it attaches after the main output, and its single frame can briefly replace newer frames. All objects are reference counted. This is from code reading; nothing was run.

**Fix direction**

In `UpdateVideoTrackListeners`, return early while `mFirstFrameVideoOutput` is `Detaching`. The method already watches `mFirstFrameVideoOutput->mAttachment`, so it runs again when the state becomes `Detached`. Then it attaches the first-frame output first and creates `mVideoOutput` after it. A change to the assertion alone is not sufficient, because the assertion on the attach order then fails later. The testcase is deterministic in debug builds, so a crashtest can cover the fix.

**Next steps**

Andreas, could you please confirm this fix direction? Could you please also confirm that the new order does not bring back the cross-graph problem of bug 2025515?

comment:
Thank you for the report and the patches.

**Analysis**

The current tree shows the problem in both templates. In [DecoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/DecoderTemplate.cpp#352), `OutputDecodedData` has only a `MOZ_ASSERT` on the state and no check at runtime. Its loop calls the output callback for each frame of the batch, also after the callback itself calls `reset()`. `ResetInternal` keeps no reset counter. Also, `configure()` sets the state back to Configured at once, so a state check cannot detect `reset()` followed by `configure()`.

In [EncoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/EncoderTemplate.cpp#387), the output loop only checks `mActiveConfig`. `reset()` clears `mActiveConfig`, but `configure()` sets it again at once. Thus the remaining outputs of the batch pass the check. This probably explains the 19 stale packets in the Part 2 test, if the encoder returns all 20 packets in one batch.

The WebCodecs algorithm text is not clear on this point. The open spec issue [w3c/webcodecs#755](https://github.com/w3c/webcodecs/issues/755) discusses it, and the code comment in EncoderTemplate.cpp says that the editors agreed that no output comes after a reset. The WPT subtest "Verify reset() suppresses outputs" also expects this. It fails on Linux with openh264, as [videoDecoder-codec-specific.https.any.js.ini](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/testing/web-platform/meta/webcodecs/videoDecoder-codec-specific.https.any.js.ini#127) shows.

Part 1 (attachment 9671633) adds a reset counter. Each output task captures the counter, and the task checks it before the output loop and after each callback. This addresses the cause in both templates. One path is still open: the "Destroy + recreate encoder" task in `DrainAndReconfigure` checks only `mState` ([EncoderTemplate.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/86136a5faf970e59063cd07b822717f6fd03a958/dom/media/webcodecs/EncoderTemplate.cpp#746)). After `reset()` and `configure()` in an output callback, this task can destroy the new encoder and configure it again with the old configuration. The same counter check can protect this task.

Part 1 applies on top of the patches of bug 2087195. It also changes the same function as the patch of bug 2026835, so one of the two patches needs a rebase. This bug blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

**Next steps**

Phabricator is the usual path for review. The page [How to submit a patch](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/contributing/how_to_submit_a_patch.html) shows how to submit with `moz-phab`.

comment:
This is a shutdown race in the tab process, in [RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/9fcf3a1690ecec7078bc93cd2048d6447247f582/dom/media/ipc/RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp). Bugs 1674404, 1786806 and 1857154 reported the same failure under the old name `RemoteDecoderManagerChild`. All three closed with no fix.

**Analysis**

- `DeallocateSurfaceDescriptor` calls `GetManagerThread()`, which copies the thread pointer and releases the lock. Then it calls `Dispatch` inside `MOZ_ALWAYS_SUCCEEDS`.
- At xpcom-shutdown, `RemoteMediaManagerChild::Shutdown()` clears the static pointer under the lock. Then it shuts down the manager thread. After that, `Dispatch` returns `NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED`.
- `ShutdownXPCOM` fires xpcom-shutdown before `ShutdownLayersIPC`, so the ImageBridgeChild thread is still active. A late `PTexture` destroy calls `GPUVideoTextureData::Deallocate` on that thread.
- If that thread copies the pointer just before `Shutdown()` clears it, the dispatch goes to a thread that no longer accepts events. Then the check crashes.
- The log agrees with this. The tab process logs "GetUserData call for port ... failed" at the time of the crash, which shows that its IPC ports already close. The test passes, and the job fails only on the minidump.

**Impact**

`MOZ_ALWAYS_TRUE` uses `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_CRASH`, which does nothing in release builds. Tab processes run full XPCOM shutdown only when `NS_FREE_PERMANENT_DATA` is defined, for example in debug, ASan and TSan builds. Other builds exit fast and do not reach this path. The lost runnable sends nothing anyway, because every manager is already closed and `CanSend()` is false. The message changed from "Assertion failure" to "Hit MOZ_CRASH" because bug 1931877 changed the macro text. The same builds crash as before.

**Fix direction**

The fix stays in RemoteMediaManagerChild.cpp. The same pattern is also in `OnSetCurrent` and `DeallocShmem`.

1. Preferred: add a helper that holds the `sRemoteMediaManagerChildThread` lock across the null check and the `Dispatch`. `Shutdown()` clears the pointer under the same lock before the thread shuts down, so a dispatch under the lock always reaches a live thread.
2. Smaller: dispatch with `NS_DISPATCH_FALLIBLE` and ignore the failure at shutdown.

A test cannot show this reliably, because the race window is very small.

comment:
This intermittent timeout occurs only on Windows 11 25h2, on opt and shippable builds, 32 and 64 bit. Treeherder shows 43 failures from 2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01.

**Analysis**

The CI logs of tasks fTI_ZFdaQWaw-S-6rCPlaA and VPagsbOASCKUwLdGmOKNog show two hang points. In both, a synthesized key never reaches the popup document, and the test waits until the harness timeout. The retry in a new browser also fails, so earlier tests do not cause it. The logs show no JS error and no assertion.

- Pattern A: the hang is at the first key, CapsLock, in the first popup. The log has no "Received keydown event: CapsLock" line.
- Pattern B: all blocklisted keys and Space pass in the first popup. The hang is at Ctrl+F5 in the second popup, in `testCtrlF5Activation`. The log has no "Received keydown event: F5" line.

The probable cause is a focus race in the test. The opener waits only for the popup `load` event, then posts the message ([test_autoplay_policy_key_blacklist.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/autoplay/test/mochitest/test_autoplay_policy_key_blacklist.html#34)). It does not wait for the popup to get focus. The helper sends each key one time from a chrome script into `Services.wm.getMostRecentWindow("navigator:browser")` ([file_autoplay_policy_key_blacklist.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/autoplay/test/mochitest/file_autoplay_policy_key_blacklist.html#56)). The key goes to the focused element of that chrome window. If the content `<browser>` does not have focus yet, chrome gets the key and the one-shot `keydown` listener never fires.

The line "Unable to restore focus" after each timeout agrees with this. The popup stays open because `child.close()` never runs. No log proves where the key lands yet. A try run with `MOZ_LOG=Focus:5`, or an `info()` that logs the focused element of `browserWin` when the key is sent, can confirm it. Why only the Windows 11 workers show the race is not known. Bug 2012615 also shows focus failures on these workers.

Regression status: no change in Firefox code is known to cause this. No change to the test or the helper matches the start of the failures in November 2025. Bug 2001938 added the second popup and the Ctrl+F5 subtest, where Pattern B hangs.

**Fix direction**

The fix stays in the two test files under `dom/media/autoplay/test/mochitest/`:

1. In the opener, await `SimpleTest.promiseFocus(child)` after the `load` event.
2. Send each key to the popup window, not to `getMostRecentWindow`.
3. Focus the content `<browser>` of that window before each key.
4. Close the popup in a `SimpleTest.registerCleanupFunction`, so a failure does not affect later tests.

This bug blocks the autoplay meta bug 2023365. It also waits for the request to Jim Mathies in comment 102. Alastor, could you please look at this fix direction, because the test covers the autoplay policy?
title: High frequency dom/media/autoplay/test/mochitest/test_autoplay_policy_key_blacklist.html | single tracking bug

comment:
This shutdown hang is in the QuotaManager code, not in media code. The bug moves to Core :: Storage: Quota Manager, the owner of `dom/quota` in its `moz.build`. The `MozPromise` frame in the summary is only the runnable that runs `ShutdownStorageOp` on the `QuotaManager IO` thread.

**Analysis**

The `QuotaManager IO` thread waits in `fsync` from `nsFileStreamBase::Flush()`. The call chain is `ShutdownStorageOp::DoDirectoryWork`, `ShutdownStorageInternal`, `UnloadQuota`, `SettleDirectoryMetadata2`, then `CreateDirectoryMetadata2`. The crash is on Nightly 161, build 20261031095059, on Linux.

Bug 2068772 (fixed in 158) put the cache DB upserts of `UnloadQuota` into transactions of 50 origins. That change does not cover the `.metadata-v2` file write. In the current tree, `CreateDirectoryMetadata2` still calls `stream->Flush()` once for each dirty origin ([ActorsParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/quota/ActorsParent.cpp#3820)). The loop is in `UnloadQuota` ([ActorsParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/quota/ActorsParent.cpp#3365)). Thus the shutdown time still grows with the number of dirty origins and the disk `fsync` latency.

One crash report cannot show if one `fsync` stalled or if many dirty origins each paid for one. The idea list in bug 2068772 comment 0 (an async metadata flush, or a shorter dirty-origin flush delay) applies to the open part.

**Next steps**

Arnaud, you changed this loop in bug 2068772. Could you please look at the remaining per-origin `fsync` in `UnloadQuota`?
title: mozilla::MozPromise<T>::ThenValueBase::ResolveOrRejectRunnable::Run blocks QuotaManager IO shutdown inside __GI_fsync

comment:
This bug repeats bug 2083336, which was closed by its reporter. The problem still occurs, so this bug stays open to track it. This bug blocks bug 2011679, which tracks Bluetooth audio and video problems.

comment:
Bug 2048390 has the same signature. Its fix landed on 2026-08-31. It blocks hardware video encoding for Intel Ivy Bridge and older, Intel Baytrail, and AMD drivers below 31.0.0.0. This crash is on Intel Haswell, and that blocklist does not cover Haswell.

**Analysis**

The crash report is Nightly 161 on Windows 10. It shows Intel device 0x0a16 with driver 10.18.15.4248 and a second NVIDIA adapter (0x0fe4). The loaded `mfx_mft_h264ve_64.dll` is version 6.15.5.20. The GPU process crashes 2 seconds after start, on a null read in the Intel encoder DLL.

`GPUParent::RecvInit` starts `MCSInfo::GetSupportFromFactory` on a background thread. For H.264, `CanCreateWMFEncoder` checks `gfxVars::UseH264HwEncode()` ([WMFDataEncoderUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFDataEncoderUtils.cpp#74)). Then `MFTEncoder::Create` calls `ActivateObject` on the Intel encoder ([MFTEncoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/platforms/wmf/MFTEncoder.cpp#523)). The Intel DLL crashes inside this call. The DLL has no symbols, so the null object is not known.

`UseH264HwEncode` stays true because no `FEATURE_HARDWARE_VIDEO_ENCODING` entry matches this device. The entries from bug 2048390 are in `GfxInfo::GetGfxDriverInfo()` ([GfxInfo.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/widget/windows/GfxInfo.cpp#1510)). Device 0x0A16 is in `DeviceFamily::IntelHaswell` ([GfxDriverInfo.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/widget/GfxDriverInfo.cpp#243)), not in `IntelHDGraphicsToIvyBridge`. The entries use `AdapterMatch::Any`, so they also match an Intel adapter next to an NVIDIA adapter.

This cause explains the other facts. The probe runs at each GPU process start, so a few installations give many reports with uptime under 10 seconds. Bugs 2047978 and 2067319 limit hardware encoding to the GPU process, so no new reports come from the RDD process. The signature exists since 2021, so this is not a regression of a recent change.

**Fix direction**

Add a `FEATURE_HARDWARE_VIDEO_ENCODING` entry for `DeviceFamily::IntelHaswell` next to the bug 2048390 entries. One option blocks the full device family. The other option blocks drivers up to 10.18.15.4248. With `AdapterMatch::Any`, the entry also turns off NVIDIA hardware encoding on these dual-GPU laptops, as for Ivy Bridge.

Open points:
- Do Haswell drivers newer than 10.18.15.4248 also crash? A crash-stats facet of the driver version on Haswell devices can show this.
- Before 2026-10-27, most reports came from CPU model 58 (Ivy Bridge) with driver 10.18.10.4358. It is not confirmed that the bug 2048390 entries match all of those device ids.

Andrew, could you please look at the fix direction? You wrote the hardware encoding blocklist in bug 2048390.

comment:
Thank you for the about:support and the profile.

**Analysis**

The `about:logging` profile in comment 4 shows that the Widevine CDM refuses to decrypt the video and the audio. The page creates a Widevine session, and both license updates succeed. Then the only key changes to `output-restricted`. A `getStatusForPolicy` check for HDCP 1.0 also gives `output-restricted`. Every output protection reply that the CDM gets has a link mask of 0 and a protection mask of 0.

The probable cause is the output protection reply in the GMP code. Gecko sets the HDCP protection bit in [ChromiumCDMProxy.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/gmp/ChromiumCDMProxy.cpp#394) when `media.widevine.hdcp-protection-mask` is true, which is the default. But `ChromiumCDMParent` keeps only the link mask. When the CDM asks again, the cached reply sends a protection mask of 0 ([ChromiumCDMParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/gmp/ChromiumCDMParent.cpp#649)). A query that comes before the CDM callback exists also gets 0 ([ChromiumCDMParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/gmp/ChromiumCDMParent.cpp#639)). So the CDM sees no HDCP on the output, and it restricts the key.

A second defect makes the failure silent. On `NoKeyErr`, [EMEDecoderModule.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/eme/EMEDecoderModule.cpp#187) sends the audio sample to the CDM again at once. [CDMCaps.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/eme/CDMCaps.cpp#20) counts `output-restricted` as usable, so the decoder does not wait for a key change. The profile shows `kNoKey` for the same AAC sample 6,382 times in 49 seconds. The CDM gives black frames for the H.264 video. No audio comes out, so the seek never completes and the element stays at `HAVE_METADATA`.

**Regression status**

This is a regression from the reporter's view, between Firefox 158 and 159. The investigation found no change in these Gecko paths in Firefox 159. The probable trigger is the release rollout of Widevine 4.10.3112.0 on 2026-10-29 (bug 2074938). The about:support shows that this profile downloaded 4.10.3112.0 on 2026-10-30. Bug 1705138 had the same `output-restricted` symptom after an earlier Widevine update. A test of Firefox 158 with Widevine 4.10.3112.0 can confirm the trigger.

**Fix direction**

1. Keep the protection mask beside `mOutputProtectionLinkMask`, and send it on the cached reply and on the early reply.
2. On `NoKeyErr` in `EMEDecryptor::Decrypted`, wait for the next key status change before the sample goes back to the CDM.

The cause is in the GMP code, so this bug moves to Audio/Video: GMP. Andrew, could you please look at the output protection reply with Widevine 4.10.3112.0?

comment:
Thanks for the local test page in comment 23 (attachment 9672196). It shows the problem every time.

**Analysis**

The test page confirms the first path from comment 18. A running AudioContext keeps its audio stream started for as long as the context runs. In [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#391), `AudioTrackPresent()` returns true for every Web Audio track in the graph, and `CheckDriver()` keeps the audio driver while it is true. The graph has no silence timer. Only `suspend()`, `close()` or the end of the window removes the tracks.

Bug 1771179 tracks the fix: pause the audio stream after some time of silence, and keep `currentTime` moving. Bug 1863193 reports the same cause on Windows. The test page plays an oscillator at gain 0.0001. These samples are not zero, but they are below the -72 dB threshold in [AudibilityMonitor.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/AudibilityMonitor.h#20). Thus [AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#823) reports the context as not audible, so Firefox shows no tab audio indicator and takes no "audio-playing" wake lock.

This fact matters for the silence test in bug 1771179. A test that looks only for zero samples does not catch this page. A test against the audibility threshold catches it, but it also pauses output that is very quiet.

The Bluetooth case in comment 14 agrees with this cause. On a default device change, the macOS cubeb backend moves a running stream to the new default device and starts it again. It does not restart a stopped stream. So comment 14 shows a stream that was still running, probably from a running AudioContext or an audio track that did not end. It does not show a leaked stream.

Code reading also shows a probable second path on macOS. Bug 2052692 landed on 2026-07-14 and turned on `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` by default on macOS. When a playing media element seeks, [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/e924f94175311819d7b549a732d0d8ee1263b31d/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#730) keeps its audio stream running for reuse. Only the next `Start()` or the shutdown of the decoder releases it. If the element is paused when the seek completes, `Start()` does not run, and the stream can stay open with silence. No test confirms this path yet, and it cannot explain the reports from 2023 to 2025.

**Next steps**

Karl, could you please look at the test page in attachment 9672196 for the silence test in bug 1771179?

Alastor, could you please check whether the stream stays running after a seek ends on a paused element? A quick test is `a.currentTime = 0; a.pause()` on a playing `<audio>`, then `pmset -g assertions`.

The bug also still waits for the profiles that comment 18 asked qseminq and Lukas for. They can show which graph keeps the stream after the Bluetooth device goes away.
