comment:
Thanks for the profile and the about:support text. This difference between the sites is not intentional.

**Analysis**

The profile shows that the two sites use two different audio paths. On m.soundcloud.com, the page sends the media element into an `AudioContext` with `createMediaElementSource`. The Web Audio graph then opens the output stream. On m.youtube.com, the media element plays through `AudioStream`, with no Web Audio.

Firefox asks AAudio for a different performance mode on each path. cubeb selects the low latency mode when the requested latency is 4000 frames or less ([cubeb_aaudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_aaudio.cpp#1434)). The Web Audio graph asks for the minimum latency of the device, here 96 frames, raised to 128 ([GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#580)). `AudioStream` asks for 100 ms, which is 4800 frames at 48 kHz. The profile agrees: the SoundCloud stream uses performance mode 12 (low latency), and the YouTube stream uses mode 11 (power saving).

Both streams use the shared mode and the same usage, `AAUDIO_USAGE_MEDIA`, so these are not the difference. The decoder is also not the difference: both paths send decoded audio to cubeb. No errors show in the profile.

The probable cause is that Android or the Samsung equalizer does not process low latency AAudio streams. Android often plays these streams on a fast path with no effects. No test proves this yet. If it is correct, all Web Audio output on Android skips the system equalizer. Firefox does not implement `latencyHint` yet (bug 2020377), so a page cannot ask for a higher latency.

**Next steps**

A test with a higher Web Audio latency can confirm the cause. Could you please do this test in Firefox Nightly or Firefox Beta on the same phone? The release version does not open `about:config`.

Caution: this pref makes the Web Audio latency higher. Delete it after the test.

1. Open `about:config`.
2. Search for `media.cubeb_latency_mtg_frames`.
3. Add it as a Number with the value `4096`.
4. Close Firefox completely and open it again.
5. Turn on the equalizer and play a track on SoundCloud.
6. Tell us if the equalizer changes the sound now.

comment:
This test timed out 3 times in the last 7 days. All failures are on Linux opt (linux2404-64 and linux2404-64-asan), on autoland, mozilla-central and mozilla-beta. The test page reported no result, and the browser did not respond until wptrunner stopped it. The log has no crash dump, no stack and no audio log. The test is not new: it landed in 2021 with bug 1735684.

**Analysis**

The probable cause is a deadlock that starts on the content main thread in `getOutputTimestamp()`. No stack proves it yet.

1. `AudioContext::GetOutputTimestamp` calls `OutputLatency()` ([AudioContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/webaudio/AudioContext.cpp#593)).
2. `MediaTrackGraphImpl::AudioOutputLatency` takes the graph `mMonitor` and holds it during the latency query ([MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#4099)).
3. `AudioCallbackDriver::AudioOutputLatency` calls `cubeb_stream_get_latency` ([GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#1282)). With AudioIPC on Linux, this is a blocking call to the parent process.
4. In the parent, cubeb-pulse `latency()` waits for the PulseAudio mainloop lock ([stream.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/third_party/rust/cubeb-pulse/src/backend/stream.rs#768)).
5. The PulseAudio mainloop thread can hold that lock while its write callback waits for the content data callback ([server.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/third_party/rust/audioipc2-server/src/server.rs#270)).
6. The content data callback waits for the graph runner thread ([GraphRunner.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/GraphRunner.cpp#87)). That thread waits for `mMonitor` in `SwapMessageQueues()` ([MediaTrackGraphImpl.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/MediaTrackGraphImpl.h#359)).

Step 5 comes from how libpulse runs its callbacks, and no stack confirms it. No step in this cycle has a timeout. The window is small, because a data callback must run at the time of the latency query. Slower ASan builds make it more probable, and the tests pass again after a restart. No regressor is known.

The same cycle can probably also hang a web page on Linux that reads `outputLatency` or calls `getOutputTimestamp()`.

**Next steps**

A stack of the parent and content processes at the timeout can confirm the cause. The cause is confirmed when the content main thread is in `cubeb_stream_get_latency` and the content graph runner thread waits in `SwapMessageQueues()`. The log modules `MediaTrackGraph:5,cubeb:5,WebAudioAPI:5` can also help.

The suggested fix direction is to not call cubeb on the main thread while it holds `mMonitor`. A more complete fix queries the latency off the main thread, after stream start and on a device change. The main thread then reads a cached value.

Karl, could you please look at this probable deadlock in `MediaTrackGraphImpl::AudioOutputLatency`?

Paul is fixing this assertion in bug 2008586 (comment 3). Bug 2008586 tracks the same defect. During content process XPCOM shutdown, the `HRTFDatabaseLdr` thread does the last release of the loader in `HRTFDatabaseLoader::ProxyRelease()`. At that time, the main thread can no longer take a dispatch.

The stack in comment 0 shows this race on Windows. The main thread waits for the loader thread in `HRTFDatabaseLoader::shutdown()`, from `nsLayoutStatics::Shutdown()`. At the same time, the loader thread asserts in `ProxyRelease()` in [HRTFDatabaseLoader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/dom/media/webaudio/blink/HRTFDatabaseLoader.cpp#133).

The patch of bug 2008586 also changes the path in `ProxyRelease()` for a release off the main thread. So it covers this stack, also when the loader starts before shutdown. The patch landed on 2026-05-22, and a backout for wpt failures followed on the same day. The patch is not in the tree again yet, so this intermittent failure can still occur.

Henrik asked in comment 6 about bug 2035725. That bug is closed with no fix, so bug 2008586 is the better target. Bug 2086026 shows the same assertion at a higher rate on macOS.

comment:
Thank you for the detailed report and the stack.

**Analysis**

This looks like the same cause as bug 2082667. Its sandbox fix landed in Firefox 161 Nightly on 2026-10-30, after your 159 build (20261027034604). In the RDD sandbox, the brokered `socket()` gives libcuda one half of a socketpair whose other half is already closed. So the poll of the CUDA service thread never sleeps, and each wake ends in the `accept4` trap that returns `-EAGAIN`. The thread does not depend on playback, so the loop continues while the video is paused.

The fix in bug 2082667 changes `CudaUvmFdTrap` in [SandboxFilter.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/141096d7cd9e6f6118d94d79ea0c1777839efe9e/security/sandbox/linux/SandboxFilter.cpp#2005). On `bind`, it replaces the fd with an unarmed timerfd, so the wait is expected to block. The change is in the sandbox, so it also applies when system FFmpeg creates the Vulkan device. Nobody has tested it on this setup yet. Firefox 160 does not get this change.

This bug also waits for the needinfo on Sotaro from comment 1. It blocks bug 2053144 (Vulkan video decoding on Linux) and bug 1766429 (Linux playback).

**Next steps**

Peder, could you please test a Firefox Nightly build from 2026-10-31 or later?

2. Play the same video, then pause it.

comment:
Thanks for the profile in comment 8. Here is what it shows, and the probable cause in the code.

**Profile analysis**

The profile has the decoder threads of the GPU and Utility processes. It does not have the content process of the YouTube tab, so it has no `MediaDecoderStateMachine` or `MediaSource` markers. The video uses the WMF hardware H.264 decoder at 1920x1080.

- At 229.71 s, the audio decoder restarts at time 0. This is about 2.2 s before the video reaches its end.
- At 231.93 s, the video decoder flushes. Its first new sample is the keyframe at 18.82 s, not a frame near 0.
- After the loop, no video sample between 0 and 18.8 s goes to the decoder. The decoder then gets no input for 18.5 s, until the audio reaches 18.8 s.

So the frozen picture is the frame at 18.8 s. It stays on screen until the audio clock reaches it.

**Probable cause**

This cause comes from code reading. No log from the content process confirms it yet.

YouTube sets the `loop` attribute. With `media.seamless-looping-video` at its default `true`, `LoopingDecodingState` in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1097) loops each track on its own, without a normal seek.

1. After about 218 s of 1080p playback, MSE eviction probably removed the first 18.8 s of video from the SourceBuffer. The smaller audio buffer keeps its start.
2. At the video end, `RequestDataFromStartPosition` resets the video demuxer and seeks it to 0. `MediaSourceTrackDemuxer::Reset` in [MediaSourceDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/mediasource/MediaSourceDemuxer.cpp#311) calls `TrackBuffersManager::Seek` with time 0. For time 0, [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2938) does not check the buffered range and selects the first keyframe in the buffer, here 18.8 s.
3. `MediaSourceTrackDemuxer::DoSeek` rejects the seek to 0 and waits for data, because 0 is not buffered. `LoopingDecodingState::HandleError` in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3220) only waits. When data arrives, `HandleVideoWaited` in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1330) asks for the next sample and does not seek again.
4. Both tracks get the same loop offset, so audio from 0 and video from 18.8 s stay 18.8 s apart. The video sink drops only late frames, so the early frame stays on screen.

A normal seek does seek again after the wait. This explains why a manual seek to 0 always works. The cause is in the MSE demuxer and the state machine, not in a decoder. This explains the same problem with AV1 software decoding (comment 9). The case in comment 0 with normal video and offset sound is probably the same problem with the audio start evicted.

Bug 2023823 reports the same problem on long YouTube videos. There, `media.seamless-looping-video` set to `false` stops the problem (comment 3). A larger video eviction threshold also makes the video return to 0. These two facts support the cause above.

The probable cause is the seamless video looping of bug 1262276, which bug 1799205 enabled by default in Firefox 109. This bug now blocks the YouTube playback meta bug 1904915.

**Fix direction**

On MSE, check that time 0 is buffered on both tracks before seamless looping starts. If it is not, leave seamless looping and let the media element do a normal loop seek to 0. A simpler option is to turn off seamless video looping for MSE where [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3002) reads the pref. The state machine already has `mIsMSE`. A mochitest can show the fix: append media, remove the start of the video buffer, and let the element loop.

Alastor, could you please review this analysis and decide the fix direction?

**Workaround**

1. Open `about:config`.
2. Set `media.seamless-looping-video` to `false`.

The loop then uses a normal seek to 0.
title: Looping a video on YouTube has a high chance causing the video/audio to completely mismatch

comment:
Thanks for the test. It confirms the cause. This comment comes from an automated triage account. The next step goes to a developer.

**Analysis**

The sites do not choose the audio mode. Firefox chooses it from the audio path that the page uses. SoundCloud sends its media element through Web Audio, so it gets the low latency mode.

Firefox opens every Web Audio graph at the minimum latency of the device ([GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#580), [CubebUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/dom/media/CubebUtils.cpp#766)). On this phone, that is 128 frames. cubeb selects `AAUDIO_PERFORMANCE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY` for 4000 frames or less, and `AAUDIO_PERFORMANCE_MODE_POWER_SAVING` above that ([cubeb_aaudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/7a315fc898bbd3e61ba7dd220a8fb1d0721a1eb7/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_aaudio.cpp#1434)). The low latency stream does not go through the system equalizer. Your value of 4096 is above 4000, so the stream used the power saving mode and the equalizer applied.

The graph does not know if the page needs low latency. A graph that only `createMediaElementSource` feeds gets the same latency as a game or a synthesizer. Firefox does not implement `latencyHint` yet (bug 2020377). cubeb has no option to select the AAudio mode separately from the latency.

This is probably not a regression. The mapping from latency to mode is in cubeb since 2020.

**Fix direction**

The fix needs a decision between low Web Audio latency and working system effects on Android. These directions can be combined:

- Implement `latencyHint` (bug 2020377). The "playback" value selects the power saving mode. This alone does not fix SoundCloud, because SoundCloud uses the default value.
- On Android, give a higher latency to graphs with no audio input, or to graphs that only media elements feed.
- Add a stream option to cubeb that selects the AAudio mode separately from the latency. `media/libcubeb` comes from github.com/mozilla/cubeb, so this change lands upstream first.

Open point: a test with `media.cubeb_latency_mtg_frames` set to 2048 keeps the low latency mode with a larger buffer. Its result can show if the mode alone causes the equalizer skip.

Paul, could you please look at this bug and choose a direction for the Web Audio latency on Android?
title: Android system-wide equalizer not applied

comment:
Thanks for the clear report.

**Analysis**

This is not specific to MPRIS. Firefox decides in the parent-process `MediaController` code which tab owns the system media controls. MPRIS only shows that choice. The two mute cases behave differently because of two rules in the media control code.

1. A tab that is muted before playback never gets media control. [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#8998) `StartMediaControlKeyListenerIfNeeded` does not start the listener while a controllable element is inaudible. Bug 1653390 added this audible check.
2. A tab that is muted after audible playback keeps media control. The element only reports that it is inaudible. [MediaController.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/mediacontrol/MediaController.cpp#486) `ShouldDeactivateController` does not check `mIsMuted`. Bug 1665527 expects muted media to stay controllable.
3. A muted tab can also take the main slot. [MediaControlService.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/mediacontrol/MediaControlService.cpp#194) `NotifyControllerPlaybackStateChanged` makes any playing controller the main controller. It does not check mute. Metadata updates go on for the same reason.

This behavior is not a regression. It comes from the 2020 media control design. Bug 1615665 is related: a silent video keeps its controller until the tab closes.

**Fix direction**

A possible fix is in `MediaController`. Deactivate the controller on a tab mute, and activate it again on unmute. `ShouldActivateController` can also check `mIsMuted`. A smaller option is to skip muted controllers when `MediaControlService` picks the main controller. This stops the slot problem, but the entry stays. Both options need a decision: should a tab mute remove the system controls while a mute in the page player keeps them?

Alastor, you wrote much of this code. Could you please decide which behavior a tab mute should have?

The bug also waits for the profile and about:support that comment 1 asks for, and for the reply from Matthew.
issue_type_note: media control / MPRIS entry on mute
title: Muting a tab doesn't remove the MPRIS playback entry

comment:
Thanks for the detailed report. The code at fault is in widget code, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk.

**Analysis**

The fallback is in `WaylandSurface::SetHDRMetadata` in [WaylandSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/widget/gtk/WaylandSurface.cpp#1731). It runs for PQ content when the stream has no CLL and no MDCV metadata. Bug 2063867 added it.

In the current tree, `sdrContentBrightness` is always 80 nits. The only caller in [NativeLayerWayland.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/gfx/layers/NativeLayerWayland.cpp#1139) passes `nullptr` for the GdkWindow, so the code finds no screen. Bug 2078134 made this change, and it landed on 2026-10-06. Before that change, the code used the SDR white of the screen. This is the probable cause of a change in behavior, but no bisection confirms it. Thus the regression status is not known yet.

Under PQ, the protocol ignores the `max_lum` value of `set_luminances` and uses `min_lum` + 10000 nits ([color-management-v1-client-protocol.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/widget/gtk/wayland/color-management-v1-client-protocol.h#2139)). So the value of 1000 nits has no effect. The values that have an effect are `reference_lum` = 80 and max_cll = max_fall = 80. A compositor that anchors content to `reference_lum` maps a signal of 80 nits to its SDR white. The PQ default reference is 203 nits, so the image can look about 2.5 times too bright. A max_cll of 80 also tells the compositor that the content has no highlights to tone map.

How KWin 6.8 uses these two values is not confirmed. The fallback values obey the protocol rules, so a compositor must not reject them.

Part 2 is valid. When metadata is present, the code calls `SetContentLightLevel` with no checks. The `create` request raises `invalid_luminance` when max_cll or max_fall is outside the mastering luminance range ([color-management-v1-client-protocol.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/widget/gtk/wayland/color-management-v1-client-protocol.h#1963)). It also raises it when max_fall is above max_cll. This is a protocol error, and it applies to every compositor, not only Weston and Mutter.

Two inputs can break these rules. The MP4 demuxer adds a default CLL of 1000 nits ([DecoderData.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/mp4/DecoderData.cpp#405)). This value can be above a real MDCV peak that is below 1000 nits. The WebM demuxer keeps a CLL when only one of its two fields is 0 ([WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#444)).

**Fix direction**

- In the fallback, do not send `reference_lum` = 80. Remove the `set_luminances` call so that the PQ default applies, or send the real reference luminance of the output.
- Set max_cll to 1000 or leave it unset. Keep max_fall at or below max_cll.
- Before `create`, check max_cll and max_fall against the effective mastering range. Remove or clamp a value that breaks the rules.

The codec, the container and the test stream of the report are not known. This bug also goes on the Linux playback meta bug 1766429.

Martin, could you please look at this bug? You changed this code in bug 2078134 and bug 2066397.
title: [Wayland][HDR] Fix HDR metadata fallback to avoid overexposure under KWin 6.8+

comment:
This crash has the same cause as bug 1503676. The native stack in both bugs nests the same way: `MediaKeys::Shutdown` calls `MediaDrmCDMProxy::Shutdown`, and `nsThread::Shutdown` then runs a queued `ProxyNativeCall<MediaDrmJavaCallbacksSupport, ...>` callback. Only the queued callback is different. The JNI glue throws a `java.lang.NullPointerException` before the callback runs, probably because `DisposeNative` already cleared the native handle. `MOZ_CATCH_JNI_EXCEPTION` then turns the exception into `MOZ_CRASH(JNI exception)`. A fix for bug 1503676 also fixes this crash.

**New data for bug 1503676**

- The crash report in comment 0 is from Fenix 160.0b4 on Android, in the content process. The queued callback has the argument types of `onSessionCreated` (int, int, byte[], byte[]). Bug 1503676 shows an (int, byte[]) callback.
- A sample of 72 crashes with this signature since 2026-10-05 has 56 crashes with `MediaDrmJavaCallbacksSupport` on top. All 56 are in the content process, and 54 of them run inside `MediaDrmCDMProxy::Shutdown`.
- The callbacks in the sample are `onSessionCreated` (25), `onSessionUpdated` or `onSessionClosed` (22), `onRejectPromise` (4) and `onSessionMessage` (4).
- The other crashes in the sample are in the parent process and have other causes, for example `widget::EventDispatcher`. These crashes are not part of bug 1503676.
- In the last 30 days, Fenix has 539 crashes with this signature on release, from 416 installations.

Bug 1503676 has no crash signature. We suggest that a person add `[@ java.lang.NullPointerException: at org.mozilla.gecko.mozglue.GeckoLoader.nativeRun(Native Method)]` to bug 1503676. Caution: the signature is generic, so crash-stats then also links the unrelated parent-process crashes to that bug.
title: Crash in [@ java.lang.NullPointerException: at org.mozilla.gecko.mozglue.GeckoLoader.nativeRun(Native Method)]

**Analysis**

When a tab is muted, Firefox closes the audio stream of a media element ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#292)). For an `AudioContext`, a muted tab only sets the volume to 0, and the stream stays open ([AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#712)). The stream in the screenshot stays when the tab is muted. So an `AudioContext` on the Iris page probably owns it, but no log confirms this yet. Bug 1984881 tracks an `AudioContext` that keeps the audio device open with no sound.

Bug 2042877, fixed on 2026-10-29, stops an `AudioContext` from opening the audio device before the page is allowed to play. A click on the page, such as on "browse", allows the page to play audio. This is also true when the site permission is "Block Audio". The stream takes its name from the page title.

The MPRIS update after a mute in comment 4 is a different behavior, in the media control code. We recommend a separate bug for it.

comment:
This crash is a remaining path of the defect that bug 1659817 and bug 1726024 fixed. Those fixes return `nullptr` only when the async shutdown service is missing. They keep the two release asserts after the getter call.

**Analysis**

`media::GetShutdownBarrier()` in [MediaUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/systemservices/MediaUtils.cpp#88) asserts that `GetXpcomWillShutdown` succeeds and gives a barrier. In a content process, `GetProfileBeforeChange` gives no barrier, so line 86 always calls `GetXpcomWillShutdown`. The async shutdown service is written in JS, so this call can fail, for example on a JS OOM exception (bug 1911632 comment 4).

The crash report in comment 0 agrees with this. It is a content process on Nightly 161, with an uptime of 34 seconds and no shutdown annotation. It has the `JSOutOfMemory` annotation, and only 11 MB of page file was available. The JS recursion idea in comment 0 does not agree with the data, because the stack is shallow.

The lazy getter in [nsAsyncShutdown.sys.mjs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/toolkit/components/asyncshutdown/nsAsyncShutdown.sys.mjs#230) deletes itself before it reads `lazy.AsyncShutdown[k]`. If that read throws once, each later read probably gives `undefined`. Then `rv` succeeds but the barrier is null, and the assert at line 89 fires.

In the last 30 days, crash-stats has 78 crashes with this signature, all in content processes, 73 on Windows. 55 crashes are at line 88 and 23 at line 89. 68 crashes come from `MediaShutdownManager::InitStatics` when a page creates a media element. 2 come from the `AudioContext` path in comment 0, and 8 from `MustGetShutdownBarrier`.

**Related bugs**

- Bug 1973140: the same failure one step later, in the `AddBlocker` call of `MediaTrackGraphImpl::AddShutdownBlocker`.
- Bug 1911632: the same failure in the `MustGetShutdownBarrier` callers, with the fix options in comment 7.
- Bug 1760855: an async shutdown service that is not written in JS. This bug depends on it.

**Fix direction**

The long-term fix is bug 1760855. A short-term option is to make `GetShutdownBarrier` return `nullptr` when `rv` fails or the barrier is null, as the `!svc` case does. `MustGetShutdownBarrier` keeps its asserts. The callers in 70 of the 78 crashes already accept `nullptr`: [MediaShutdownManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/MediaShutdownManager.cpp#60), [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#1832) and [MediaRecorder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/MediaRecorder.cpp#1066). With that change, media stops working in that process, but the tab does not crash.

This is not a regression. The asserts date from bug 1296531 in 2017, and crash-stats has this signature since build 20171211020921.
title: Crash in [@ mozilla::media::GetShutdownBarrier]

comment:
This failure is a black video picture, not a WebVTT cue problem.

**Analysis**

The failing run is on the Android 14 x86_64 emulator (GeckoView, isolated process), in web-platform-tests-reftest chunk 17. It is a debug build: the log reports assertion counts. This test is the only unexpected result in that task.

In the test screenshot, the 320x240 picture of `white.webm` is pure black (0,0,0). These are exactly the 76800 different pixels. In the reference, the same area is white. The cue text pixels are the same in both images, so the cue renders correctly.

The test pauses on `playing`, seeks to 2 s and calls `takeScreenshot()` on `seeked` ([fontsize_smaller_than_container.tentative.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/testing/web-platform/tests/webvtt/rendering/cues-with-video/processing-model/selectors/cue/fontsize_smaller_than_container.tentative.html#16)). The reference has no video. Its white area is the page background ([fontsize_smaller_than_container-ref.tentative.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/testing/web-platform/tests/webvtt/rendering/cues-with-video/processing-model/selectors/cue/fontsize_smaller_than_container-ref.tentative.html#7)).

A missing frame does not give black. With no image or a 0x0 image, `nsDisplayVideo` paints nothing, and the white page shows ([nsVideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/layout/generic/nsVideoFrame.cpp#613)). So the compositor drew an image of the correct size, and that image was black. The probable sources are a black or unfilled frame from the VP8 decoder, or a texture that was not ready at the snapshot. The log has no media logging, so the decoder that ran is not known.

`SeekCompleted` resolves the seek before it calls `Redraw` with the new frame ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3290)). The new frame reaches the compositor asynchronously. But the white frame from before the seek stays the current image, so this order alone does not explain a black picture.

The test metadata accepts FAIL only on Android opt builds, so this debug run reports an unexpected result ([fontsize_smaller_than_container.tentative.html.ini](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/dcafde486e11b7a7776137b92fec2a6f56744eab/testing/web-platform/meta/webvtt/rendering/cues-with-video/processing-model/selectors/cue/fontsize_smaller_than_container.tentative.html.ini#5)). The metadata update in bug 2007273 added that opt line. It is not known if those opt failures also showed a black picture.

In the same task, `color_hsla.html` and `color_rgba.html` failed as known intermittents, but for a different reason: cue box offsets (bug 1985013). This bug is a different failure. It blocks the WebVTT meta bug 2010319.

**Next steps**

A CI run with `MOZ_LOG=MediaDecoder:4,MediaFormatReader:4,PlatformDecoderModule:4` can show which VP8 decoder ran. It can also show which frame was current at `seeked`.

**Analysis**

The probable cause is that the SHM upload drops the color metadata of the frame. Because of that, the HLG to PQ fallback does not run on this path. This comes from code reading only, and no log proves it yet.

1. `SHMBufSurfaceYUV::UploadToDMABufSurface` in [SHMBufSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/widget/gtk/SHMBufSurface.cpp#385) returns `DMABufSurfaceYUV::CreateYUVSurface()` and copies no color data to the new surface. The RGBA variant at line 207 copies the transfer function, the primaries and the range.
2. `DMABufSurfaceYUV::UpdateYUVData(GLContext*, BufferSurface*)` in [DMABufSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/widget/gtk/DMABufSurface.cpp#1894) reads only the format, the textures and the size. The new surface keeps the defaults: the BT709 transfer function, the BT709 color space and full range.
3. `NativeLayerWaylandExternal::AttachExternalImage` in [NativeLayerWayland.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/gfx/layers/NativeLayerWayland.cpp#1578) reads the transfer function from the uploaded surface. The HLG check is then false, so `ConvertHLGToPQ` does not run.
4. The color properties still describe the original SHM surface, which reports HLG. When the compositor does not support HLG, Firefox sets no image description. The compositor then probably shows the HLG samples with its default description, and the colors look washed out.

**Fix direction**

Copy the color space, the range, the primaries, the transfer function and the HDR metadata from the SHM surface to the new DMABuf surface. `SHMBufSurfaceYUV::UploadToDMABufSurface` or `DMABufSurfaceYUV::UpdateYUVData()` can do this copy. After that, the conversion runs on this path, so this path also needs the fix of bug 2089494. There, the color properties must describe the buffer that Firefox attaches. `ConvertHLGToPQ` also picks its matrix from `IsFullRange()`, so limited range video needs the correct range from the copy.

**Related bugs**

The SHM path came from bug 2078134 and bug 2068021. Bug 2068021 removed the direct FFmpeg upload, which set this metadata, so it is the probable cause for software decoded HLG video. The HLG fallback came from bug 2066397. A run with `MOZ_LOG=Dmabuf:5,WidgetCompositor:5` can confirm the cause: the `HLG->PQ converted` line is absent, and the `Transfer function HLG isn't supported. Quit` line is present.

The code at fault is in `widget/gtk` (Core :: Widget: Gtk) and `gfx/layers` (Core :: Graphics). This bug now also blocks bug 1766429, the Linux playback meta bug.

This failure is in service worker registration, not in WebCodecs code. So we move the bug to Core :: DOM: Service Workers.

**Analysis**

All three failures in the last 7 days are on linux2204-64-wayland on autoland. Two are debug runs (tasks GVeKX5y8Q3yXIG1LwWkv2A and ZMGhDahSS2aaa6IdJSNquw), and one is an opt run (task ZJXPC4wJTxCdI14UQG-0yg).

The test runs 7 service worker subtests. Each subtest unregisters, registers and activates a new service worker through `postToServiceWorker` in [serialization-to-shared-and-service-workers.https.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/testing/web-platform/tests/webcodecs/serialization-to-shared-and-service-workers.https.html#18). The file uses the default timeout: 30 s on debug and 10 s on opt. The test came into the tree with the WPT sync of bug 2079603.

- In both debug runs, five service worker subtests pass. Then "AudioData cannot be cloned to a service worker" is still in `register()` when the harness timeout fires.
- After the timeout, both debug logs show `'Canceled() || !swm'` at [ServiceWorkerUpdateJob.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/serviceworkers/ServiceWorkerUpdateJob.cpp#321) and `Not resolving response 'PServiceWorkerContainer::Reply_Register': actor is dead`. So the register job was still in its script comparison step, and the AudioData `postMessage` never ran.
- In GVeKX5y8Q3yXIG1LwWkv2A, the log has no lines for 14.3 s during the service worker subtests. In ZMGhDahSS2aaa6IdJSNquw, each service worker subtest takes 4 to 7 s, with no single long stall.
- In the opt run, the first service worker subtest times out. It is "A plain object can be posted to a service worker". The 6 other service worker subtests do not run.
- In all three runs, `encodedVideoChunk-serialization.crossAgentCluster.https.html` had an earlier timeout in its service worker subtest in the same browser. That timeout is known intermittent. It has the same late `Reply_Register` pattern. Bug 2070302 tracked it.
- The logs show no `CacheOpParent` or "Could not open cache." lines, and no crash or assertion.

The subtest that times out changes from run to run, and it is not always an AudioData subtest. This points to slow or stalled service worker registration on the Linux Wayland pool. A test expectation in a new `testing/web-platform/meta/webcodecs/serialization-to-shared-and-service-workers.https.html.ini` can stop the failures. That expectation is `[OK, TIMEOUT]` for the file, and `[PASS, TIMEOUT, NOTRUN]` for the service worker subtests. The expectation does not fix the stall. A debug log with `MOZ_LOG=ServiceWorkerManager:5` can show which step of the register job is slow.

Harveer, could you please look at the slow service worker registration on the Linux Wayland pool?

Thanks for the split from bug 2089034. The checks belong in widget code, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk.

**Analysis**

`WaylandSurface::SetHDRMetadata` in [WaylandSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/widget/gtk/WaylandSurface.cpp#1692) sends the stream values to the compositor with no checks. `SetContentLightLevel` sends max_cll and max_fall unchanged. `SetMasteringDisplayColorVolume` only clamps negative values to 0.

The `create` request raises `invalid_luminance` when max_cll or max_fall is not above min L, or is above max L of the mastering range ([color-management-v1-client-protocol.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/widget/gtk/wayland/color-management-v1-client-protocol.h#1961)). It also raises it when max_fall is above max_cll. These rules apply to every compositor.

Web content can give such values. One example is an MP4 file with an MDCV peak below 1000 nits and no CLL box. The demuxer then adds a default max_cll of 1000 ([DecoderData.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/mp4/DecoderData.cpp#405)). Other examples are max_fall above max_cll, an MDCV box with zeros, and a max_cll of 0, which CTA-861.3 defines as "unknown".

A protocol error that `WlLogHandler` does not match goes to the generic `MOZ_CRASH` in [nsWaylandDisplay.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/widget/gtk/nsWaylandDisplay.cpp#1299). This is a crash of the parent process. This path is probable: it comes from code reading, and no crash report confirms it. It needs `gfx.color_management.hdr` and a compositor with color management.

**Points to add to comment 0**

- When the stream has no MDCV, the mastering range is the PQ primary volume, 0.005 to 10000 nits. So the max_cll check applies without MDCV too.
- max_fall must also be above min L.
- Compare the MDCV values after the scaling and the rounding that Firefox applies, because max L becomes whole nits.
- Today `set_luminances` gets only the fixed fallback values, which pass. So rule 3 is defensive.

**Fix direction**

- Put the checks in one pure helper that `SetHDRMetadata` calls before `create`.
- Drop an MDCV that has max L at or below min L, or a value that is not finite.
- Treat a max_cll or max_fall of 0 as not set.
- Clamp max_cll to max L, and set max_fall to min(max_fall, max_cll).
- Send each value only when it is above min L.
- A GTest in `widget/tests/gtest` can test the helper with no compositor.

The WIP patch by Louis-Philippe Manette on bug 2089034 (comment 3) already has some of these checks. This is not a regression: the values had no checks since bug 2057751 added this path. This bug also goes on the Linux playback meta bug 1766429.
title: [Wayland][HDR] Harden parameter validation for HDR metadata to prevent protocol errors

comment:
This looks like a problem in the Wayland compositor code in `gfx/layers`, so the bug moves to Core :: Graphics.

**Analysis**

In [NativeLayerWayland.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/gfx/layers/NativeLayerWayland.cpp#1522), `NativeLayerWaylandExternal::GetSurface()` returns the surface of `mTextureHost`. That is the P010 YUV surface from the decoder.

When the HLG->PQ conversion runs, `AttachExternalImage()` puts only the output of `ConvertHLGToPQ()` into `mFrontBuffer`. That output is an RGBA DMABuf surface with `GBM_FORMAT_ABGR2101010`.

`SetColorProperties()` reads the coefficients from `GetSurface()`. So it sends BT.2020 YCbCr coefficients and a chroma location for the RGB buffer that the commit attaches. The compositor then raises error 3 of `wp_color_representation_surface_v1`.

`GetWLColorCoeficients()` in [BufferSurface.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/widget/gtk/BufferSurface.cpp#285) gives IDENTITY for an RGBA surface. It is correct for the surface that it gets.

The same wrong surface also gives the HLG transfer function to `SetColorProperties()`. The compositor has no HLG, so the PQ buffer probably gets no PQ image description either.

**Regression**

This is a regression. The probable cause is bug 2078134, which landed on October 6, 2026. Before it, `GetSurface()` returned the surface of `mFrontBuffer`. Bug 2078134 changed it to return the surface of `mTextureHost`. This comes from code reading only.

Bug 1999636 is probably not the cause. Its change touches only `SharedSurface_DMABUF` and the color fields of `DMABufSurfaceRGBA`. An RGBA surface always gets IDENTITY coefficients.

**Fix direction**

Make `GetSurface()` return the surface of `mFrontBuffer`, because the commit attaches that buffer. Use the surface of the texture host only when there is no front buffer. Also check the SHM->DMABuf upload path in `AttachExternalImage()`, because it also replaces the source surface.

A `MOZ_LOG=WidgetWayland:5` log can confirm the cause. It shows `SetColorRepresentationLocked()` with `COEFFICIENTS_BT2020` after "HLG->PQ converted".

Martin, could you please look at this bug, because you know this code?
title: [Wayland] wl_display.error: Commit contains a color representation with coefficients for a YCbCr pixel format and a buffer with an RGB pixel format

comment:
This looks like a build ID mismatch in the GMP process after the update, not a crash of the WidevineCdm plugin. The bug also waits for the profile and the about:support that comment 1 asks for.

**Analysis**

The running instance launches each GMP child from the files on disk, and the update replaced them. The parent sends its own build ID to the child ([GMPProcessParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/gmp/GMPProcessParent.cpp#133)). In `GMPChild::Init`, a mismatch makes the child call `ProcessChild::QuickExit()` before the crash reporter starts ([GMPChild.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/gmp/GMPChild.cpp#113)). `SendStartPlugin` is the first sync message after that exit, so the log shows "Failed to send start to child process" ([GMPParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/gmp/GMPParent.cpp#477)).

`GMPParent::ActorDestroy` then gets `AbnormalShutdown` and treats the exit as a crash ([GMPParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/gmp/GMPParent.cpp#841)). It does not check `DoBuildIDsMatch()`. It sends the `gmp-plugin-crash` notification with a fake dump ID, so "Submit a crash report" has no dump to send. It also calls `ReAddOnGMPThread`, which adds a new clone of the plugin with no limit ([GMPServiceParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/gmp/GMPServiceParent.cpp#1300)). Each new MediaKeys request or reload starts the new binary again, so the loop continues until a restart.

Content processes handle the same exit differently. `nsFrameLoader` compares the build ID in memory with the build ID on disk and fires `oop-browser-buildid-mismatch`, which shows about:restartrequired ([nsFrameLoader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/base/nsFrameLoader.cpp#3624)). The GMP parent has no equivalent, and the RDD, GPU and Utility parents also have none. This explains why only the new tab showed about:restartrequired: the Spotify tab kept its old content process.

This cause is probable. It explains every observation, but no log shows the child exit at the build ID check. The capture from comment 1 can confirm it if it shows the child `GMPChild::Init` log line with nothing after it.

This does not look like a regression of a recent change. The child side check is from 2023 (bug 1845946). The profiles feature makes the case more common, because two instances often run from one install. Bug 2088735 comment 4 describes the same unlimited relaunch for a different load failure on Windows.

**Fix direction**

In `GMPParent::ActorDestroy`, or where `SendStartPlugin` fails, check that `DoBuildIDsMatch()` is false and that the build ID on disk changed. In that case, skip the crash notification and do not add the plugin again for this session. Reject the request with a distinct error, so that the front end can show a restart notice in place of the crash bar. The disk check is necessary because `DoBuildIDsMatch()` is also false when the child crashes before it sends the build ID message. A shared helper made from `BuildIDMismatchMemoryAndDisk` can serve GMP and the other child processes.

Andrew already has a needinfo on this bug from comment 1.

comment:
Thank you for the crash IDs and for the test with the pref.

**Analysis**

The crash comes from a defect in the OpenH264 2.6.0 plugin, not from Firefox code. It occurs only when `media.gmp.decoder.multithreaded` is `true`. The default is `false` in [StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml), and comment 8 confirms that `false` stops the crashes.

Crash report bp-fcb7e86e-ccaa-4611-bb5a-6718c0261014 shows `SIGABRT` on `GMPThread` in the plugin process, at startup, on Firefox 158 release. `GMPThread` was idle in its message loop when it aborted, and three OpenH264 decoder threads were alive. This probably means that another thread wrote to the stack of `GMPThread`, so libc stopped the process. The report itself has no abort message.

Firefox only passes the pref to the plugin in [GMPVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/cf103b9362d64aa14c7adc0c0e4b9469ccbf6caa/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/gmp/GMPVideoDecoder.cpp#334). Bug 2071378 changed the Linux sandbox in Firefox 158 so that the plugin can read the CPU count. Before that change, the plugin used one thread also with the pref set to `true`. So bug 2071378 exposed the plugin defect in 158, but it is not the defect.

The same crash shape is in bug 2065570, comment 43 and comment 44: Linux, plugin 2.6.0, multithreaded mode, `GMPThread`, crash at plugin startup. There, the upstream fix cisco/openh264 PR #4009 stopped the crashes. That fix is in [OpenH264 2.7.0](https://github.com/cisco/openh264/releases/tag/v2.7.0). Bug 2085032 tracks the update of Firefox to OpenH264 2.7.0. Comment 5 doubts that the two crashes are the same, so the link is probable, not proven. The check that can confirm it is a new test with the pref set to `true` after Firefox installs OpenH264 2.7.0.

Crash Stats has about 12 similar `GMPThread` crashes on Linux since 2026-10-01. They come from plugin 2.6.0 on Firefox 158, 159 and 160 Nightly, in snap, Fedora and Mozilla builds. So the problem is not specific to the snap build.

**Next steps**

The fix direction is the OpenH264 2.7.0 update in bug 2085032. Until then, keep `media.gmp.decoder.multithreaded` set to `false` as the workaround. Andrew Osmond has an open needinfo from comment 4 about the plan for this crash.

Thank you for the clear analysis and the workaround. This is the same defect as bug 2076733.

In bug 2076733, Andrew Osmond reports the same pref name mismatch, which he found when he ran the WPT EME tests on Windows ARM64. [GMPProvider.sys.mjs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/toolkit/mozapps/extensions/internal/GMPProvider.sys.mjs#796) reads `media.gmp-clearkey.allow-x64-plugin-on-arm64`, but the defined pref is `media.gmp-gmpclearkey.allow-x64-plugin-on-arm64`. The code does not find the pref, so it uses the fallback `true` and looks for Clearkey in the `i686` directory. Bug 2076733 is assigned to Andrew. Its fix direction is to remove this code, and that also fixes the Clearkey path on Windows ARM64.

Your details are useful for bug 2076733. The workaround is to set `media.gmp-clearkey.allow-x64-plugin-on-arm64` to `false` and restart Firefox. A real trigger is a script on epicurious.com. The patch sketch in comment 2 reads the same static pref as GMPParent.cpp, with the default `false`, which is a smaller alternative fix.
title: Windows ARM64: Clearkey never registers because GMPProvider reads media.gmp-clearkey.allow-x64-plugin-on-arm64 but the pref is defined as media.gmp-gmpclearkey.allow-x64-plugin-on-arm64

comment:
Thank you for the three profiles. They show the freeze clearly.

**Analysis**

All three profiles show the same pattern. The GPU process creates a new hardware video decoder, and this blocks the decode of the video that plays. The playing video runs out of decoded frames and drops them, while audio continues. The profiles show steady sampling and a busy Firefox thread, so the system does not take the CPU (this answers comment 8).

- Profile in comment 0: another YouTube tab loads its next video at about 100.1 s. Its decoder creation keeps the GPU `MediaSupervisor` thread busy for 215 ms. The 1080p60 decode requests wait, and 10 frames drop. Six more create and shutdown cycles of 60 to 90 ms follow, with 10 more dropped frames.
- Profile in comment 4: at about 17 s of the video, YouTube switches from 720p60 to 1080p60. `MediaChangeMonitor` sees the VP9 resolution change and creates a new decoder. The creation takes about 100 ms, no frame comes out for about 140 ms, and 7 frames drop.
- Profile in comment 5: a hidden YouTube tab creates and destroys VP9 decoders many times. Each creation takes 70 to 230 ms on the same GPU thread. The livestream drops frames in two bursts, at about 82 s and 87.5 s.

**Cause**

The GPU process uses one task queue ("RemVidParent") for all remote video decoders of all tabs, in [RemoteMediaManagerParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/ipc/RemoteMediaManagerParent.cpp#92). `RecvDecode` runs on this queue, in [RemoteDecoderParent.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/ipc/RemoteDecoderParent.cpp#164). `RemoteVideoDecoderParent` also calls `CreateDecoder` on it, in [RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/ipc/RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp#285). `WMFDecoderModule::AsyncCreateDecoder` does the work synchronously, in [WMFDecoderModule.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFDecoderModule.cpp#390). It calls `WMFVideoMFTManager::Init`, which blocks in `InitInternal`, in [WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/platforms/wmf/WMFVideoMFTManager.cpp#206).

The profiles show the time in `MFTEnumEx`, `D3D11DXVA2Manager::ConfigureForSize`, `SetDecoderMediaTypes` and `D3D11CreateDevice`. This GPU (Intel Gen12) is blocklisted for decoder device reuse, so each creation also makes a new D3D11 device. The cause does not depend on the decoder, so it also explains the H.264 (avc1) freezes in comment 5.

**Fix direction**

Move the WMF video decoder creation off the shared "RemVidParent" queue, for example to a separate task queue for each decoder. Then a new decoder does not block the decode of other videos. For the resolution change in the comment 4 profile, decoder reuse across a resolution change can also help. Bug 1685099 and bug 1694485 track the decoder recreation for YouTube live streams.

This bug blocks bug 1416090 (dropped video frames) and bug 1445470 (video playback performance).

**Comment 10**

Comment 10 describes a different pattern on Linux: exactly one dropped frame every 100 frames. Linux does not use this WMF path, so this bug does not cover that problem.

**Workaround**

1. Close other YouTube tabs while a video plays.
2. Select a fixed quality in the YouTube player settings, not "Auto".
title: VP09 1080p60fps Videos - Play smoothly but random moments of freeze + dropped frames throughout

comment:
The problem is still open in the current tree, but it is smaller than in Firefox 91. The FFmpeg update in bug 1889978 (Firefox 127) added a partial CET property note.

**Analysis**

All ffvpx x86 assembly files include [x86inc.asm](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/media/ffvpx/libavutil/x86/x86inc.asm#907), so this file controls the CET property note of each NASM object. In Firefox 91, this file had no `.note.gnu.property` section, which explains both annocheck failures in comment 0. Today the file emits the section for ELF x86_64 with NASM 2.14.03 or later.

The note sets only `GNU_PROPERTY_X86_FEATURE_1_SHSTK` (`pr_data = 0x2`), not IBT. The `cglobal_internal` and `cglobal_label` macros put no `endbr64` at function entries. The linker ANDs the property bits of all inputs. Thus a build with `-fcf-protection` probably gets SHSTK but not IBT in libmozavcodec.so and libmozavutil.so. A `readelf -n` on the two libraries of a current build can confirm this.

The distro `CFLAGS` do not reach NASM. The ffvpx NASM flags come only from [moz.configure](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/toolkit/moz.configure#2604), and NASM has no `-fcf-protection` option. Mozilla's own Linux builds do not use `-fcf-protection` (`security_hardening_cflags` in [toolchain.configure](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/build/moz.configure/toolchain.configure#2886)). So only hardened distro builds show the failure. The build already includes h264_intrapred.asm by default ([moz.build](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/media/ffvpx/libavcodec/x86/moz.build#12)), and all ffvpx assembly objects have the same gap.

**Fix direction**

x86inc.asm is vendored code, so the change belongs upstream first and then in a new vendor import. Behind an opt-in define such as `__CET__`, `cglobal` can emit `endbr64` at each function entry, and the note can set IBT and SHSTK (`0x3`). Indirect branch targets that are not function entries, such as jump tables, also need a landing pad. Then the Mozilla configure can pass `-D__CET__` to NASM when the C compiler defines `__CET__`.

libjpeg-turbo already uses this pattern in [jsimdext.inc](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/media/libjpeg/simd/nasm/jsimdext.inc#79), but our build does not pass `-D__CET__` to it either. The dav1d copy of [x86inc.asm](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/third_party/dav1d/src/ext/x86/x86inc.asm#919) has the same SHSTK-only note. Bug 2089942 shows the same linker behavior for libonnxruntime.so. This is not a regression.

The result agrees with the cause in comment 3. When X removes the video element, the element stops being controllable. Then the tab has no controllable media, and the play key does nothing ([ContentMediaController.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/mediacontrol/ContentMediaController.cpp#366)). The result does not fully rule out the case of bug 1696731. When the page registers a `play` action handler, Firefox sends the play key only to that handler ([ContentPlaybackController.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/mediacontrol/ContentPlaybackController.cpp#100)). Then a hidden video element does not get the key either. It is not known if X registers such a handler.

One detail adds to comment 3. The page does not have to set `MediaMetadata`. The media session exists as soon as the page uses `navigator.mediaSession` ([MediaSession.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/mediasession/MediaSession.cpp#78)).

comment:
Thanks for the testcase and the profile with logs.

**Analysis**

The profile shows why the output becomes mono. With `echoCancellation: true`, the graph opens one duplex cubeb stream with the VOICE preference ("using VOICE and requesting input processing params AEC"). cubeb then plays the page output through the macOS VoiceProcessingIO (VPIO) unit. Before the mic opens, the output is a normal stereo stream at 48000 Hz.

On the VPIO output, cubeb reads a format of 1 channel at 44100 Hz. VPIO rejects the stereo layout (`kAudioUnitProperty_AudioChannelLayout rv=-10851`), and `get_output_channel_layout` returns `MONO` for VPIO. A mixer then downmixes 2 channels to 1, and the output is resampled to 44100 Hz. The downmix explains why the chord stops moving and plays in the middle. The mono 44100 Hz VPIO path is the probable cause of the thin sound, but no test proves it yet.

In this testcase, the VPIO unit also does no processing. cubeb rejects AEC without NS ("couldn't set input processing params ECHO_CANCELLATION. AEC != NS."). Gecko then uses the libwebrtc AEC and sets the platform params to NONE, so cubeb puts VPIO in bypass. `IsVoiceInput` stays true because the software AEC is on, so the stream stays on the mono VPIO unit. With `echoCancellation: false`, the profile shows an aggregate device with stereo output at 48000 Hz.

**Affected code**

- [GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#499) selects `CUBEB_DEVICE_PREF_VOICE` when `IsVoiceInput` in [MediaEngineWebRTCAudio.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/webrtc/MediaEngineWebRTCAudio.h#130) is true.
- [mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#3641) selects VPIO for input and output when the input has VOICE.
- The same file tries the stereo layout on the VPIO output ([mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#4137)) and hard-codes `MONO` in `get_output_channel_layout` ([mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#4850)).

**Fix direction**

- In cubeb-coreaudio, try a 2-channel stream format on the VPIO output bus, and use mono only when VPIO rejects it. Nobody has tested yet whether VPIO on macOS 14 and 15 accepts it.
- When the platform processing params are NONE, VPIO gives no benefit for the output. Note that the non-VPIO duplex path has its own open problems (bug 2090431, bug 2073800).

No regressor is known. Bug 1869526 limited VPIO to VOICE input streams, and its description already says that VPIO makes the output mono.

The code at fault is in cubeb, so this bug moves to Audio/Video: cubeb. Matthew, could you please look at the VPIO output format in cubeb-coreaudio?
title: Opening a mic input stream with echoCancellation:true makes WebAudio output sound terrible on macOS

comment:
Thanks for the report and the profile. This is a duplicate of bug 2057748. That bug has the same trigger and the same cause, and it has a patch.

**Analysis**

When `media.getusermedia.microphone.prefer_voice_stream_with_processing.enabled` is `false`, the `AudioCallbackDriver` constructor in [GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#489) does not use the `VOICE` input preference. But `MediaTrackGraphImpl::AudioInputDevicePreference()` in [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#4287) still requests a `Voice` input for any track with input processing, such as echo cancellation. `MediaTrackGraphImpl::CheckDriver()` sees the mismatch and replaces the driver on each graph iteration. The patch in bug 2057748 makes the graph read the same pref. Bug 2057748 also sets `media.getusermedia.audio.processing.platform.enabled` to `false`, but the cause does not depend on that pref.

The profile agrees. While the microphone is open, the `GraphRunner` thread logs "Switching to new driver" 249 times in about 2.6 seconds. In the parent process, each new duplex stream creates a CoreAudio aggregate device and destroys it soon after. cubeb and CoreAudio report no error. Each new driver runs on its fallback `SystemClockDriver` first, and the next switch comes before the audio callback takes over. Thus the playback output stays silent until the microphone closes.
title: With media.getusermedia.microphone.prefer_voice_stream_with_processing.enabled set to false, turn mic input breaks audio output

Thank you for the Edge test and the phone test.

**Analysis**

Edge on this laptop fails in the same way, also with its "Hardware Media Key Handling" flag disabled (comment 8). With the flag disabled, the failure came after about 15 songs. So the failure does not need the Windows media controls (SMTC). The Firefox level bar in the Volume Mixer moves (comment 5). The profile in comment 3 shows audible sound data with no underruns. So the sound reaches the Windows mixer, and the silence starts after that point.

The profile analysis in comments 4 and 6 shows two "paused" and "playing" updates at each change of video. These updates come from the page. Firefox sends the `paused` state of the video element to SMTC ([MediaStatusManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/mediacontrol/MediaStatusManager.cpp#312), [WindowsSMTCProvider.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/widget/windows/WindowsSMTCProvider.cpp#182)). When `media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled` is `false`, Firefox does not register with SMTC ([MediaControlKeyManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/d9bd6be9a67efb1c2667ef91a89856f35eb7cf5e/dom/media/mediacontrol/MediaControlKeyManager.cpp#71)). The SMTC updates probably make the failure occur sooner. The Edge test shows that the failure also occurs without them.

The speaker works with a phone, and the previous laptop did not have this problem (comment 7). The about:support text shows Windows build 26300, which is a Windows Insider preview build. The probable cause is in the Windows Bluetooth audio path on this laptop, for example the Bluetooth driver or this Windows build. Firefox has no defect here, so we close this bug. It stays linked to bug 2011679, which tracks Bluetooth audio and video problems.

**Suggestions**

These steps are outside Firefox:

1. Update the Bluetooth driver from the support site of the laptop vendor.
2. Report the problem to Microsoft in the Feedback Hub app.
3. As a workaround, keep `media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled` set to `false`.

Caution: with this workaround, the play and pause buttons on the headset and the speaker do not work in Firefox.

If a driver update fixes other apps but Firefox still fails, please add a comment to this bug.

Thanks for the profile.

**Analysis**

The profile in comment 9 is from Firefox 159 on twitch.tv, with H.264 video. Each time Firefox starts a hardware H.264 decoder, the RDD process crashes about 0.5 seconds later. The media log then shows `NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_REMOTE_CRASHED_RDD_OR_GPU_ERR` and "Video remote decoder crashed, disable HW acceleration". Firefox then uses a software decoder, so the hardware decoder stays idle. The profile shows five such crashes, one after each quality change of the stream.

The bundled ffvpx has no H.264 decoder. So the FFmpeg of the Flatpak runtime (libavcodec 61, FFmpeg 7.x) does the Vulkan decode. Firefox 159 does not check the version of a system libavcodec before it uses direct export. Bug 2056593 had the same setup: Flatpak, FFmpeg 7.1.3, an AMD GPU and direct export, with a segfault in `libvulkan_radeon.so`. On an AMD GPU, a system FFmpeg older than 63.20.101 does not use direct export. Firefox then uses the copy path, which works for this setup (comment 0). This fix is in Firefox 161, and it is not in Firefox 159. GPUs of other vendors with an old system FFmpeg have no such check yet.

This bug stays under the Vulkan video decoding meta bug 2053144 and the Linux playback meta bug 1766429. It also still waits for the Flatpak runtime version that Tymur asked for in comment 6.

comment:
Thanks for the profile and about:support.

**Analysis**

The profile shows a race between two audio sinks in the media code. With these autoplay prefs, the first `play()` fails. After the click, the page sets `currentTime = 0`, calls `play()`, and sets `currentTime = 0` again within 7 ms.

A seek that completes during playback starts an async init of a new `AudioSink`, see [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#516). The sink creator in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3542-3549) moves `mAudibleListener` to each new sink when it creates the sink. In the profile, the listener moves to the second sink at 6.612s.

Then the first init finishes and its sink plays. The check in [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#576-582) does not see that a newer `Start` superseded this init. The `mAsyncDispatchSeq` check in [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#531-535) runs only before the init starts. The wrapper then shuts down the second sink as "unneeded".

At 6.785s the first sink logs "Notifying that audio is now audible". Nothing listens to that sink, so the element does not become audible and the tab shows no icon. [AudioSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSink.cpp#497-508) sends the event only on a change, so the event does not come again.

This explains each observation. The 15s buttons mute and unmute, and the unmute creates one new sink with the listener. A long pause probably makes the decoder dormant, and the resume then creates one new sink. A wait between the steps removes the overlap of the two seeks. The audio output is correct; only the audible state is wrong.

The probable cause is bug 2050845, which landed on 2026-07-03 for Firefox 154. It added the async init for a seek resume. Before it, a seek resume created the sink at once. No bisection confirms this, and the regression status is not known yet. The current tree has the same code.

**Fix direction**

- Connect the audible event to the sink that starts, not to the sink that the creator makes. When the listener moves, send the current audible state again.

Thanks to everyone for the `powercfg -requests` results. The SYSTEM line and the EXECUTION line come from two different parts of Firefox.

**Analysis**

The SYSTEM line "The audio stream is already in use" probably comes from a silent `AudioContext`. A page can create an `AudioContext` and not suspend or close it. Then Firefox keeps an audio output stream open, also when the page outputs only silence. [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#391) keeps the audio device driver while any Web Audio track exists. Each realtime destination node adds an audio output ([AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#490)). The stream stays open until the page suspends or closes the context, or until the tab closes.

This cause agrees with these facts on this bug:

- The stream starts after an Outlook notification sound (comment 25).
- The stream stops when that tab closes (comment 29).
- The problem stops with `dom.webaudio.enabled` set to `false` (comment 31).

Bug 2002450 tracks the fix. It removes the destination output when the node has no active input for some time. Bug 2057010 shows the same symptom with Soundcloud on Windows 11. This bug also blocks bug 2023379, the meta bug for media sleep problems.

The EXECUTION line "non-display request" is the `audio-playing` wake lock ([nsAppShell.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/widget/windows/nsAppShell.cpp#81)). The code does not explain why this lock stays when no sound plays. A Web Audio page holds it only while its output is audible ([AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/b42441b06bc2b98160f12ee2dff262dd55583a9f/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#841)). A paused media element releases it after 10 seconds.

Thus a source that Firefox measures as audible probably holds the lock. Examples are a page with very quiet audio, or an extension page with no tab icon. Comments 30 and 40 say that the problem continued after the tab closed or unloaded. Another page, window or extension can explain this, but nothing confirms it yet.

comment:
Thanks for the detailed data. The attached `dumpsys media.aaudio` output agrees with the AAudio code in the current tree.

**Analysis**

The Web Audio graph asks for a latency below `POWERSAVE_LATENCY_FRAMES_THRESHOLD` (4000 frames), so cubeb opens the output stream in `AAUDIO_PERFORMANCE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY` ([cubeb_aaudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a82bcf39e8d23e7b06e021044db52f74210862ce/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_aaudio.cpp#1434)). In that mode, cubeb sets the output buffer to 3 bursts when the burst is smaller than 128 frames ([cubeb_aaudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a82bcf39e8d23e7b06e021044db52f74210862ce/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_aaudio.cpp#1476-1480)). With a burst of 96 frames, the buffer is 288 frames, or 6 ms. This is the "Avail 288" in the attached dump.

The buffer size does not depend on the requested latency. cubeb also does not read the XRun count and does not make the buffer larger after XRuns. The probable reason for the XRuns is that 6 ms is too short for each callback, which goes through AudioIPC. No log or profile proves this yet.

Firefox ignores `latencyHint`: `AudioContextOptions` declares only `sampleRate` ([AudioContext.webidl](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a82bcf39e8d23e7b06e021044db52f74210862ce/dom/webidl/AudioContext.webidl#12)). This explains why the burst and the buffer stay the same for every hint. Bug 2020377 covers the `latencyHint` implementation. The `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` route plays through the same graph stream, so it crackles too.

The plain `<audio src>` control asks for about 100 ms ([AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a82bcf39e8d23e7b06e021044db52f74210862ce/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#338)). That is above the threshold, so the stream gets the power saving mode and the AudioFlinger deep buffer mixer. This explains why the control is clean.

The probable cause is the libcubeb update of bug 2026000, which landed on 2026-03-25 for Firefox 151. It added the fixed 3 burst sizing in the output setup of `cubeb_aaudio.cpp`. Before it, the buffer also grew with the requested latency, and the Android graph asked for at least 1024 frames (bug 1930825). This comes from code reading only, so a regression range can confirm it.

Fix direction: in upstream libcubeb first, then vendored, make the low latency output buffer depend on the requested latency again. Another option is to add one burst to the buffer after new XRuns. Implementing `latencyHint` (bug 2020377) can also let `'playback'` open a power saving stream. This bug already blocks the crackling meta bug 1951155.

Matthew, could you please look at the output buffer sizing of the AAudio backend for this bug?

**Next steps**

@vincent.kerdraon, could you please record a capture while the single `sine` page crackles? It shows how Firefox 158.0.2 opens the stream and where the callback is late.

comment:
The Treeherder data points to bug 1981478 as the probable regressor of the spread to all Android emulator media jobs, not bug 2083318.

**Analysis**

Opt and non-isolated jobs fail only while bug 1981478 is in the tree. Bug 1981478 makes the MediaCodec NDK decoding path the default on Nightly, through `media.android-media-codec.enabled` in [StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#13213). Sheriffs backed it out several times. These windows matter:

- Oct 21, 18:56 to 23:51: opt failures on push 3d065f26e67c, which is inside this window.
- Oct 22 to Oct 26 morning, not in the tree: no opt failures, only 2 failures on debug isolated jobs.
- Oct 26, 12:12 to 23:40: opt failures from 15:24 to 19:37.
- Oct 27, 13:07, relanded: opt failures from 17:44 on, now about 20 jobs per day.

Bug 2083318 stayed in the tree from Oct 21 on, also during the gap of Oct 22 to Oct 26. So it does not explain the gap. Its change touches only the display list code in layout/painting. `nsDisplayVideo` keeps no image container and no video frame as a member ([nsVideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/layout/generic/nsVideoFrame.cpp#584)).

All failures from Oct 13 to Oct 21 are on debug `geckoview-mochitest-media-isolated` jobs. That variant forces the same NDK path with prefs ([variants.yml](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/taskcluster/test_configs/variants.yml#200-229)). So the stall is a problem of the NDK path, and bug 1981478 spread it to all variants. The trigger inside the NDK path is not known yet.

The symptom fits a remote video decoder creation that never finishes. For H.264 and AV1, the decoder stays "uninitialized" with no decoder and a pending promise. `RemoteVideoDecoderParent::RecvConstruct` in [RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/ipc/RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp#180) waits on several asynchronous steps with no timeout. If one step never answers, the content process waits until the browser restarts. This mechanism is probable: no log shows which step stops.

This bug now blocks bug 1980764, the meta bug for the Android MediaCodec NDK implementation.

**Next steps**

Andrew, could you please look at this NDK decoder stall? A failing retrigger with `MOZ_LOG=RemoteDecode:5,PlatformDecoderModule:5,MediaFormatReader:5,FFmpegVideo:5` and its logcat can show which step of the decoder creation stops. If the timeline above is correct, the Regressed by field can change from bug 2083318 to bug 1981478.

Thanks, PA, for the profile and the about:support text (comments 45 and 46).

**Analysis**

The profile shows one source for the open audio stream. A background tab, very probably the pinned x.com tab, runs an `AudioContext` with a started `OscillatorNode`. The Web Audio graph of that tab ran on the audio device driver for about 5.5 hours. It holds the only WASAPI output stream of Firefox. No other tab shows audio activity, and no media element plays. about:support shows no media prefs that are not at their default.

This agrees with the cause in comment 44. While the context runs, [AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#490) keeps an audio output, and [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#391) keeps the audio device driver. Nothing in this path checks whether the output is silent.

A started oscillator stays active until the page calls `stop()` ([AudioNodeTrack.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webaudio/AudioNodeTrack.cpp#522)). It also stays active behind a gain of 0. Thus a test for "no active input", as bug 2002450 describes, probably does not release this stream. A test for silent output over some seconds can release it.

Bug 1735412 reports the same open stream after `OscillatorNode.start()`. Bug 2002453 tracks the change to the system clock driver in the graph.

The profile does not show which source holds the EXECUTION lock. The verbose `MediaTrackGraph` log filled the profile buffer, so only the last 7 minutes of 11 hours remain. No `WinWakeLock` or `AudioChannel` line survived. A Web Audio page holds the `audio-playing` lock while its output measures above -72 dBFS ([AudibilityMonitor.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/AudibilityMonitor.h#20)). The lock stays also in a background tab. So a very quiet oscillator in the x.com tab can probably hold the lock, but no log confirms it yet.

Karl, could you please look at the profile in comment 46? It shows a started `OscillatorNode` that keeps the output stream open for hours, which the plan of bug 2002450 may not cover.

**Next steps**

PA, could you please do this test the next time the computer does not sleep?

2. Right-click the x.com tab and click "Mute Tab".
