comment:
Thanks for the bisection, the per-build log and the profile. They answer both requests of comment 3.

**Analysis**

The mozregression range in comment 5 is one push: changeset 974d05baa690, the libcubeb update of bug 2026000 (Firefox 151). This confirms the regressor in the Regressed by field. The update changes three output settings in `aaudio_stream_init_impl` ([cubeb_aaudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_aaudio.cpp#1471-1488)). It removes the capacity request of two times the requested latency, and the `setFramesPerDataCallback` call. It also replaces `max(3 bursts, latency_frames / 2)` with a fixed 3 bursts when the burst is below 128 frames. The bisection does not show which of the three changes matters most.

All 19 runs in attachment 9678174 agree with this. Firefox 151 to 159 ask for 1024 frames on Android. With that request, the old code gave a capacity of 2112 frames and a buffer of at least 576 frames. The new code keeps the AAudio default capacity of 1536 frames. It cuts the AAudio default buffer of 768 frames to 288 frames, or 6 ms.

The `about:logging` profile in comment 5 has the AudioIPC callback threads and the `GraphRunner` thread. The graph work is small: `MTG::Process` takes 55 µs on average, against a burst of 2 ms. The time between two callbacks reaches 9.2 ms, and 124 gaps are longer than 4 ms. This is close to the reported XRun rate. Most of the delay is the wait for `GraphRunner` to wake up, and the return to the callback thread.

11 of the 12 gaps over 6 ms come within 80 ms of the paint that the page does once per second. Thus the cause is the thread scheduling delay against a 6 ms buffer, not heavy audio work. The profile has no XRun markers, and its libxul stacks have no symbols.

**Fix direction**

Bug 2009308 (Firefox 160) changes the fix on trunk, because it removed the Android minimum of 1024 frames. Now `GetCubebMTGLatencyInFrames` returns the cubeb minimum latency ([CubebUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/CubebUtils.cpp#766-791)). The graph then clamps it to 128 frames ([GraphDriver.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/GraphDriver.cpp#600-604)). With 128 frames, `latency_frames / 2` is 64 frames, so the old floor alone gives 288 frames again. The bad build of 2026-11-05 in attachment 9678174 (157 XRuns in 60 s) agrees with this.

The fix belongs in upstream libcubeb first, then in the vendored copy. Options are a floor tied to the request together with an Android minimum request in `GetCubebMTGLatencyInFrames`. Another option is a floor at the AAudio default buffer size. A third option is one more burst after each new XRun from `AAudioStream_getXRunCount`. The new sizing in bug 2026000 looks intentional, so the choice needs the cubeb owner. Matthew already has the needinfo from comment 3 for this.

No test in the tree can show the XRuns, because they depend on real device scheduling. The dumpsys XRun method of comment 5 on a patched build can confirm a fix. This bug still blocks the crackling meta bug 1951155.

comment:
Thanks for the sample and for the new measurements in comments 3 and 4.

**Analysis**

The attached plain.mp4 has H.264 video and AAC audio. The movie timescale (`mvhd`) is 1000, and the video timescale (`mdhd`) is 15360. The video edit list has an empty edit of 3000 movie ticks (3.0 s), then 5000 ticks of media.

Progressive playback has two problems. Both are in the vendored mp4parse code, which parses non-fragmented MP4.

1. The empty edit has the wrong scale. This is bug 2082877. `get_indice_table` uses the empty edit duration in movie ticks as if it were in track ticks ([lib.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/third_party/rust/mp4parse_capi/src/lib.rs#1579)). So the video moves by 3000/15360 = 0.195 s, not by 3.0 s. The same error explains comment 2: Firefox applies 1327/15360 = 0.086 s in place of 1.327 s, so the video plays 1.24 s early. mp4parse-rust PR 459 fixes this function. It merged on 27 October, but the tree does not have it yet.
2. The duration does not include the empty edit. `mp4parse_get_track_info` reports the track duration as the edited duration only ([lib.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/third_party/rust/mp4parse_capi/src/lib.rs#752)). For this file that value is 5.0 s, so Firefox reports 5.0 s at load ([DecoderData.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mp4/DecoderData.cpp#337)). At the end of playback, the duration increases to the end position, 5.195 s (comment 4). PR 459 does not change `mp4parse_get_track_info`, so this problem stays after the vendor update.

The MSE path uses a different parser. `Moof::ParseTrun` converts the empty edit with the movie timescale ([MoofParser.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mp4/MoofParser.cpp#1010)). `SourceBuffer` then increases the duration to the end of the appended media, 8.0 s ([SourceBuffer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mediasource/SourceBuffer.cpp#565)). This is why the MSE page shows the 3.0 s offset and the 8.0 s duration.

This is not a regression. The offset code is from the 2017 vendor update in bug 1343793.

**Fix direction**

The A/V offset needs the vendor update of PR 459, which bug 2082877 tracks. After that update, progressive playback can still report 5.0 s at load and 8.0 s only at the end, while MSE reports 8.0 s. The duration needs a separate change in mp4parse-rust upstream, then a vendor update. One direction is to add the rescaled empty edit to the track duration in `mp4parse_get_track_info`. Another direction is to use the `tkhd` duration, which is 8000 movie ticks (8.0 s) for this file.

Caution: the audio duration also goes into the AAC trim calculation in [MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#543). A change that adds only the empty edit keeps the audio duration of this file the same, because its audio edit has no empty part. With both changes, plain.mp4 should show the flash at 4.0 s and report a duration of 8.0 s at load. plain.mp4 is small and can be the regression test file. Bart plans to test the progressive page again after the vendor update (comment 3).
title: Firefox applies a leading empty-edit (elst media_time=-1) presentation offset via MSE but not via progressive <video src> (internally inconsistent)

comment:
This is the file playback side of bug 2065822, which covers the MSE path on macOS. The cause is in the current tree. The attached samples match the report: HEVC with a CRA_NUT at each sync sample, and no IDR, RASL or RADL picture.

**Analysis**

On macOS, both demuxers mark an HEVC sample as a keyframe only when it has an IDR picture. `H265::IsKeyFrame()` uses `H265NALU::IsIframe()`, which accepts only `IDR_W_RADL` and `IDR_N_LP` ([H265.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/platforms/agnostic/bytestreams/H265.h#113)). Thus a CRA picture is never a keyframe on macOS.

- Matroska: `MatroskaDemuxer::CheckKeyFrameByExamineByteStream()` uses `H265::IsKeyFrame()` under `MOZ_APPLEMEDIA`, and `H265::IsRandomAccessPoint()` on other platforms ([MatroskaDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webm/MatroskaDemuxer.cpp#254-260)). The Matroska keyframe flags on the CRAs are not used.
- MP4: `MP4TrackDemuxer::GetNextSample()` replaces the stss sync flag with the result of `H265::IsKeyFrame()` ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#479-494)).

After a seek, `WebMTrackDemuxer::GetSamples()` skips every sample until it finds a keyframe ([WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#1432-1434)). With no IDR after the seek point, it reads to the end of the file, and the video track ends. This explains the `cra.mkv` seek: no video, audio continues, no `MediaError`, and `totalVideoFrames` stops. It probably also explains the `buffered` range that jumps to the end of the file. `cra-start.mkv` has no IDR, so no video plays at start or after a seek.

`MP4TrackDemuxer::Seek()` tries again from the first stss sync sample when it finds no keyframe ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#395-407)). In `cra.mp4`, that sample is the IDR at 0, so the seek works but decodes from the start. `cra-start.mp4` has no IDR. At start, `MediaChangeMonitor` drops every sample that is not a keyframe, with no error. The seek fails with end of stream, so the audio seek does not start and playback goes to the end.

**Regression status**

The MP4 part probably comes from bug 2049615 (Firefox 154), which is the regressor of bug 2065822. The Matroska part is not a recent regression. Bug 2065822 comment 9 reports the same MKV failure in Firefox 158 and in a Nightly from May.

**Fix direction**

The patch D338450 on bug 2065822 (comment 7, by Marcus) keeps the container keyframe flag in `MP4Demuxer`. It also skips the RASL pictures that VideoToolbox cannot decode, in `AppleVTDecoder`. It does not change `MatroskaDemuxer`. Bug 2065822 comment 9 reports that `H265::IsRandomAccessPoint()` in `MatroskaDemuxer` on macOS too makes MKV seeks work (0/10 to 10/10). This bug keeps the Matroska part open, and it blocks bug 1422891 (Matroska support).
title: HEVC playback can’t start decoding at a CRA keyframe: no video for streams that start on a CRA, and every seek fails in Matroska

comment:
Thanks for the clear regression range: Firefox 156 works and Firefox 157 fails.

**Analysis**

This is a regression between Firefox 156 and Firefox 157. The decoder is the same inline and in fullscreen, so the difference is in the compositor. In fullscreen, WebRender can show the video as a DirectComposition overlay. When hardware acceleration is off, Firefox does not use this overlay. The about:support shows one SDR display, the video overlay available, and `HwOverlayHDR=Not Supported`.

The probable cause is bug 2008887, which landed on 2026-09-02 in the Firefox 157 Nightly cycle. That change is in `DCSurfaceVideo::AttachExternalImage` in [DCLayerTree.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/gfx/webrender_bindings/DCLayerTree.cpp#2295). Now the transfer function alone sets `mContentIsHDR`, so an 8-bit NV12 video tagged PQ or HLG also counts as HDR content. Then `useHDR` in [DCLayerTree.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/gfx/webrender_bindings/DCLayerTree.cpp#2382) depends on `gfx.webrender.overlay-hdr` and the content, but not on the monitor. The overlay can then get an RGB10A2 swap chain with PQ output on an SDR monitor, with no tone mapping. This can give the washed-out fullscreen colors.

This cause holds only if the video is 8-bit and tagged PQ or HLG. The codec and the color tags of the sample are not known. No bisection confirms the cause.

The code at fault is in Core :: Graphics: WebRender, so this bug moves to that component. Ashley, could you please look at this bug? The change in bug 2008887 is the probable cause.

**Next steps**

Brian, could you please do this test and add the result to this bug?

1. Open `about:config`.
2. Set `gfx.webrender.overlay-hdr` to `false`.
3. Close all Firefox windows, then start Firefox again.
4. Play the video in fullscreen and look at the colors.
5. Reset `gfx.webrender.overlay-hdr` to its default value after the test.
title: Firefox 157 regression: Fullscreen video severely washed out with hardware acceleration on Windows 11

comment:
Thanks for the macOS audio log and the about:support data.

**Analysis**

The macOS log shows that the voice-processing unit runs in bypass mode in each microphone session. With bypass on, Apple's echo cancellation and noise suppression do not run. The built-in microphone then gives a very quiet signal, about -60 dBFS in this log. Firefox then applies its own processing in software. Its automatic gain control starts at 15 dB of gain and adds at most 6 dB each second during speech ([audio_processing.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/third_party/libwebrtc/api/audio/audio_processing.h#358-361)). This slow gain increase is the probable cause of the silent first seconds.

Chrome does not use the macOS voice processing (bug 1896938 comment 66), so this agrees with the difference between the two browsers. Bug 1896938 comment 58 reports the same slow start on Google Meet with other MacBooks.

Why Firefox requests the bypass is not known yet. [DeviceInputTrack.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/DeviceInputTrack.cpp#320-328) combines the requests of all microphone tracks on the device. So one track with no processing turns off echo cancellation for all tracks. Also, cubeb refuses echo cancellation without noise suppression ([mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#5392-5400)). After such an error, Firefox requests no platform processing ([MediaEngineWebRTCAudio.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webrtc/MediaEngineWebRTCAudio.cpp#1145-1150)).

The restart loop with voice processing turned off matches bug 2057748. With `media.getusermedia.microphone.prefer_voice_stream_with_processing.enabled` set to `false`, the driver opens a normal input, but the graph still requests a voice input. So `CheckDriver` in [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#474-481) replaces the AudioCallbackDriver again and again. Each new driver creates one `CubebAggregateDevice`. This agrees with the 262 aggregate devices in the log, about one each 0.25 s.

**Next steps**

Viacheslav, could you please record a capture while you join a Google Meet instant meeting and speak from the start? Keep `media.getusermedia.microphone.prefer_voice_stream_with_processing.enabled` at its default value, `true`. In step 2, choose the **WebRTC** preset in place of **Media playback**.

Please capture a profile:

1. Open `about:logging`.
2. Under **Log module selection**, choose **"Media playback"** in the **Logging preset:** drop-down.
3. Under **Logging output**, select **"Logging to the Firefox Profiler"**.
4. Click **Start Logging**.
5. Reload the page. Then do the steps that show the problem.
6. Click **Stop Logging**. The profile opens in the Firefox Profiler.
7. Click **Upload Local Profile**. This is the share button.
8. Copy the share URL. Add it to this bug.

The [instruction video](https://www.loom.com/share/24ea3a8e3a054c478de94643a0ea8620?sid=87b0ffaa-c4ea-43ce-8107-639f24b747a8) shows these steps.

The capture shows the processing that each microphone track requests and any cubeb error. This tells which of the two paths above turns on the bypass.
title: macOS: microphone is silent for the first ~10 s of a WebRTC call (built-in mic, voice-processing input), and disabling voice processing causes a continuous aggregate-device restart loop with no audio at all

comment:
Karl leads the analysis of this bug. In comment 70, Karl names bug 2070740 as the cause of the recent failures. The facts below come from the current tree and the newest CI logs. None of them contradicts that claim.

**Confirmed facts**

- The failures continue after bug 2070817 landed on 2026-09-21. The two newest logs (2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06, macOS aarch64 debug) show the same error at line 98 of the test. The logs show no crash and no assertion:
  `TEST-UNEXPECTED-ERROR | /webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audioworklet-interface/audioworkletprocessor-unconnected-outputs.https.window.html | Unhandled rejection: Closed before resume completed`
- `AudioContext::Close()` rejects every promise in `mPendingResumePromises` with this message ([AudioContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webaudio/AudioContext.cpp#1248)). `Resume()` adds each promise to this list, also when the context is allowed to play ([AudioContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webaudio/AudioContext.cpp#1134)).
- Only `OnStateChanged()` with the Running state resolves these promises ([AudioContext.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/webaudio/AudioContext.cpp#877-882)).
- On the graph thread, `PendingResumeOperation::Apply()` unsuspends the tracks and then resolves the graph promise ([MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#4030-4039)). The landed change of bug 2070817 adds one more main thread dispatch before the main thread handles that result.
- The test does not wait for its `resume()` promise before the worklet message calls `close()` at line 98.
- The wpt metadata now lists ERROR as an expected status on every configuration ([audioworkletprocessor-unconnected-outputs.https.window.js.ini](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/testing/web-platform/meta/webaudio/the-audio-api/the-audioworklet-interface/audioworkletprocessor-unconnected-outputs.https.window.js.ini)). Bug 2079648 and bug 2089029 made this change. So new failures of this type are now hidden as expected results.
- The timeouts in comment 0 (2024) come before bug 2047321 and do not show this error. They are a different failure mode.

**Open points**

- No log shows directly that the worklet message runs before `OnStateChanged()` with the Running state. A failing run with `MOZ_LOG=MediaTrackGraph:4` can show the order.
- The cause of the older macOS timeouts is not known.

The needinfo to Alastor from comment 61, as the author of bug 2047321, stays open.

comment:
Treeherder shows four failures in the last week. All four are on the Android 14 x86_64 emulator, opt, in GeckoView mochitest-media. They have two different causes.

**Analysis: test timeout**

Task HxrWU7o5QMeSkV0mIjcHAA (mozilla-central, 2026-11-05) ran the test for 328 s and hit the 300 s limit in `test_live_mp3_duration`. The last check that passed is "Appended more audio without ending the response". The next step is `await progress` at [test_live_duration.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/test/test_live_duration.html#40-45). It is the only wait in the test with no time limit, so a missing `progress` event becomes a five-minute hang. The log has no media error and no crash.

The probable cause is a suspended download before the append request. The test sets `preload="auto"`. On a cellular link, `GetPreloadDefaultAuto()` in [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#3433-3443) reads `media.preload.auto.cellular`, and its default is "metadata". The test profile sets `media.preload.auto` and `media.preload.default.cellular`, but not `media.preload.auto.cellular` ([user.js](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/testing/profiles/unittest-required/user.js#138-140)).

With "metadata", the element suspends the download after the first frame. Then the appended audio does not arrive, and no `progress` event fires. This can explain why all four failures are on Android and why the failure is intermittent. No log proves it yet. A run with `MOZ_LOG=HTMLMediaElement:5,MediaCache:4` that shows a suspend before the append request can confirm it.

**Analysis: harness error**

Task TuKzKaDdSYySLz_DqpfWNg (comment 0) and task E1JP9QQUSS6MdB8RibwkMg, both on 2026-11-09, show "exception reading log: [Errno 2] No such file or directory". All 26 checks of the test passed in both runs. The error comes from `read_stdout()` in [remote_process_monitor.py](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/testing/mozbase/mozdevice/mozdevice/remote_process_monitor.py#119-134), when `get_file()` in [adb.py](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/47f2a88cbab9072c8f8f156494b92d6891e488fb/testing/mozbase/mozdevice/mozdevice/adb.py#3237-3265) loses its host temporary file. The harness then reports an ERROR for the test that runs at that time. Bug 2021271 tracks a similar error from the same log reader.

The `httpd.sys.mjs` `writeByteArray` errors in the logs also occur during other tests that pass. They do not come from the live stream of this test. The confirm task WjpU_tnGQEGQ9FJdiyz5Ag ran the test five times, and every run passed.

**Fix direction**

- Set `media.preload.auto.cellular` to 3 for this test with `SpecialPowers.pushPrefEnv`, or in user.js beside `media.preload.default.cellular`.
- Give the `progress` wait a time limit that fails with a message, so that a hang shows the step.
- A desktop run with `media.preload.auto` set to 2 probably takes the same suspend path, so it can show the hang and the fix.

This is not a regression of Firefox code. The test has had the unbounded wait since it landed with bug 2049797 on 2026-09-22. Matthew, could you please look at this test?
title: Intermittent dom/media/test/test_live_duration.html | single tracking bug

comment:
Thanks for the check in the volume mixer.

**Analysis**

The Windows volume mixer had a mute on the Firefox Nightly audio session, and an unmute restored the sound (comment 5). The parent process opens the audio streams of all tabs, so one session mute silences every tab. The attached log agrees: the WASAPI output stream renders full buffers with no error.

Firefox code does not mute its Windows audio session. [WinAudioSession.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/widget/windows/WinAudioSession.cpp) only sets the display name, the icon and the grouping of the session, and listens for session events. [cubeb_wasapi.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/media/libcubeb/src/cubeb_wasapi.cpp) only registers for session events. Windows keeps the mixer settings of each app between sessions, so a mute from an earlier session can stay. Thus the cause is outside Firefox.

The earlier report bug 2042323 has the same symptom. Nobody checked the volume mixer there, so a session mute is possible but not confirmed for that bug.

This bug closes as not a defect in Firefox. If the mute comes back with no user action, a new bug with the steps that come before the mute can help.
title: Regression: Total audio loss on media playback in Firefox Nightly 162 (162.0a1) on Windows 11 WASAPI

comment:
**Analysis**

All failures in the last two days are on `windows11-64-24h2-hw-ref-shippable` opt, in the `mochitest-media-mda-gpu` job. This job forces hardware video decoding. The failure repeats on the rerun in a fresh browser. The log shows no decoder error, no `NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_*` code and no assertion.

The clone shows a different frame of the new video, not a scaling or color difference. The new video is `pixel_aspect_ratio.mp4` (H.264). In the failing tasks, the clone frame is always 3 decoded frames after the frame of the original. The frame dumps are byte-identical across passes and machines, so the offset is deterministic.

The probable cause is that the two `VideoFrameContainer`s hold different images after `pause()`. With hardware decoding, the video queue target is `media.video-queue.hw-accel-size` (3) in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4712-4716). While it plays, `VideoSink` sends the whole queue to both containers. On pause, `VideoSink::SetPlaying` sends one frame at the clock time ([VideoSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/mediasink/VideoSink.cpp#205-215)). A clone that keeps the old frame list shows its last entry, which explains the fixed offset. This is not confirmed: the call that updates one container and not the other is not identified.

These calls are the candidates:

1. The reinstall of the clone container after the source change in [HTMLVideoElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLVideoElement.cpp#690-692).
2. The copy of the images when not playing in `VideoSink::SetSecondaryVideoContainer` ([VideoSink.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/mediasink/VideoSink.cpp#702-716)).
3. The decoder going dormant right after pause, because the test sets `media.dormant-on-pause-timeout-ms` to 0 in [cloneElementVisually_helpers.js](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/test/cloneElementVisually_helpers.js#17).

The test takes the `drawWindow` snapshots right after the `pause` event. Nothing makes sure that both containers show the paused frame first.

Regression status: not known yet. The test file has not changed since 2019. The first failure in this job is on 2026-11-03, and the rate rose on 2026-11-10. Bug 2078676 changed the frame that `SetPlaying` sends on pause, but it landed on 2026-10-06 with no failure until 2026-11-03.

**Next steps**

The fix direction is to make the clone container get the same image list as the original at pause, seek, dormant and reinstall. The test can also wait until both containers show the paused frame before the snapshots. A CI run of this job with `MOZ_LOG=VideoFrameContainer:5,MediaDecoder:4` can show which call splits the two containers.

Bug 1776945 is the earlier tracking bug for this test. Bug 2090005 is a failure of the same test on Android.

comment:
Thanks, nobeks and PA, for the profile in comment 48 and the test in comment 50.

**Analysis**

The test in comment 50 confirms the source of the SYSTEM line. The Realtek stream stays open after "Mute Tab" on the x.com tab. It stops when that tab closes. EXECUTION shows None in all three outputs, so the `audio-playing` wake lock does not block sleep in this case.

The profile in comment 48 shows the same tab with a different pattern. The background x.com tab runs about 47 `AudioContext` objects with only a destination node and no source node. These contexts output silence, but the graph keeps its WASAPI output stream open for the whole capture. A YouTube page also resumed two contexts with no source, and their stream stays open after the video pauses. The extra log modules of comment 44 logged nothing in this capture. The about:support file on dropmefiles.com.ua is not readable for triage.

The code shows why the stream stays open:

- Each realtime destination node adds its audio output when the context starts ([AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#490)). Nothing removes it while the context runs.
- `DestinationNodeEngine::IsActive()` always returns true ([AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#240-246)). Its code comment relies on `SetIsOnlyNodeForContext()`, but that function no longer exists.
- The graph keeps the audio device driver while a Web Audio track exists ([MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#391-405)). After bug 2083466, the check counts each output track that is not suspended. Neither check looks at silence or volume.
- "Mute Tab" only sets the output volume to 0 ([AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#713), [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp#2499)). The output stays, so the stream stays open.

The plan of bug 2002450 removes the destination output after a period with no active input. Nothing for it has landed yet. It covers the destination-only contexts of comment 48.

It probably does not cover the started `OscillatorNode` of comment 46 when the oscillator connects to the destination, also through a gain of 0. A started oscillator stays active until it ends ([OscillatorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/webaudio/OscillatorNode.cpp#342-345)). It also does not cover a muted tab with an active input. A test for silent output or zero volume over some seconds can cover all three cases.

Comments 30 and 40 say that the problem continued after the tab closed or unloaded. This path does not explain those reports.

**Next steps**

The needinfo to Karl from comment 47 is still open. His answer can show whether bug 2002450 also covers silent and muted outputs. The request of comment 44 for a capture with the `WinWakeLock` and `AudioChannel` modules is still open for the EXECUTION line.

comment:
Thanks for the Nightly profile and about:support.

**Analysis**

The [profile](https://share.firefox.dev/4j9OdOq) shows no underrun and no missed audio callback. One AudioSink and one cubeb stream play for the whole capture, with no seek. So the glitch comes from the switch between the two audio paths in `AudioStream`. At 1x, `GetUnprocessed()` copies the decoded audio directly. At other rates, `GetTimeStretched()` sends the audio through the SoundTouch time stretcher. A change between two rates other than 1x only calls `setTempo()`, so it is clean, as the report says.

**Return to 1x.** `UpdatePlaybackRateIfNeeded()` in [AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#748-751) calls `flush()` on the time stretcher. [SoundTouch.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/media/libsoundtouch/src/SoundTouch.cpp#318) pads the input with silence during the flush. In the profile, each return to 1x plays about 1200 to 1800 frames (25 to 37 ms) from the flushed stretcher. This tail ends in silence. Then `GetUnprocessed()` starts the direct audio at full level with no crossfade. Below 1x, the flush can also cut the waveform and drop a few ms of audio.

**Leave 1x, new in Nightly.** After the flushed audio plays, `GetUnprocessed()` now clears the stretcher and calls `PrimeTimeStretcher()` ([AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#651-656)). Bug 2075947 added this step. The [prime](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/eebfc2395a938361f2ecaf6107f3767c1df8d04e/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#239) feeds 1200 frames of silence. With the default prefs, the stretcher needs about 1488 input frames before it gives output, so these zeros stay in front of the real audio. Each move away from 1x then plays a hard cut, a short silence and a fade-in. In Firefox 159 the prime ran only once per stream, so this symptom was not there.

**Regression status.** This is a regression: the noise on leaving 1x is new in Nightly 162. The probable causes come from code reading and the profile, not from a bisection. Bug 1955841 (Firefox 157) added the flush on the return to 1x and the silence prime. Bug 2075947 (Firefox 161) added the prime after each return to 1x. Bug 1683437 reported a similar pop at rate changes in 2020.

**Fix direction.** Do not insert silence in the middle of the stream. On the return to 1x, keep the stretcher running at tempo 1.0 and crossfade into the direct path at the matching position. On leaving 1x, prime the stretcher with the last played audio, not zeros, and crossfade into the first stretched output. A gtest in `TestAudioStream.cpp` can show the gaps and the hard cuts. It can use MockCubeb output recording, a sine source, and switches such as 1x to 2x to 1x and 1x to 0.5x to 1x.

Paul, could you please look at how `AudioStream` changes between the stretched path and the direct path?

This bug blocks bug 1904915 (YouTube playback).
title: Brief stutter in audio when going returning to 1x playback speed on a Youtube video

comment:
Thank you for the report.

**Analysis**

The probable cause is bug 2080127. It landed on 2026-10-20 and first shipped in Firefox 160. Since that change, [WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#1133-1134) treats every `audio-playing` wake lock as a background lock. A background lock only asks the system to block suspend. It does not stop the screen lock or the screensaver.

Audio playback takes only the `audio-playing` wake lock, in `HTMLMediaElement::CreateAudioWakeLockIfNeeded` in [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp). The `video-playing` wake lock needs a video track, so an audio-only stream never takes it. Thus Firefox still tells KDE that audio plays, but it no longer asks KDE to keep the screen unlocked.

The change looks intentional. From Firefox 146 to 159, audio in the active tab also stopped the screensaver on Linux. Bug 1996504 caused that behavior, and bug 2080127 reverted it. Before Firefox 146, bug 1749187 already kept audio playback from stopping the screensaver.

On Windows, audio uses `PowerRequestExecutionRequired` and video uses `PowerRequestDisplayRequired`, in [nsAppShell.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/widget/windows/nsAppShell.cpp#75-84). On macOS, audio uses `kIOPMAssertionTypeNoIdleSleep`, in [nsAppShell.mm](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/widget/cocoa/nsAppShell.mm#82). A site that must keep the screen on can use the [Screen Wake Lock API](https://w3c.github.io/screen-wake-lock/). Firefox on Linux still honors the `screen` wake lock.

This bug blocks the wake lock meta bug 1665980.

**Next steps**

This is a regression in Firefox 160 for audio-only playback, from a deliberate change in the GTK wake lock code. The code is in `widget/gtk`, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk. Martin wrote the change in bug 2080127. Martin, could you please decide if audio-only playback on KDE must keep the screen unlocked?

comment:
Thanks for the testcase and the analysis. The code confirms the cause in comment 1.

**Analysis**

`DynamicsCompressorNodeEngine::ProcessBlock` replaces the `WebCore::DynamicsCompressor` each time the input channel count changes ([DynamicsCompressorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/DynamicsCompressorNode.cpp#81-86)). The new kernel starts with zeroed pre-delay buffers ([DynamicsCompressorKernel.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/blink/DynamicsCompressorKernel.cpp#84-107)). The default pre-delay is 0.006 s ([DynamicsCompressor.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/blink/DynamicsCompressor.cpp#91)), which is 288 frames at 48 kHz. The output is `delayBuffer[readIndex] * totalGain` ([DynamicsCompressorKernel.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/blink/DynamicsCompressorKernel.cpp#465-469)), so the first 288 frames after the change are exact zeros. The 289th zero in the testcase is a normal zero crossing of the sine at t = 1 s. The rebuild also resets the `ZeroPole` filter state, the gain envelope and the `reduction` value.

This explains each case in comment 0. The constructor creates a 2-channel compressor ([DynamicsCompressorNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/DynamicsCompressorNode.cpp#42)). With mono input, the engine rebuilds it once at t = 0 and never again. With `channelCountMode = 'explicit'` and `channelCount = 2`, the count always matches, so the engine never rebuilds it. The stereo to mono change goes through the same path and gives the same gap.

`DynamicsCompressor::setNumberOfChannels()` also creates new zeroed buffers, so it does not help. This behavior is old: the rebuild came with bug 867511 in 2013, so this is not a regression.

**Fix direction**

The node accepts only 1 or 2 channels ([DynamicsCompressorNode.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/DynamicsCompressorNode.h#57-72)). The engine can keep the one 2-channel compressor for its full life and remove the rebuild. For mono input, call `AllocateChannels(2)`, process, then `AllocateChannels(1)` ([AudioBlock.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/AudioBlock.cpp#139-151)). `process()` already copies mono input into both channels ([DynamicsCompressor.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/webaudio/blink/DynamicsCompressor.cpp#170-183)). The detector uses the maximum across channels and one gain for all channels, so mono output stays the same as today.

After this change, a stereo to mono change has no gap. For 6 ms, the output then holds the delayed left channel, not the (L+R)/2 down-mix. To make it exact, average the two channels' delay buffers and filter states at the change. Apply that only with `channelInterpretation = 'speakers'`. With `'discrete'`, the remix keeps the left channel and leaves a new right channel silent.

A WPT in `webaudio/the-audio-api/the-dynamicscompressornode-interface/` can show the fix. It can render the mono then stereo sine of the testcase and fail on a run of exact zeros longer than 1 ms. No current test covers a channel count change on this node.
title: DynamicsCompressorNode outputs ~6 ms of silence when its input channel count changes

comment:
Since 2026-11-11, this test fails often on the Android x86_64 emulators (debug, opt and ccov builds). Every failure is on the detector at 96000 Hz. The failing subtests are "suspending the input AudioContext" and "closing the input AudioContext". Bug 2091794 shows the same failure in the "disabling one MediaStream's tracks (shared)" subtest.

**Analysis**

The test can lose a detector message. In [mediastreamaudiosourcenode-from-context-with-different-rate.https.html](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/testing/web-platform/tests/webaudio/the-audio-api/the-mediastreamaudiosourcenode-interface/mediastreamaudiosourcenode-from-context-with-different-rate.https.html#21), `waitForMessage` sets `port.onmessage = null` after the first message. A message that arrives before the next wait starts is lost.

[silence-detector.js](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/testing/web-platform/tests/webaudio/the-audio-api/the-mediastreamaudiosourcenode-interface/silence-detector.js) posts a message only when its state changes. Thus a message with `isSilent: false` can only come after a silent state. `testSuspendingInputContextSilencesAll` asserts on the first message after the action. So the failure shows that the 96000 Hz detector went silent before the action, and the test lost that message. This also explains why the disable subtest fails the same way, although it suspends nothing.

The probable cause of the new failure rate is bug 2083466. It changed `MediaTrackGraphImpl::CheckDriver()` in [MediaTrackGraph.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/MediaTrackGraph.cpp), and it landed on mozilla-central on 2026-11-10. Now the output of a suspended or ended track does not keep the AudioCallbackDriver. Each subtest suspends or closes its contexts, so each graph switches to a SystemClockDriver and back. On a slow emulator, the driver start can starve the `CrossGraphReceiver` of the 96000 Hz graph, which then outputs silence. This link comes from code reading and push timing, not from a bisection or a log.

All failing pushes contain that change. The test file and its meta file did not change since May 2026. The meta file expects a pass on Android x86_64. Two Treeherder entries on this bug are not this test: job 606547578 has media mochitest timeouts, and job 606557394 has a jittest setup error. This triage did not read the full log of comment 0 because of a tool limit. The failure lines come from comment 0 and from Treeherder.

**Fix direction**

- In the test, keep one `port.onmessage` handler for each detector for its whole life, and record the latest state.
- After the action, wait until the state is silent or has no input. Do not assert on the first change.

These checks can confirm the cause:

1. Retrigger the android-em-14-x86_64 debug `geckoview-web-platform-tests-nofis` job on the push before 953c24d5abd1.
2. Retrigger the same job on the push with 953c24d5abd1, and compare the failure rates.
3. Run the test on try with `MOZ_LOG=MediaTrackGraph:4,DriftControllerGraphs:4` to see the driver switches and receiver underruns.

The regression status is not known yet: bug 2083466 is only the probable regressor. Bug 2085698 covers related cross-graph receiver dropouts after stalls.

Karl, could you please look at whether the driver switch on suspend and close from bug 2083466 is correct for graphs with cross-graph tracks?
title: Intermittent /webaudio/the-audio-api/the-mediastreamaudiosourcenode-interface/mediastreamaudiosourcenode-from-context-with-different-rate.https.html | single tracking bug

comment:
The data agrees with comment 1 by Thomas: the page can get `seeked` before the new frame is ready to draw. Two details differ from comment 1.

**Analysis**

The failures are on windows11-64-24h2-hw-ref-shippable opt, in mochitest-media-mda-gpu, at revision e98520026a95 (autoland and mozilla-central). The test came with bug 2080453. Caution: the triage tooling could not read the full CI log, so the log does not tell us the file or the seek phase yet.

The test waits only for `seeked`, then calls `drawImage` at once, with no `requestVideoFrameCallback` and no retry. The test checks each color channel with the same message. Thus the PASS after the FAIL is the green channel check, not a retry.

The seek to 8 expects yellow (255, 255, 0). Red got 0, and green and blue passed, so the drawn frame was green. This is probably the frame of the previous seek to 0.9. In the 7 second `stss-extra-entries` files, the frame at 0.9 is green, so a leftover frame gives this pixel in both phases. In the 4 second files, the frame at 0.9 is blue, and green fits only the playing phase. Thus the data does not show that only the paused phase fails.

The probable cause is the order in `SeekingState::SeekCompleted` in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3290). It resolves the seek promise first, and then the main thread queues `seeked`. Then the state machine thread calls `Redraw` ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/a9a644f66adb0cbb132f042bb7df24032f56346a/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#3315)), which puts the new frame into `VideoFrameContainer`. Nothing orders the two threads, and `drawImage` reads the image that the container holds at that time. This order is from 2016, so the new test shows an old race and no recent product change caused it.

**Fix direction**

The test can wait until the drawn frame shows the seek target before it checks the colors. One way is a poll on animation frames with a time limit. `requestVideoFrameCallback` is another option, because `Redraw` gives the frame a new id. Caution: a callback registered after `Redraw` already ran waits for a next frame, and a paused element does not present one. The lines "Running with file" and "Seek while playing" before each failure in the full log show the file and the phase.

Thomas, could you please look at these facts when you choose the change to the test?

comment:
Timothy Nikkel leads the analysis of this bug (comments 5 and 6). The bug waits for the answers from Chris to comment 6, which include about:support. Below are confirmed facts from the profile in comment 3 and from the code.

**Facts from the profile in comment 3**

- FFVPX decodes the VP9 video in software in the RDD process. The decoder log shows "YUV colorspace: BT709, color range: LIMITED".
- The profile has no Renderer, RenderBackend or Compositor thread from the GPU process. So the profile does not show if the video overlay was in use when the tint appeared.
- The profile shows an Intel Core i5-5300U CPU. It does not show the GPU, so the GPU is not known yet.
- The media log has no decode error that relates to the tint.

**Facts from the code**

- A software-decoded frame goes to the overlay only as an NV12 texture with limited range. [TextureHostWrapperD3D11.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/09b86521110cb23b77f5385a0e02aa4013a41f97/gfx/layers/d3d11/TextureHostWrapperD3D11.cpp#247-250) refuses other ranges.
- On the overlay path, [DCLayerTree.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/09b86521110cb23b77f5385a0e02aa4013a41f97/gfx/webrender_bindings/DCLayerTree.cpp#2703) maps this video to `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_YCBCR_STUDIO_G22_LEFT_P709`. The D3D11 video processor gets this limited-range tag through `VideoProcessorSetStreamColorSpace1`.
- On the path without an overlay, WebRender does the limited-range conversion in its own shader.
- For this texture, [TextureD3D11.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/09b86521110cb23b77f5385a0e02aa4013a41f97/gfx/layers/d3d11/TextureD3D11.cpp#1327-1336) allows the overlay when `gfx.webrender.dcomp-video-sw-overlay-win` is on. So test 1 in comment 6 separates the two paths.
- `SetVpSuperResolution` in [DCLayerTree.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/09b86521110cb23b77f5385a0e02aa4013a41f97/gfx/webrender_bindings/DCLayerTree.cpp#145-156) calls the driver only for NVIDIA (vendor 0x10DE). For other vendors, it returns `E_NOTIMPL`. If the GPU is Intel, test 2 in comment 6 cannot change the result.
- No code was found that explains why the tint starts a fraction of a second after playback starts.

**Open points for Timothy**

- Firefox tags the overlay input as studio range. If the tint goes away with test 1, where does the range get lost?
- A "Graphics" preset profile that keeps the GPU process threads can show if the overlay is in use when the tint appears.
- It is not known if a hardware-decoded H.264 video shows the same tint.

Bug 2091358 and bug 2023466 also show washed-out or grey video in the overlay area, with different triggers. The code above is in Core :: Graphics and Core :: Graphics: WebRender. This bug stays on the YouTube meta bug 1904915.
title: Grey tint over youtube videos
